 TALBOT COUNTY PUBLIC NOTICE INVITATION TO BIDDERS TITLE: EXTENSION OF SEWER FROM THE REGION II (ST. MICHAELS) WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT, TO THE MOUNT PLEASANT AREA, UNDER BROAD CREEK, AND TO THE VILLAGES OF BOZMAN AND NEAVITT, AS OUTLINED IN RESOLUTION NO. 250 BID NO.: 23-11 OPENING: TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 5, 2023@10:00 A.M. LOCAL TIME SEALED BIDS for this project shall be accepted by the Office of the Talbot County Manager, South Wing, Talbot County Courthouse, Suite #13, 11 North Washington Street, Easton, Maryland 21601 until 10:00 a.m. on Tuesday, September 5, 2023, at which time they will be opened and read aloud. Proposals must be hand-delivered or mailed to the Talbot County Courthouse, Suite #13, 11 North Washington Street, Easton, Maryland, 21601 before 10:00 a.m. on September 5, 2023, with the package or mailing label being addressed to "Bid 23-11, EXTENSION OF SEWER FROM THE REGION II (ST. MICHAELS) WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT, TO THE MOUNT PLEASANT AREA, UNDER BROAD CREEK, AND TO THE VILLAGES OF BOZMAN AND NEAVITT, AS OUTLINED IN RESOLUTION NO. 250, c/o the Talbot County Manager." THE SCOPE OF WORK FOR THIS PROJECT includes the installation of a 3-inch through 8-inch HDPE forcemain for a length of 18.8 miles from the Region II (St. Michaels) Wastewater Treatment Plant, to the Mount Pleasant area, under Broad Creek, and to the Villages of Bozman and Neavitt, as outlined in Resolution No. 250; and the installation of service stubs, whereby individual lot connections can be made at a later date as a part of Phase 2 of the Resolution 250 septic system elimination project. The project also includes the installation of lot valves, pressure sewer cleanout assemblies, air vacuum relief valves, sewer system testing, final seeding and stabilization for disturbed areas, final site cleanup, and other items as described in the construction drawings and specifications completed by Century Engineering, LLC, dated January 2023. title: PET OF THE WEEK
content:
PET OF THE WEEK

 August 8, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: A2 | Section: News 
 
 149
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Nellie is a 10-year-old female tortoiseshell Manx mix. She is quiet and independent.She likes to be in the same room as her people and get petted, but she is not a lap cat.She wants affection on her terms and space when she isn't in the mood - don't we all?.Because of her Manx genes, Nellie has a cute little stub tail, but unfortunately has Manx syndrome and does not always use the litter box. It isn't her fault though, she just can't always tell when she has to go potty.Nellie does fine with other cats, but we do not recommend a home with children since she isn't afraid to give someone a little smack if they don't respect her space. Can you give Queen Nellie the purrfect home? Fill out an adoption application on Chesapeake Cats and Dogs website, chesapeakecatsanddogs.org. Call 410-643-9955 for an appointment to meet this cat.

Let's find Jake his new home. Jake has been waiting since March. This adorable boy is a Jack Russell mix, about 30 pounds. Even though he is 9-years-old you would never know it. For further information please call the office at 410-943-3113.William J. Gullion, III Zoning Inspector3030477 SD/DS 8/11,8/18/2023PUBLIC AUCTION OF CONTENTS OF ABOX STORAGE UNIT OF JIM FREEMAN AUGUST 24, 2023 AT 12:00 P.M.ABOX LLC3063 BEVERLY LANE CAMBRIDGE, MARYLAND 21613 FOXWELLS AUCTION3029314 SD 8/4,8/11/2023PUBLIC NOTICE - STATE OF MARYLAND DRAFT 2022 Consolidated Plan Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) and Amendment to the Recovery Housing ProgramNotice is hereby given that the State of Maryland has opened a 30-day public comment period on the Draft 2020 Consolidated Plan Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER). In addition, notification is also given of an amendment to the Recovery Housing Program.The Consolidated Plan is a planning document required by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and is prepared by the Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It covers a five-year period and is designed to coordinate Federal, and to a lesser extent State, resources to provide decent housing, economic opportunities, and an acceptable living environment for Maryland's citizens. The Plan is updated every year during the five-year period through an Annual Action Plan and includes a series of one year goals toward meeting the overall five year goals of the Plan.Maryland's Consolidated Plan covers the State's non-entitlement jurisdictions. Entitlement jurisdictions - those that receive funding directly from HUD, including Anne Arundel, Baltimore, Harford, Howard, Montgomery and Prince George's Counties, and the Cities of Annapolis, Baltimore, Bowie, Cumberland, Frederick, Gaithersburg, Hagerstown, and Salisbury - prepare their own Consolidated Plans and are not covered by the State plan.As part of the Consolidated Planning process, the State submits a CAPER to HUD which describes the progress the State has made in carrying out the one-year goals contained in the five-year Plan.DHCD has completed the third year of the five-year Plan that ended June 30, 2023, and the draft CAPER details the progress DHCD made toward it housing and community development goals in the last year.DHCD is interested in public input and comment on the draft CAPER available on our website@https://dhcd.maryland.gov/Pages/ConsolidatedPlan.aspx. We will take written comments (via email) on the report through COB Monday, September 18, 2023. In addition, we will hold four in-person hearings at the locations listed below and one virtual hearing: First Hearing:Monday, August 14 · 11:30 am - 12:30 pmOwings - Calvert Library Fairview Branch8120 Southern Maryland BlvdOwings, MD 20736Second Hearing:Tuesday, August 15 · 11:00 am - 12:00 pmTowson - Baltimore County Public Library320 York RoadTowson, MD 21204Third Hearing: Friday, August 18 · 11:00 am - 12:00 pmCaroline - Caroline Public Library Federalsburg Location123 Morris AveFederalsburg, MD 21632Fourth Hearing: Monday, August 28 · 11:00 am - 12:00 pmCumberland - Allegany County Department of Economic and Community Development701 Kelly RoadCumberland, MD 21502Fifth Hearing: Wednesday, August 30th · 6:00 pm - 7:00 pmTime zone: America/New YorkVideo call link: https://meet.google.com/biq-jxor-ifeOr dial: (US) +1 575-518-3167 PIN: 151 751 081#2023 Action Plan Amendment - Recovery Housing ProgramThe State of Maryland has been awarded a fourth year of funding in the amount of $1,295,266 from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development for the Recovery Housing Program (RHP). A substantial amendment to the FY 2023 Annual Action Plan is necessary in order to receive the fourth round of RHP funds. For this grant, like the previous three awards, the State is proposing to use the funds through a competitive process to county governments who can apply for themselves or on behalf of eligible non-profit providers to provide recovery housing for women and children.The Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development hereby gives notice that the substantial amendment to the FY 2023 Action Plan, as well as revisions to the three previous RHP amendments, will be available for public review and comment from August 14 through September 12, 2023. Upon conclusion of the comment period on September 12th, any responses received will be considered and the plan will be finalized and submitted to HUD.There will be two public hearings during the comment period to discuss the proposed plan. title: Retreat House offers serenity, contemplation
content:
Retreat House offers serenity, contemplation

 August 11, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: A10 | Section: News 
 
 506
 Words 

 Read News Document

 GALENA - In October, the Retreat House is offering two weekend retreats at the Foehliage Retreat Center. The first fall weekend retreat entitled "'Neath the Oaks: The Spirituality of Plants," begins at 4 p.m. Friday, Oct. 13, and ends on Sunday, Oct. 15, at 11 a.m.The retreat will be guided by Francie Thayer and Heather Strang, spiritual companions on staff at the Retreat House. They will be joined by Rachel Field, an Episcopal priest focusing on environmental ministry, who will offer a selection of guided spiritual practices from her farm in Vermont via Zoom.There will be ample time for silence, and for walking and resting amid the community of trees above and along the Sassafras River at the Foehliage Retreat Center For retreat participants who wish to engage in spiritual practice during this quiet weekend, Field will delve into what Robin Wall-Kimmerer speaks to in her book Braiding Sweetgrass as her love song to the more-than-human world.Participants will spend time in quiet contemplation, conversation and encounter with trees that guide, nourish, support and build community. Practices will be rooted in an exploration through a Christian lens, and seekers or practitioners of other faiths are warmly welcome.Learn more about making a deposit and how to register at tinyurl.com/RHSpiritualityofplants.The second fall weekend retreat, "Blessing the Ordinary: A Women's Weekend" will be begin at 4 p.m. on Friday, Oct. 27, beginning and close on Sunday, Oct. 29, at 1 p.m. This retreat coincides with the season of fall, when the rhythm of life picks up pace with a new school year and plans for Thanksgiving, Advent, Christmas, and the dawn of a New Year.This retreat is an opportunity to remember that every day is holy and that, when we pay attention, we can be blessed by the ordinary of our relationships, environments, and work.Retreat activities will include group discussion, silent time for reflection and practicing the art form of blessings through poetry, writing, music and movement.Learn more about making a deposit and how to register at tinyurl.com/2023FallWeekend.For both retreats individual rooms at the Foehliage Retreat Center are available at $395; limited shared rooms are available at $345. Fees include lodging, meals and retreat materials.The mission of the Retreat House is to share God's abundant love in the world by holding a sacred, compassionate and inclusive space. Retreat House facilitators support all who come to journey with God.Begun in 2014 as a ministry of the Episcopal Diocese of Easton in the town of Hillsboro, the Retreat House is now based in Chestertown.The Retreat House offers spiritual direction, retreats and community circles in person at locations throughout Maryland's Eastern Shore and in the Annapolis area and through virtual online programs. For more information about the Retreat House, visit retreathousehillsboro.org or call 410-364-7069.Also follow the Retreat House on Facebook and Instagram.Learn more about the Foehliage Retreat Center at foehliageretreatcenter.org. 
 
 Caption: Set on the shores of the Sassafras River in Galena, the Foehliage Retreat Center will be the site of two weekend retreats hosted by the Retreat House in October.

 All kittens are cute and special, but little Ursula and siblings should be called "super special" as they are a litter of the most loving, trusting and relaxed kittens you'll meet. Ursula loves other kittens and people; she is playful and affectionate, always making eye contact with her foster parents and visitors in the hopes that she will be picked up to receive hugs and kisses. title: Community invited to 9/11 Day of Remembrance Ceremony
content:
Community invited to 9/11 Day of Remembrance Ceremony

 August 25, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: A5 | Section: News 
 
 510
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON - The Easton Economic Development Corporation along with community partners the Town of Easton, Talbot County Government, Talbot County Department of Emergency Services and the Talbot County Chamber of Commerce Young Professionals invite the public to a Day of Remembrance Ceremony on Sept. 11, 2023.Throughout the summer, volunteers have been working together to help strengthen relationships between members of the community by supporting projects that exemplified the theme, "We Are One: Community Supporting Community." The project is one of many across the country that will pay tribute to the individuals lost and injured on September 11, 2001, as well as honor the first responders and the many others who have risen to service in a crisis. The purpose of this awareness effort is to empower the general public to be caring, responsive community members should their fellow citizens need their support and to be mindful of the work of first responders in their community.The Day of Remembrance ceremony concludes the summer events."Easton is a resilient community, one that has supported its citizens through hundreds of years, through the good and the challenging times," said Easton Mayor Megan Cook. "I am proud of the summer-long project that helped our neighbors get to know each other and reinforce the idea that everyone will reach out and lend a hand across the city in times of need." Projects throughout the year included citizen responder trainings, a community mosaic project, community conversations and creation of downtown banners illustrating the theme."We are so grateful to be in such a supportive community.Teaching our community how to keep themselves and their neighbors safe is the first step in making our community resilient and able to endure whatever may come our way," said Geneva Schaffle, Talbot Emergency Management coordinator.This year's ceremony will incorporate volunteers from several local towns in the area, including the Easton Middle School Band and representatives from the Talbot County School system, local law enforcement officers and fire department volunteers, and members of local churches.Keynote speaker and Talbot County Council Vice President Pete Lesher will remark on the significance of the ceremony to the Easton community. Following the ceremony, the public is invited to a reception at the Talbot County Free Library, which will feature works of art created by program participants."We Are One: Caring for our Community" is funded through The Arc of The United States through a sub-grant from Ameri-Corps, a federal agency that engages millions of Americans in service and leads the nation's volunteer efforts for Patriot Day and the national 9-11 Day of Service and Remembrance Project.The ceremony will take place beginning at 8:30 a.m. at the Service Memorial on the corner of West and Dover streets in Easton. In the event of inclement weather, the ceremony will be moved to the Talbot County Free Library on Dover Street.More information about the event is available online at discovereaston.com/weareone.

title: County seeks comments on hazard mitigation
content:
County seeks comments on hazard mitigation

 August 30, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: B5 | Section: News 
 
 108
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON - The Caroline County Department of Emergency Services is asking the public to respond to an online survey regarding potential hazards and disasters.The Caroline County 2019 Hazard Mitigation Plan needs to be updated every five years, as required by the Federal Emergency Management Agency.Caroline County DES is the lead agency for updating the plan. The survey consists of 17 questions and will take an average of 8 minutes or fewer to complete.The purpose of the plan is to identify, plan and implement cost-effective hazard mitigation measures through a comprehensive approach known as hazard mitigation planning.To participate, please take the survey by logging onto www.surveymonkey.com/r/KB5QVX2.

title: Capital Region Honor Flight plans Oct. 3 trip
content:
Capital Region Honor Flight plans Oct. 3 trip

 September 1, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: A2 | Section: News 
 
 346
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Honor Flight Network is excited to introduce Capital Region Honor Flight as the most recent hub to join the nonprofit organization's extensive network. Capital Region Honor Flight will serve veterans residing in Maryland, Delaware and the broader Washington, D.C. metropolitan area.This expansion aims to fill the void left by the discontinuation of Honor Flight Maryland's operations in the region. As with all Honor Flight trips, the experience is entirely free of cost to honored veterans.Under the leadership of Jenny Brawley, Capital Region Honor Flight is poised to make a profound impact, enlisting the support of dedicated local volunteers including Mark Brickell and Candi Johnson, among others.Capital Region Honor Flight is set to embark on its inaugural Honor Flight journey on Oct. 3. The trip will commence with 23 esteemed senior war veterans departing from Huntingtown Volunteer Fire Department in a memorable event made possible through the generous sponsorship of Mission BBQ. This trip reflects the community's shared commitment to honoring those who have selflessly served our nation.Capital Region Honor Flight trips for 2024 are already in the planning stages.Meredith Rosenbeck, CEO of Honor Flight Network, noted the significance of this newly created hub."We are thrilled to be able to serve the greater D.C. area again, now through Capital Region Honor Flight," Rosenbeck said. "While some veterans in the region may have independently visited the memorials built to commemorate their service, participating in an Honor Flight trip with other veterans brings an entirely new element to that experience. The shared camaraderie among veterans on an Honor Flight trip - combined with the outpouring of gratitude from the community - truly takes this experience to the next level." For veterans residing in the area, Capital Region Honor Flight extends a heartfelt invitation to apply for one of these transformative trips. To gather more information about Capital Region Honor Flight, or to apply as a veteran or guardian for a Capital Region Honor Flight trip, please visit capitalregion.honorflight.org.The public is invited to give the veterans a warm welcome back for this inaugural Capital Region Honor Flight trip.

 The Star-Democrat in Easton, Maryland, is looking for a seasoned Managing Editor to supervise and coordinate the work of the newsroom. We are looking for someone to direct or participate in developing, writing and editing news stories.You'll assign work to reporters and help them develop their stories. You will be as much a coach and mentor as an editor.As a team member we want you to inspire and be inspired. You're passionate, creative and highly technical, driven to flourish in a competitive, fast-paced environment. You're fiercely accurate, with a desire to leverage your knowledge, skills and abilities to share news stories to viewers in our local communities.You're nimble, having the ability to pivot in an ever-changing workflow. You are a team player with a positive attitude and strong interpersonal skills. You have the ability to multitask, meet tight deadlines and remain calm under pressure.You will ensure stories are ready for immediate digital posting and you will be able to juggle the demands of digital and print journalism.The Star Democrat has a close-knit newsroom. The reporters and editors are supportive, and we want to see each other succeed. We work hard, but we are serious about maintaining a good balance between work and life.The newspaper is the flagship of the APG/Chesapeake group located in Easton, Maryland, on the beautiful Eastern Shore. Our circulation area includes Talbot County (37,600 population), Dorchester County (32,500 population) and Caroline County (33,400 population).Amenities include close proximity to Chesapeake Bay and all of its many water sports and activities. There is a vibrant arts and entertainment scene and hundreds of wonderful restaurants on the Eastern Shore.Talbot County is near Annapolis, Baltimore and Washington, D.C.This newspaper is part of APG - the Adams Publishing Group. title: Wreath laying at Oxford will honor Col. Tench Tilghman
content:
Wreath laying at Oxford will honor Col. Tench Tilghman

 September 15, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 3 | Section: News 
 
 292
 Words 

 Read News Document

 OXFORD - On Saturday, Sept. 16, the Col. Tench Tilghman Chapter of the Sons of the American Revolution (SAR) will perform a wreath-laying ceremony at Oxford Cemetery located off Oxford Cemetery Road just before entering the town of Oxford, Maryland, beginning at 1:30 p.m.The Colonel Tench Tilghman Chapter of the Sons of the American Revolution serves its members and the community in Talbot, Kent, Queen Anne's and Caroline counties.Members of the Col. Tench Tilghman Chapter of the SAR and descendants of the Tilghman family will be present at the wreath ceremony. The ceremony is open to members of the public who are interested in honoring the memory of Tilghman and learning about his contributions to the cause of freedom during the American Revolution.Tench Tilghman was born in Talbot County to James and Anna Tilghman on Christmas Day in 1744.He graduated from College of Philadelphia in 1761 and afterward went into a business with his uncle.Tilghman is best remembered for serving as an aide-de-camp for General George Washington during the war for independence and being selected by Washington to carry the official news of the British surrender at Yorktown, Virginia, to the Continental Congress in Philadelphia.The National Society of the Sons of the American Revolution, founded in 1889, is a non-profit and non-partisan organization dedicated to promoting patriotism, preserving American History, and promoting education to our future generations.To learn more about the Col.Tench Tilghman Chapter of the SAR, go to the Maryland Society of the Sons of the American Revolution website at mdssar.org or follow them on Facebook.

All persons desiring to become a candidate for the Town Council shall have resided in the Town at least one year prior to election, shall be a registered voter of the Town of Denton, shall be at least 25 years of age, and shall file in accordance with the Denton Charter, Article V, Section C5-8 which reads in part as follows: Candidates for election to the office of the Denton Town Council shall file with the Board of Supervisors of Elections a petition signed by at least twenty (20) registered voters of the Town of Denton. The candidate shall file the petition for an elective office not less than thirty (30) days, including Sundays and holidays, prior to the date of such election. Such petition shall state the name and address of the candidate, the fact that such person is eligible for election of the office of council, and that such person wishes his/her name placed on the ballot as candidate.Such petition shall be sworn to by the person filing same, both as to the fact of the candidate's eligibility and as to the genuineness of the signatures on such petition. title: CASA of Caroline goal: Raise $20,000 to celebrate 20 years
author: Contributed
content:
CASA of Caroline goal: Raise $20,000 to celebrate 20 years

 September 28, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 377
 Words 

 Read News Document

 For the past two decades, CASA of Caroline has established a legacy of caring for our community's most vulnerable children. The agency and its extraordinary volunteer advocates have been the voice for more than 100 children in the Caroline County foster care system due to abuse and/or neglect.CASA volunteers are unstoppable advocates for a child's best interest. They sustain this dedication despite the heartbreak and complexity of the cases and the diverse needs of children. Whatever each child's and youth's circumstances, CASA volunteers are frequently the only consistent adult in their lives and the ones who can make the difference between achieving permanency or lingering in the system, between succeeding in school or becoming involved with the juvenile justice system.Their tireless efforts make a huge difference in the life of a child, as kids with CASA volunteers spend less time in foster care, have greater access to more resources, do better in school, and are much better prepared for young adulthood and independent living.CASA volunteers are the heroes who "Change a Child's Story." In honor of this monumental achievement, CASA of Caroline will be holding a celebration dinner, A Legacy of Caring: Twenty for Twenty, at Caroline's Table in Denton on Thursday, Oct. 12 at 6 p.m.Caroline's Table will provide the setting for an elegant and intimate evening, complete with a four-course meal and wine pairings. The keynote speaker for this event is Lisa Spicknall, who will share her inspirational story about the power of advocacy. Spicknall is currently the executive director of Donate Life Maryland, has served as executive director of MADD, and has been a victim advocate since her life was forever changed on one tragic night in Talbot County in 1999.She has presented to numerous federal agencies, including the U.S. Department of Justice and the FBI and has been recognized for her work through awards including the Maryland Governor's Victim Assistance Award and People Magazine's Heroes Among Us Award.The goal for the celebration is to raise $20,000 in honor of 20 years of child advocacy in Caroline County. Tickets are $150 per person, and donations are welcome. If you are interested in attending the dinner or making a donation in honor of this milestone, please visit casaofcaroline.org or contact CASA of Caroline at info@casaofcaroline.org or call 410-479-8301.

PET OF THE WEEK

 October 3, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 108
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Caption: Coco first came to the Talbot Humane shelter as a tiny little puppy with her nine siblings. She went right into foster care and was adopted. The family had a change of life circumstance, and sadly Coco had to come back to the shelter. Coco is a young girl with tons of puppy energy. She loves to run and really enjoys playing with other dogs. Coco is working hard on her manners and learning how to walk on a leash. Coco also lived with children. She isn't doing well in the kennel, and we would love to find a foster home for her so she can get some of her stress out.

title: Mid-Shore Gives registration open until Oct. 31
content:
Mid-Shore Gives registration open until Oct. 31

 October 5, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 9 | Section: News 
 
 356
 Words 

 Read News Document

 On Tuesday, November 28th, Mid-Shore Community Foundation will host Mid-Shore Gives 2023, the 24-hour fundraising event to benefit local nonprofits."Mid-Shore Gives is a way for us to support our nonprofits, while engaging the community," said Buck Duncan, president of the Mid-Shore Community Foundation. "Last year's event was a success, with 443 donors and 70 participating organizations, the inaugural event raised $62,869 for local nonprofits.We hope to make an even greater impact this year." Nonprofit organizations, including those under fiscal sponsorship, serving Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's and Talbot Counties, are encouraged to take advantage of this opportunity. Participants will be provided with the tools and resources needed to have a successful charitable campaign, including best-in-class fundraising technology, and there is no cost to participate.Businesses are invited to join with the Mid-Shore Community Foundation in sponsoring this year's event.Thanks to generous sponsors, prize money and incentives will be awarded throughout the day. This year's sponsors include Easton Utilities, Mason Investment Advisory Services and Envision Wealth Planning.The giving begins on Tuesday, Nov. 28, at midnight Donations will be accepted online at midshoregives.org.Donors can use the shopping cart feature to select the nonprofits they want to support and how much they wish to donate to each, then check out with just one credit card transaction. 100% of all gifts will go to the designated nonprofits, less any credit card fees, unless the donor selects to cover the fees. The minimum donation is $10, and all donations are tax-deductible.This year, a feature has been added to allow both businesses and individuals to participate in fundraising.Businesses and individuals may host an event or create a fundraising profile to invite friends, family and colleagues to join them in giving back.This is a great opportunity for those looking to engage with the community, while putting your brand at the forefront of this local philanthropic event.Registration closes on Oct. 31. For additional information or to get involved, visit midshoregives.org or contact Heather Pickens at (410) 820-8175, Ext. 102 or hpickens@mscf.org. 
 
 Caption: SUBMITTED PHOTO
 
The Mid-Shore Community Foundation is located in the Bullitt House on Dover Street in Easton

title: PET OF THE WEEK
content:
PET OF THE WEEK

 October 10, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 206
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Meet Toffee Nut, a beautiful and vibrant spayed female bunny who is available for adoption. Toffee Nut was born in foster care and has spent her entire life being nurtured and cared for by loving foster parents. She has been raised around children and is great with them, making her an excellent addition to any family. Toffee Nut is an active and playful bunny who loves to run, jump and play in her enclosure. She is always up for a game with her toys, and her energy is contagious. You will be entertained for hours just watching her bounce around and explore her surroundings. Toffee Nut is a big fan of treats, and she enjoys her daily fruits and veggies. She is currently learning how to use a litterbox, and we have been making great progress with her.You can be confident in her ability to adapt to any new environment and routine you may have for her. If you are looking for a sweet, young, and energetic bunny who loves to play, Toffee Nut is the perfect match for you. She is ready to bring joy and excitement into your home and heart, so come meet her today. For more info, contact Talbot Humane, 410-822-0107 or email info@talbothumane.org.

The property is improved by a dwelling.The property, will be sold in an "as is" condition and subject to conditions, restrictions, easements, encumbrances and agreements of record affecting the subject property, if any, and with no warranty of any kind.Terms of Sale: A deposit in the form of cashier's or certified check, or in such other form as the Substitute Trustees may determine, at their sole discretion, for $6,000 at the time of sale. title: Easton Airport Day canceled
content:
Easton Airport Day canceled

 October 11, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 142
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON - Easton Airport Day, which was originally scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 14, has been canceled due to an unfavorable weekend weather forecast.The event will not be rescheduled this year. A date for 2024's event will be announced in the coming weeks, according to a news release from the airport."We understand your disappointment and share in it, but safety always comes first," said Micah Risher, the airport manager, in a statement. "The forecast is not favorable for a large portion of the eastern U.S. With pilots flying in from all over, we feel the decision to cancel now is the correct call." Risher encouraged members of the public to stay tuned on the airport's website and social media for more information on next year's Easton Airport Day.

Asher is a 2-year-old domestic short hair. She is a spayed female who arrived at the shelter on Sept. 22. title: Caroline County Commission to meet Nov. 7
content:
Caroline County Commission to meet Nov. 7

 October 18, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: A2 | Section: News 
 
 203
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON - The next Caroline County Commission meeting will be held 9 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 24, in Room 106, Caroline County Courthouse, 109 Market St., Denton.The commission will not meet Oct. 31.Meetings are held 9 a.m.Tuesdays except the fifth Tuesday of the month.Meetings are open to the public for attendance.Attendees will be security screened as they enter the courthouse.All Commission agendas with hyperlinks to documents can be found at www. carolinemd.org.The public can also attend meetings and work sessions remotely via ZOOM at https://zoom. us/j/300062187. The tollfree phone numbers to dial in are 888-475-4499 or 877-853-5257, and the meeting ID number is 300 062 187.Public comment will be held during the beginning and end of each meeting.You may submit written comments through the county's email system, website, and by USPS at 109 Market Street, Room 123, Denton, MD 21629.Written comments received prior to a meeting will be entered into the record and made available to the Commissioners prior to the meeting or hearing.All speakers, including the Commissioners must announce their name each time before they speak.Any document being voted on by the Commissioners will be linked on the agenda in advance when possible.

The purchaser shall be responsible for the payment of the ground rent escrow, if required. Condominium fees and/or homeowners association dues, if any, shall be assumed by the purchaser from the date of sale. Purchaser is responsible for obtaining physical possession of the property, and assumes risk of loss or damage to the property from the date of sale. The sale is subject to post-sale audit of the status of the loan with the loan servicer including, but not limited to, determination of whether the borrower entered into any repayment agreement, reinstated or paid off the loan prior to the sale. In any such event, this sale shall be null and void, and the Purchaser's sole remedy, in law or equity, shall be the return of the deposit without interest.If purchaser fails to settle within ten days of ratification, subject to order of court, purchaser agrees that property will be resold and entire deposit retained by Sub. Trustees as liquidated damages for all losses occasioned by the purchaser's default and purchaser shall have no further liability. The purchaser waives personal service of any papers filed in connection with its failure to settle within ten days of ratification and expressly agrees to accept service by first class mail at the address provided by the Purchaser as identified on the Memorandum of Sale. The defaulted purchaser shall not be entitled to any surplus proceeds resulting from said resale even if such surplus results from improvements to the property by said defaulted purchaser. Sub. Trustees will convey either marketable or insurable title. If they cannot deliver one or the other, or if ratification of the sale is denied by the Circuit Court for any reason, the Purchaser's sole remedy, at law or equity, is return of the deposit without interest. DAR to mark Col. Richardson's grave Nov. 5

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly; cconnolly@chespub.com | Page: 15 | Section: News

 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON - The General Perry Benson Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution will honor Colonel William Richardson by placing a bronze marker on his grave 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 5.The public is invited to attend the ceremony at 23322 Holly Park Drive, Gilpin Point, Preston, the site of his former plantation.Born in 1735 in Talbot County, Richardson was colonel of the Fifth Regiment of the Maryland Line and the Eastern Shore Battalion of the Flying Camp. He fought at the Battle of Harlem Heights. He died in 1825 at Gilpin Point.Colonel Richardson Middle and High schools in Federalsburg are named for him. Members of the high school band will perform at the ceremony.For more information call 609-605-2156 or emailgen-bensondar.org.

In accordance with Section 404(c) of the Talbot County Charter, "The Planning and Zoning Commission shall make advisory recommendations to the County Planning Officer and the Council relating to the Comprehensive Plan, the zoning maps, and rules and regulations relating to zoning.  Words

 Caption: TALBOT HUMANE
 
Celia is a 5-year-old spayed female who has lived her life as an outdoor cat. Being at the shelter is very scary for Celia, who would do best in a home where she could be both indoor and outdoor. She has a strong independent spirit and loves the freedom of the outdoors but also loves a warm lap and gentle pets. Celia is shy with new people and takes time to warm up to them. Once she is comfortable, she is a really sweet cat with a gentle personality that is impossible not to fall in love with. She is a well-behaved cat that is relaxed and enjoys lounging around. Find out about adopting Celia by callingTalbot Humane,410-822-0107, or emailing info@talbothumane.org.

Interested parties may provide written comments on the application or request an informational hearing on any listed application.A request for a hearing must be in writing and provide the following information: 1) Name, Address, and Telephone Number of the person making the request; 2) The identity of any other person(s) the requestor is representing; and 3) the specific issues proposed to be considered at the hearing. Please refer to the case number (i.e., 00-NT-0000, 00-WL-000, 00-WP-000, 00-WQC-0000) which identifies each application.Address correspondence to the attention of the Administration contact contained in the project's public notice. If none is listed, send correspondence to the Wetlands and Waterways Program, Water and Science Administration, 1800 Washington Boulevard Baltimore, Maryland, 21230. For questions regarding any public notice, you can contact the Wetlands and Waterways Program by Telephone; (410) 537-3751.Written comments or requests for a hearing must be received on or before November 20,2023 unless otherwise noted in the Public Notice.Talbot County 23-WL-0455/Town of Easton, 14 S Harrison Street, Easton, MD 21601, applied to install a 20-foot long by 6-foot 8 inch wide floating platform with a 24-foot long by 5-foot wide kayak launch platform, two 40-foot long rails supported by four two-inch wide galvanized pipes, an irregular 10-foot long by 5-foot wide platform, and a 5-foot wide by 16-foot long gangway, all extending 30 feet channelward of mean high water.Town of Easton has also applied to construct a 12-foot wide by 35-foot long sand kayak launch, all extending a maximum of 20 feet channelward of mean high water. This project will require mitigation for the 420 square feet of vegetated tidal wetlands that are proposed to be impacted by the construction of the sand kayak launch. The applicant will mitigate by restoring 650 square feet of a degraded low marsh with sand fill and Spartina Alterniflora plantings and by removing 1,160 square feet of Phragmites. The purpose of this project is to create kayak access for the public and organizations to engage in education, research, monitoring, and recreation. The proposed project is located within the tidal waters of the Tred Avon River along the shoreline of 672 W Glenwood Ave, Easton, MD. The public comment period closes November 20, 2023. The public comment period closes November 20, 2023. For more information, please contact Michaela Harrington at michaela.harrington@maryland. gov or at 410-537-4182.3038734 SD 11/3/2023TOWN OF EASTON NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING PROPOSED AMENDMENTS TO CHAPTER 28 OF THE EASTON TOWN CODE (ZONING) The Council of the Town of Easton will hold a public hearing on Monday, November 6, 2023 at 5:35 P.M. in the Council Meeting Room, 14 South Harrison Street. The purpose of this hearing is to solicit public comment on various proposed amendments to Chapter 28 of the Town Code (Zoning). Specifically, twelve amendments addressing a variety of issues are proposed The purpose of the proposed amendments is to correct oversights/omissions resulting from the original enactment of the comprehensive update of the Zoning Code completed in November of 2021, based upon the Planning Commission and staff's experiences in working with this new document.The public is hereby invited to comment on the proposed amendments.Such comments may be either submitted in writing at any time prior to the Hearing, or made in person at the Hearing. The complete packet of specific amendments is on file in the office of the Town Planner and is available for public inspection during normal business hours and may also be found on the Town of Easton's website (www.Eastonmd.gov). In general terms, the proposed amendments address the following issues:· The addition of Short-Term Housing as a Use in Table 312 A, the MXW USe Table.· Revisions to Table 2.1, the overall Table of Permissible Uses, with a focus on Uses 103.1 - 103.9, the "Middle Housing" use types.· The deletion of the supplemental standard which requires a 1,000 foot separation of liquor stores (and other uses, by reference) from certain other uses.· Revision to the examples of non-material changes to Planned Unit Development (PUD) projects.· Revision of the wording of existing language regarding architectural styles associated with multi-family apartment complexes, and clarification that certain of the supplemental standards for this use are not applicable to projects in the Central Business Zoning District.· The addition of a new supplemental standard applicable to all middle housing types intended to insure that any such use remains of an appropriate height in the context of the neighborhood in which it is proposed.· Clarification that graphics included in the definitions of Middle Housing types are for illustrative purposes only.· The addition of the use "Any Middle Housing Type or Variation not listed above", and associated supplemental standards, to enable consideration of a middle housing type not contemplated or described by the existing list of such uses.· Revision to the language describing how expired or soon-expiring PUD projects may be treated.· The correction of an inadvertent redundancy of the use "Live-Work Unit" in the Zoning Code.· Revisions to the language prohibiting the enactment of negative use restrictions concerning grocery stores by exempting grocery stores of less than 15,000 square feet from any such use restrictions.In addition, the Town Council solicits the public's input on two potential revisions to the draft amendments that the Planning Commission has forwarded. These are:· Continuing to maintain the more intense Middle Housing types as Special Exception uses in some zoning districts. This would mean Cottage Courts, Townhouses, Mansion Apartments, and Courtyard Buildings would remain SE in the R-10A and R-7A zoning districts, but would be outright permitted in the CB District. Fourplex stacked and triplex stacked would become outright permitted uses in all zoning districts.· Revising the language concerning the expiration of PUD approvals to allow for an initial approval of three years or a longer period if specifically requested and approved by the Town Council pursuant to their legislative approval (rather than the current two years).Persons wishing to attend or participate in the public hearing who require special accommodations or assistance because of a disability should contact the Town Clerk, Kathy Ruf at the Town Office, telephone number (410) 822-2525 during normal business hours by October 30, 2023.Kathy M. Ruf Town Clerk 3037405 SD 10/22,11/3/2023PLANNING COMMISSION VACANCY The Talbot County Council is seeking an individual for appointment to a vacancy on the County's Planning and Zoning Commission.Interested applicants must be residents of Talbot County who have been qualified voters for at least two (2) years. In accordance with Section 404(c) of the Talbot County Charter, "The Planning and Zoning Commission shall make advisory recommendations to the County Planning Officer and the Council relating to the Comprehensive Plan, the zoning maps, and rules and regulations relating to zoning. The Planning and Zoning Commission shall have final decision-making authority over major subdivisions and commercial and industrial site plan review.The Council, by resolution, may provide for reference to the Commission for review and recommendations, any additional matters related to the Commission's functions and duties." Should you be interested in serving the County in this capacity, please complete the "Request for Appointment" form found on the County's website www.talbotcountymd.gov and forward your one page resume to the Office of the County Manager, Talbot County Courthouse, 11 North Washington Street, Suite 13, Easton, Maryland 21601. Submittal deadline for receipt of resumes is Wednesday, November 8, 2023 at Noon.  Words

 GREENSBORO - Although hundreds of donations have come in for the Greensboro Winter Clothes Giveaway on Friday, Nov. 17, organizer Cathy Spencer is still looking for more."I said we're going to do it bigger this year, but I didn't mean" Spencer said as she laughed and gestured to dozens of boxes still to be unpacked and organized.New and gently used coats, jackets, hats, scarves and gloves in all sizes will be available for free Friday, Nov. 17, at the Greensboro Meeting Hall.The event is hosted by the Greensboro Connects Initiative.Donations can be dropped off at the Town Hall during normal business hours."I've got a great group of volunteers coming," Spencer said."We're not putting it all out at one time because we're open from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. and then we're open 4 to 7 p.m., and I might even open up Saturday if I have a lot left." For more information, contact Amanda Weaver at 410-482-6222 or aweaver@greensboromd.com. 
 
 Caption: CONNIE CONNOLLY/STAR DEMOCRAT

 Words 

 Read News Document

 Following an article published Nov. 3, the Star Democrat learned the following about 807 N. Washington St. property: George Lee Whiteley built the original 1,391 square foot home in 1930. He had three chicken houses on the 2.71 acre property until his passing in 1963. They were later moved to a property in Caroline County after his death.The Whiteley's also owned the Easton Candy Company and several hundred acres in Trappe.Whiteley owned a trucking company with his brother Olen Whiteley, who owned Whiteley's Store in Bruceville (Trappe).Their trucks were kept at 807 N.Washington St.Whiteley's wife, Della Whiteley, resided at 807 N.Washington St. until her passing in 1992. Her grandson lived there until 2002. The property was sold in 2021 by the four grandchildren, the heirs to the property.

Info: 410-226-5904 or www.oxfordcc.org.SOUP'N WALK, Walk, 11 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., Adkins Arboretum.Theme: Autumn Harvest.Hunt for nutritious berries, nuts and seeds and check for signs of beaver. title: Brighter Christmas Fund - CARING & SHARING
content:
Brighter Christmas Fund - CARING & SHARING

 November 15, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 4A | Section: News 
 
 231
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Families needing assistance are urged to apply as soon as possible. To be eligible for assistance, youmust be a resident of Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's or Talbot counties.If you receive assistance from social services, you must apply through your agency.If you do not receive assistance from social services, applications can be picked up in the lobby at The Star Democrat's office, located at 29088 Airpark Dr, Easton.Youmust submit with your application: · Copies of Social Securitycards for adults and children on application · Proof ofhomeaddress (copyofutilitybill, rent or mortgage payment inyour name) · Proof of income(copyof 2022 incometax returnand/or last twopay stubs).Return the completed application no later than 3 pm, December 1.Eligible families may receive a shopping voucher for $100 per child, with a $300 maximum per family, to be redeemed at their local Walmart. Shopping must be done by Sunday, December 31. A total of $100,000 will be given out for this year's Brighter Christmas Fund, so families are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.Families may receive assistance from the Brighter Christmas Fund for up to three consecutive years. Families that have received funds from the program for three years in a row must wait one year before they are eligible to reapply.Brighter Christmas Fund awards are dependent on donations from the community.Filling out an application does not guarantee that you will receive anything.

title: PET OF THE WEEK
content:
PET OF THE WEEK

 November 21, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2A | Section: News 
 
 200
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Caption: Meet Sheba, a beautiful 5-year-old spayed female pitbull mix who's ready for a loving forever home. Sheba is a resilient girl who has spent her entire life living outside, so she's eager to experience the comforts of indoor life. She's hoping to find a family who will give her a warm bed, plenty of toys, and lots of love. Although Sheba can be a little shy at first, she is a very friendly dog who loves cuddles and pets once she gets to know you. Her charming smile is just irresistible, and it's hard not to fall in love with her gentle disposition. She is also very playful and loves to chase after toys, making her a great companion for anyone who wants an active and affectionate pet. Because Sheba hasn't had much experience with new environments, it can take her some time to adjust. But with patience and loving support, she will soon blossom into a confident and happy dog who will bring joy to any home. She would do best in a quiet and loving household that will give her the attention and care she deserves. If you are interested in adopting Sheba and giving her the warm home that she deserves call 410-822-0107 or email info@talbothumane.org.

title: Toys for Tots collection gets underway
content:
Toys for Tots collection gets underway

 November 22, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 12 | Section: News 
 
 327
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE - The annual Toys for Tots collection drive has already begun in advance of this year's upcoming holiday. Jamie Brown of Centreville is this year's chair, taking over from longtime Chair Craig Manning, also of Centreville.Brown is coordinating toy collections for all five Mid-Shore counties Kent, Queen Anne's, Talbot, Caroline and Dorchester.Saturday, Nov. 18, was the kickoff for this year's collection campaign with a meeting at American Legion Jeff Davis Post 18, in Centreville. The Kingsman Run Motorcycle Group, who have been involved collecting toys of this event for more than 40 years, has been joined by the Legion Riders of Post 18 in this year's efforts.For more information about the many drop-off locations in the Mid-Shore area, go online at Midshore-md. toysfortots.org, or facebook.com/Mid-ShoreToys4Tots. These websites also provide parents with pre-registration information if they are in need of help for Christmas for their children, and pick-up dates, times, and locations.Any further questions can be directed to Brown at centreville.md@toysfortots.org. Parent will have to bring with them, proof of residence and proof of life for each child. Parents can also sign-up in person Sunday, Nov. 26, at the American Legion in Centreville, from noon - 3 p.m. or at the VFW on Glebe Road in Easton from 5 - 8 p.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 29. Once they sign-up, and are approved, they will be contacted with a distribution date and time to pick-up toys for their children. 
 
 Caption: DOUG BISHOP
 
Left, Michael and Jamie Brown, this year's Toys for Tots Mid-Shore chair, of Centreville are joined Saturday, Nov. 18, by members of Centreville American Legion Jeff Davis Post 18 Legion Riders and members of the Kingsman Run Motorcycle Group. This year, the Legion Riders joined forces with the Kingsman who have been involved with collecting Toys for Tots for more than 40 years. Donation/collections of toys have already begun. See website Midshore-md.toysfortots.org or facebook.com/MidShoreToys4Tots for where to drop off toys and parent registration information and dates/times for distribution.

The project is located at 480 Port Street in Easton, Maryland, southeast of the intersection of Port Street and Meadow Drive. The project aims to serve a need for the community and the proposed structure will include a community hub, behavioral health suite, office and training spaces, and affordable housing to those most vulnerable to rising living costs in Maryland.Approximately 4,899.4 square feet (sf) of the wetland will be impacted by the construction of the new facility and associated parking area. Activities impacting the wetland include excavation, removal of vegetation, filling, and grading. The project was designed to leave pockets of wetlands undisturbed on-site.HUD has considered the following alternatives and mitigation measures to be taken to minimize adverse impacts and to restore and preserve natural and beneficial values: Three alternatives were investigated including two alternative sites and the "no action" alternative. The subject property was chosen because the area is part of the Port Street Redevelopment Plan and is in proximity to downtown Easton, the waterfront area, and has access to recreation areas such as the rail trail and nearby parks.Permits for this work include a Nontidal Wetlands and Waterways permit from the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) as well as a Maryland State Programmatic General Permit-6 (MDSPGP-6) from the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Authorization Number: 22-NT-2038/202260713. The MDSPGP-6 permit allows for the construction of the new building, associated parking areas, stormwater management, and other features. The project will be designed and permitted to comply with all federal, state, and local codes and regulations.HUD has reevaluated the alternatives to building in the wetland and has determined that it has no practicable alternative. Environmental files that document compliance with steps 3 through 6 of Executive Order 11990, are available for public inspection, review and copying upon request at the times and location delineated in the last paragraph of this notice for receipt of comments.There are three primary purposes for this notice. First, people who may be affected by activities in wetlands and those who have an interest in the protection of the natural environment should be given an opportunity to express their concerns and provide information about these areas. Second, an adequate public notice program can be an important public educational tool. The dissemination of information about wetlands can facilitate and enhance Federal efforts to reduce the risks associated with the occupancy and modification of these special areas. Third, as a matter of fairness, when the Federal government determines it will participate in actions taking place in a wetland, it must inform those who may be put at greater or continued risk.Written comments must be received by HUD no later than November 29, 2023. They should be addressed to Mr. Kerry Johnson, Field Environmental Officer, U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, Region III, 600 E. Broad Street, Richmond, VA 23219-1800, (800) 842-2610 ext. 4803 or (804) 822-4803. content:
PET OF THE WEEK

 November 28, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 180
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Caption: TALBOT HUMA NE
 
Meet Fendy, the sweet and affectionate 2-year-old spayed pitbull mix who is looking for her forever home. Fendy is an adorable girl who loves nothing more than pleasing her people. She is a happy and active dog who enjoys going for long walks and playing in the yard. Fendy is a little shy around new people, but once she gets to know you, she is truly a loving companion. She thrives on human affection and loves to cuddle up with her owner for snuggles and pets. While Fendy enjoys the company of other dogs, she is a bit particular about them. She prefers the company of male dogs her size, as they make her feel more comfortable and secure. She is not a fan of female dogs. Fendy is a smart and eager learner who does well with positive reinforcement training. She is already spayed, so there will be no worries about unwanted litters. She is up to date with all her vaccinations and is in good health. If you want to provide Fendy with a forever home, call 410-822-0107 or email info@talbothumane.org.

title: Highway Administration to host open house on Shore Highway study
author: Contributed
content:
Highway Administration to host open house on Shore Highway study

 November 29, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: 17 | Section: News 
 
 264
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration will host a public open house on Wednesday, Dec. 6, to share information and answer questions about the agency's study of MD 404 (Shore Highway) between MD 16 (Harmony Road) and MD 16 (Greenwood Road) in Denton.The purpose of this study, according to a release from the SHA, is to assess the transportation needs along MD 404, including traffic operations safety and pedestrian and bicyclist accommodations.The public open house will be held from 5 to 7 p.m. in the Denton Elementary School cafeteria, located at 303 Sharp Road in Denton.The study team began planning for potential improvements along MD 404 in spring 2023. Known as a Planning and Environmental Linkages Study (PEL), the effort considers environmental, community and economic goals early in the planning stage.This study helps to identify needs and recommend improvements to move into the preliminary design phase and is anticipated to be complete in spring 2024.During the public open house, a study overview, as well as information about existing conditions, environmental features, corridor needs, a proposed study schedule, preliminary findings, recommendations and next steps, will be provided.The State Highway Administration also is accepting public input through a survey accessible on the Project Portal Page.Those requiring assistance to participate in the public open house, such as a need for an interpreter for hearing/speech difficulties or assistance with the English language, may send an email to SHATitleVI@MDOTmaryland.gov.For a list of all major State Highway Administration projects, visit the project portal or the homepage at roads.maryland. gov. For a look at real-time traffic conditions, go to md511.maryland.gov.

author: Contributed

Be a Santa to a senior

 November 29, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: 7 | Section: News 
 
 525
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON - This year, Home Instead is celebrating 20 years of bringing joy to the Easton community with Be a Santa to a Senior, a gift-giving program for older adults who may be overlooked, isolated or alone during the holiday season.Since the program's nationwide inception in 2003, Be a Santa to a Senior has engaged more than 65,000 volunteers, provided more than 2.2 million gifts and shared the holiday spirit with about 800,000 older adults."The holidays can be hard for many older adults, especially those who may not have a companion to share them with and it's incredibly rewarding to see the impact that Be a Santa to a Senior has had over the past 20 years," said Jennifer Marchi, owner of the Easton Home Instead office. "Gifts aside, the true value is the connection Be a Santa to a Senior makes between the community and our older neighbors." This year, program coordinators hope to collect gifts for 800 local older adults.To participate, shoppers can look for Be a Santa to a Senior trees or displays at locations around the area.Ornaments featuring the name and desired gift of an older adult will be on display, and shoppers can buy the requested gift and return it wrapped to the location with the ornament attached.Ornaments will be available until December 1. title: St. Michaels Community Center renovations to be topic of upcoming dinner
content:
St. Michaels Community Center renovations to be topic of upcoming dinner

 November 30, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 6 | Section: News 
 
 384
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The public is invited to a waterfront dinner and a presentation about the St. Michaels Community Center's renovations and programs at the Miles River Yacht Club in St.Michaels on Thursday, Jan. 11, beginning at 6:00 p.m.The Yacht Club's Sail Committee sponsors the speaker series, with Jan. 11 speakers including St. Michaels Community Center Board Chair Langley Shook, Executive Director Patrick Rofe, and renovation project architect Mark McInturff, FAIA.The panelists will provide updates as they discuss and take questions from the audience about SMCC's current building renovations and what the future holds for community food distribution, a new culinary and hospitality workforce development program, education, technology and more.The event is $30 per person, including dinner and a cash bar.Reservations are required by Monday, Jan. 8, by calling the Yacht Club at 410-745-9511, extension 6.The renovations on SMCC's building at 103 Railroad Avenue are expected to be completed in early 2024 and will provide state-of-the-art spaces for more children and adult programs. The renovated Community Center will also provide several classrooms and a large common area for community gatherings, complete with audio-visual technology for presentations and screenings.The renovations also will house a modern, well-equipped commercial kitchen, where SMCC will train people for jobs in restaurants and hotels, and from which the Center can continue to serve and deliver prepared meals as well as tens of thousands of bags of groceries to those in need."We're grateful to the Miles River Yacht Club and its Sailing Committee for opening this event to the public," said Rofe."It will be a great evening out with a delicious dinner and an informative talk about how we will serve our neighbors from the Oak Creek Bridge in Royal Oak all the way down to Tilghman Island through expanded programs and our renovated building."Rofe said the Center serves the community at large with programs and activities for all ages, and that its food distribution services help provide for the area's low-income workers, homebound and other senior citizens, those facing disabilities, and families in emergencies.Donations to the St. Michaels Community Center's annual fund and proceeds from its Treasure Cove Thrift Shop, located on Railroad Avenue in St. Michaels, help provide essential human services, programs and community events for people in St. Michaels and from throughout Maryland's Bay Hundred area.

title: Dorchester County Public Library to change hours at both locations
author: Maggie Trovato; mtrovato@chespub.com
content:
Dorchester County Public Library to change hours at both locations

 December 1, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Maggie Trovato; mtrovato@chespub.com | Page: 8 | Section: News 
 
 476
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CAMBRIDGE - The Dorchester County Public Library is changing its hours at both its Cambridge and Hurlock locations.In a letter posted online and addressed to Dorchester Public Library patrons, Library Director Crystal Henningsen said these decreases in operational hours are temporary.Beginning Dec. 4, the Cambridge branch will be open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.Monday through Saturday.The Hurlock branch will be open from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Monday through Wednesday, and it will be open from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Thursday.In an interview, Henningsen she has received both positive and negative feedback regarding these changes in hours."Most of our patrons have been very supportive," she said. "But the truth of the matter is that the staff doesn't want to do this. It's being done out of necessity."The letter states that this decision was made due to staffing shortages as well as "an increase in incidents at the Cambridge branch."While Henningsen said in the interview that she could not go into detail on the increase in incidents at the Cambridge branch, she said that it's been all age groups and both inside and outside the library."Ultimately, what it really is, is some of the things that we're seeing within the community as it's experiencing its challenges, has now filtered their way into the library," she said.In response to these incidents, the library's Board of Trustees voting unanimously to adopt the temporary 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. schedule in Cambridge.The library is taking steps to ensure patron safety and will be installing a new security system at the Cambridge branch in mid-December, Henningsen said. She will be meeting with Cambridge Police Chief Justin Todd to talk about a possible partnership, as well.Henningsen said she is interested to see how opening at 9 a.m., rather than 10 a.m., goes."We're going to use that to the patron's advantage and try to see if that public service hour makes a big difference," she said.At the end of her letter, Henningsen said the library hopes to begin discussing operational hours "that best meet the community's changing needs" at the beginning of the new year.In the interview, she said she hopes that, by February, the library will be able to return to some of its original hours."We want to go back to providing at least one evening per week," she said. "But there are just some measures we have to have into place before we can do that."Henningsen said that the main thing she would like to stress is that this change is temporary."We are hoping that we can change this before spring," she said. "We don't want to keep it this way." 
 
 Caption: The Cambridge branch of the Dorchester County Public Library on Nov. 30. Both the Cambridge and Hurlock branches will have new hours of operation beginning Dec. 4.

title: Life - Rotarians Holding Food Drive In Honor Of Late Lord Scott
author: Contributed
content:
Life - Rotarians Holding Food Drive In Honor Of Late Lord Scott

 December 6, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: 6 | Section: News 
 
 473
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON. The Rotary Club of Easton and other community partners are teaming up to host the Drop for Scotty Community Food Drive through the end of December.The food drive is named after the late Lord "Scotty" Scott Sr., who passed away in January 2020.Scott was well-known throughout Easton and Talbot County for hosting his annual Operation Christmas Spirit event at the Easton Volunteer Fire Department.Established in the 1970s, Operation Christmas Spirit made the holidays brighter for thousands through a large community meal and gifts for local children, supported by volunteers and donations."Scotty's kindness and love for the community knew no bounds, and this food drive is a way to honor his giving spirit," said Andrew Walsworth, Easton Rotary president. "Our club is privileged to carry on his legacy, continue his good work and provide direct relief to families in Talbot County during this holiday season." Individuals and organizations may drop off non-perishable food at 2023 designated drop sites: ¡ The ARC Chesapeake on N. Hanson Street ¡ BAAM on Jowite Street ¡ Bay Capital Mortgage on E. Dover Street ¡ BSC Group on Bay Street ¡ Critchlow Adkins on N. Magnolia Street or on Glenwood ¡ Eastern Shore Land Conservancy on S. Washington Street ¡ Easton Visitors Center on S. Harrison Street ¡ Easton Family YMCA on S. Washington Street or Peachblossom ¡ 4H Extension Office on Mary's Court ¡ Harris Teeter on Marlboro Avenue ¡ Mid Atlantic Tire on Teal Drive ¡ Provident State Bank on N. Harrison Street ¡ Queenstown Bank on N. Washington Street ¡ Saints Peter and Paul on High Street or S. Washington Street ¡ Shore United Bank on East Dover Street ¡ Marlboro Ave or Elliott Road ¡ Star Democrat on Airpark Drive ¡ Talbot County Library on West Dover Street ¡ Willow Construction on Commerce Drive.In addition to dropping off food, the community may also make a financial contribution to the Easton Rotary's Youth and Community Fund by visiting dropforscotty.com. Funds raised will be used to purchase additional food and critical supplies.All food and financial donations will stay local and will support vulnerable families in Talbot County.The Rotary Club of Easton Maryland is comprised of nearly 100 professional men and women committed to the Rotary Motto, "Service Above Self." They are part of a global network of more than 1.2 million Rotarians who are changing lives in their own communities and around the world.As the world's first Rotary Club in a town of fewer than 10,000 people, The Rotary Club of Easton celebrated its centennial in 2021. The Rotary Club of Easton meets on Thursdays at noon at Scossa Restaurant, with guests welcome. For more information, please visit eastonrotary.org.

title: Col. Tench Tilghman Chapter of the SAR holding holiday social
author: Contributed
content:
Col. Tench Tilghman Chapter of the SAR holding holiday social

 December 8, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: 8 | Section: News 
 
 371
 Words 

 Read News Document

 On Thursday, Dec. 14, the Colonel Tench Tilghman Chapter of the Sons of the American Revolution will conduct a meet-and-greet social event at the White Swan Tavern in Chestertown from 4:30 to 6:30 p.m.The local chapter of the SAR is inviting all its members, spouses and anyone interested in learning more about the SAR to come out during the holiday season to enjoy food and beverages and to socialize with members of the SAR.The White Swan Tavern is a historic building located at 231 High Street and has been used since the early 1700s as a tannery, private home and inn.Have you ever considered joining the SAR? To join one must be a lineal descendant of an American Revolutionary War patriot.Did any of your male ancestors:▪Serve in the Continental Army or Navy?▪Sign the Oath of Fidelity to support the cause of independence?Did any of your ancestors, male or female:▪Render material aid to the cause such as furnishing supplies or paying a tax to support the cause?▪Provide any type of civil service to support the new state or provisional government?▪Provide medical assistance (e.g., as a physical, surgeon, or nurse) to aid the wounded?If so, and you can show direct unbroken lineage to one of these individuals, you would qualify to join the Sons of the American Revolution or Daughters of the American Revolution.A member of the General Perry Benson Chapter of the Daughter of the American Revolution will also be present on Dec. 14 to answer questions about the DAR.The Colonel Tench Tilghman Chapter of the SAR serves citizens in in Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne fs and Talbot Counties.The National Society of the Sons of the American Revolution, founded in 1889, is a nonprofit and non-partisan organization dedicated to promoting patriotism, preserving American History and promoting education to future generations.To learn more about the Colonel Tench Tilghman Chapter of the SAR, please visit its Facebook page at facebook.com/ColTenchTilghman.If interested in attending this event, please contact Warren Tewes at wdtewes@gmail.com by Friday, Dec. 8, to RSVP, and advise how many will be in your party.

content:
PET OF THE WEEK

 December 12, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 169
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Caption: TALBOT HUMANE
 
Meet Maverick, a handsome 4-year-old neutered pitbull mix who will steal your heart with his sweet and gentle personality. Maverick is a cuddle boy who loves nothing more than being close to his people. He's very clingy and wants to be with his family all the time. He's a very affectionate boy who will follow his people around the house, constantly wagging his tail and giving kisses. Maverick is selective about the dog friends he will tolerate. He prefers dogs who are low energy and leave him alone. He is protective of his people and can get a bit anxious if he feels like they are in danger. Once he's attached, he will want to protect you at all costs. Maverick would be a great fit for a family who can provide him lots of love and attention. He loves kids and would make a great companion for a family. He's looking for a family who can appreciate his gentle nature and provide him with a loving home. To learn about adopting Maverick, go to talbothumane.org/pets/maverick.

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: B6 | Section: News

 Now through Dec. 30, tickets can be purchased for a chance to win one of three highly sought-after and collectable bourbons: a Little Book Chapter 07, an Old Fitzgerald Bottled in-Bond 11 year and a Willett 8 year.These rare whiskies are prized by collectors, extremely difficult to find and would make unforgettable holiday gifts, said organizers of the fundraiser raffle.
All of the proceeds from this year's raffle will be divided equally between the Tilghman Area Youth Association, The Eastern Shore Land Conservancy and Bay Hundred Community Volunteers, local nonprofits doing important work in our community every day.
Tickets are $25 each or five for $100 and can only be purchased at Town and Country Wine, Liquor, Etc., located at 28248 St. Michaels Road in Easton.
The drawing will be held on Facebook Live on Dec. 30.
T&C's Rare Bourbon Raffle started in 2020 as a way to help raise money for local non-profits during the pandemic, and in a short three years, has raised over $22,000 for organizations including: CASA Mid-Shore, Habitat for Humanity, Pickering Creek Audubon Center, Talbot Mentors, Talbot Hospice, St. Michaels Volunteer Fire Department, St. Michaels Community Center, Talbot Interfaith Shelter and For All Seasons.
Questions will be cheerfully answered at 410-822-1433.

title: Nominations Sought For Women & Girls Fund Award
author: Contributed
content:
Nominations Sought For Women & Girls Fund Award

 December 15, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Contributed | Page: 8 | Section: News 
 
 319
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Women & Girls Fund of the Mid-Shore is accepting nominations for its annual Women & Girls Fund Award.Established in 2004, the award honors a community member from Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's or Talbot counties who has made outstanding professional or personal contributions towards addressing the needs of local women and girls.
Candidates for this award should have demonstrated leadership, vision, integrity, compassion, cooperation and generosity of time and talent in their efforts to improve the lives and opportunities of women and girls.
The 2023 Women & Girls Fund Award was presented to Jo Ann Asparagus Murray of McDaniel for her outstanding professional and personal contributions to the Mid-Shore.
As an attorney, now retired, she served as the Family Law Magistrate in Caroline County, and, later, as the Domestic Relations Master for the Second Judicial Circuit (Caroline, Kent, Queen Anne's and Talbot counties).
Committed to community service, Asparagus Murray has volunteered - and continues to volunteer - for many organizations, including Habitat for Humanity, Talbot Mentors, Mid-Shore Pro Bono, Talbot Interfaith Shelter and her sorority, Kappa Theta Omega Chapter of Alpha Kappa Alpha.
She is a past president of the Talbot County Board of Education and current commissioner for the Talbot County Police Accountability Board.
She has made long-lasting contributions to improving the lives of women, girls and families in the Mid-Shore.
The late Lois Duffy of Centreville and Chestertown was the first recipient of the award. In succeeding years, the Women & Girls Fund has honored: the late Harriet Critchlow; Sandra King; Dr. Maria Boria; Sister Patricia Gamgort, OSB; Tracy Davenport; Sandra Redd; Sara Jane Davidson; Judge Karen Murphy Jensen; the five founders of For All Seasons Behavioral Health and Rape Crisis Center; Mary Lou McAllister; Diana Mautz; the late Kathy Weaver; Ellen Rajacich; Susan Stockman; Krista Pettit; Carlene Wilson; Julie Lowe; and Chrissy Aull.
The application deadline is Jan. 15. Nomination forms can be downloaded from womenandgirlsfund.org/awards.
For further information, contact 410-770-8347 or info@womenandgirlsfund.org.

title: Caroline County Commission to meet Jan. 9
author: STAFF REPORT
content:
Caroline County Commission to meet Jan. 9

 December 20, 2023 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: STAFF REPORT | Page: A8 | Section: News 
 
 242
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON - The next meeting of the Caroline County Commission will be held 9 a.m. Tuesday, Jan. 9, 2024, in Room 106, Caroline County Courthouse, 109 Market St., Denton.The commission will not meet Dec. 26 or Jan. 2, 2024, due to the upcoming holidays.
Meetings are held 9 a.m.
Tuesdays except the fifth Tuesday of the month, unless announced otherwise. They are sometimes moved to a different location to accommodate larger attendance.
Meetings are open to the public, and attendees will be security screened as they enter the courthouse.
All Commission agendas with hyperlinks to documents can be found at www. carolinemd.org.
The public can also attend meetings and work sessions remotely via ZOOM at https://zoom. us/j/300062187. The toll-free phone numbers to dial in are 888-475-4499 or 877-853-5257, and the meeting ID number is 300 062 187.
Public comment will be held during the beginning and end of each meeting.
You may submit written comments through the county's email system, website, and by USPS at 109 Market Street, Room 123, Denton, MD 21629. Written comments received prior to a meeting will be entered into the record and made available to the Commissioners prior to the meeting or hearing.
All speakers, including the Commissioners must announce their name each time before they speak. Any document being voted on by the Commissioners will be linked on the agenda in advance when possible. 
 
 Caption: MICKEY PULLEN

 The Caroline County Commissioners will meet at the Caroline County Courthouse, decorated here for the 2023 holiday season.

title: Brighter Christmas fund assists single mother with holiday gifts
content:
Brighter Christmas fund assists single mother with holiday gifts

 January 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Page: 2 | Section: News 
 
 261
 Words 

 Read News Document

 A single mother was struggling to purchase Christmas gifts for her 4-month-old while finishing college and working full time."I support my family by working full time and making sure that my baby's needs are met first," she said. "I am currently a college student working on my bachelor's degree so I can get a better paying job in the future." The mother received assistance with her family's holiday celebration from the Brighter Christmas Fund.
Though awards for this year have already been distributed, your donation to the Brighter Christmas Fund can help families in similar situations provide holiday gifts for their children in years to come.
The Brighter Christmas Fund is a nonprofit charity which helps families in need on the Mid-Shore, may be sent to The Star Democrat, 29088 Airpark Dr., Easton, MD 21601. Donations also may be made online via credit card or PayPal at brighterchristmasfund.org. Click the "Donate" button. Donations are tax-deductible.
The administrative costs for the Brighter Christmas Fund are covered entirely by The Star Democrat and APG Chesapeake, so 100% of donations go to families in need. For more information about the fund, call 410-200-1884.
The total donated for this year's Brighter Christmas Fund to date is $65,165.

 Words 

 Read News Document
