Info: chesapeakfilmfestival.com.

 Those seeking to have events, services or times of worship published in the Star Democrat's weekly religion calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.PANCAKE SUPPER, Feb. 13, 4:30 to 7 p.m., Christ Episcopal Church, 601 Church Street, Cambridge. Members are invited to Pancake Supper at Whatley Hall. Call the Church office for any information: 410-228-3161, Monday through Thursday, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.
All Faith Chapel, 26282 Tunis Mills Road, Easton. Sunday service 9:30 a.m. followed by coffee hour. First and third Sundays, Holy Eucharist; second and fourth Sundays, morning prayer. Fifth Sunday, vicar's choice. The Rev. Patricia Drost Kuhns. Info: allfaithtunismills@gmail.com
Asbury United Methodist Church, 18 S. Higgins St., Easton. 10 a.m. Sunday worship service. Bible Study 6 p.m. Tuesday. Pastor Reginald Pinkett.
Bethel AME Church, Chestertown. Conference call worship, prayer and study. Dial in: 425-436-6341, access code: 540836. If unable to join the call after several attempts, call the backup number: 520-420-9081 and follow instructions given. Worship service: Sundays 11 a.m. to noon. Corporate prayer: Mondays 7 to 7:30 p.m. Life Application Bible study: Wednesdays 7 to 8 p.m. All are welcome.
Bethesda Methodist Church, 155 Main St.. P.O. Box 147, Preston. Contemporary Service at 9 a.m.Traditional Service at 11 a.m. Bethesda Bible Adventures at 9 a.m. Adult Bible Study at 10 a.m. Pastor Paul Lewis. Info: 410-673-7538 or bethesdapreston.faith

title: For All Seasons to host online Valentine's auction
author: FOR ALL SEASONS
content:
For All Seasons to host online Valentine's auction

 February 1, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: FOR ALL SEASONS | Section: Life 
 
 257
 Words 

 Read News Document

 For All Seasons is hosting a Valentine's Day Silent Auction online from Feb. 8 to Feb. 14, featuring one-of-a-kind experiences and unique getaways to benefit the agency's mental health and victim services.Among the items included in the upcoming auction are:
Two-Hour Sail on the Chesapeake Bay. Set sail aboard the Woodwind, a beautiful, wooden 74-foot schooner. Whether you try raising the sails, steering the boat, or simply relaxing, you are sure to enjoy every minute as you sail from the Annapolis waterfront, past the Naval Academy, and into the Chesapeake Bay.
Couples Photoshoot. Capture the essence of your love with a couple's photoshoot, the perfect Valentine's Day gift.
Eastern Shore Golf Experience for Four. Enjoy the fresh air and beautiful views during a round of golf for four at these scenic courses: Chester River Yacht & Country Club, Hyatt River Marsh Golf Club, and Prospect Bay Country Club.
Two-night stay at Ocean City Resort. Treat your Valentine to a luxurious getaway. Enjoy two nights for two at Ashore, a beautiful new beachfront resort in Ocean City, Maryland.
Create & Name Your Own Ice Cream. Surprise your Valentine with the opportunity to collaborate with the Scottish Highland Creamery to invent and name an original ice cream flavor. Includes four delicious quarts to enjoy at home (or share with friends).
If you have a unique experience you would like to donate to the For All Seasons Valentine's Day Silent Auction, email Kelsey Trumbull-Meyers, event coordinator, at ktmeyers@forallseasonsinc.org. To preview the auction site, visit forallseasonsinc.lpages.co/valentines-auction-2024/.

 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have events, services or times of worship published in the Star Democrat's weekly religion calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.BLACK HISTORY MUSICAL PROGRAM, Feb. 17, 5 p.m., Union Baptist Church, Easton. The Covenant Gospel Choir, under the direction of Leroy "Spanky" Potter, along with The Second Generation Community Chorus, under the direction of Ambia Hooper, EBC For Christ Trio, and Ayla Dennis (Soloist) will be in concert. Free delivery is available for 4 or more. Call to preorder for carry-outs and delivery, 410-228-4910. Must use Glasgow Street entrances for easy access and parking.
HEALING THE DIVIDE, March 10, live music at 1:15 p.m., free talk at 2 p.m., Coats Masonic Lodge, 114 N. Washington St., Easton. How spiritual perception brings healing by Alexandre Fischer. Info: 410-924-3109.
All Faith Chapel, 26282 Tunis Mills Road, Easton. Sunday service 9:30 a.m. followed by coffee hour. First and third Sundays, Holy Eucharist; second and fourth Sundays, morning prayer. Fifth Sunday, vicar's choice. The Rev. Patricia Drost Kuhns. Info: allfaithtunismills@gmail.com
Anchor Church, 620 Goldsborough Street, Easton. Sunday morning at 10 a.m. Live stream on Facebook or on website. www.anchoreaston.com 410-822-3038

If unable to join the call after several attempts, call the backup number: 520-420-9081 and follow instructions given. Worship service: Sundays 11 a.m. to noon. Corporate prayer: Mondays 7 to 7:30 p.m. Life Application Bible study: Wednesdays 7 to 8 p.m. All are welcome.

Mid-Shore Calendar

 February 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Angela Price | Section: Calendar 
 
 2843
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.GARDEN LECTURE, 11 a.m. Talbot County Free Library, 100 W. Dover St., Easton. Talbot County Garden Club's Free Winter Lecture Series presents horticultural consultant, garden coach, award-winning educator/author/podcaster Eva Monheim on "Shrubs and Their Ecological Function in the Landscape." Info: connellypaige@gmail.com 301-641-7337.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WHEN DEMOCRACY FELL, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. Author Paul Callahan discusses his newly published book "When Democracy Fell" — a comprehensive exploration of Maryland's constitutional crisis during the U.S. Civil War. Free admission.
WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Wye Island NRMA, Dividing Creek Trail. Meet at Lodge LN parking area. Enjoy the brisk air of winter on these 3 to 5 mile hikes. Discover the diversity and wildlife of the area. Follow the Caroline County Schools for weather alerts. Bring water, snack, bug spray, hat. Karen.gianninoto@maryland.gov to register or for info.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborate with many different forms of media. Check out their art at Vintage Venue on Race Street. Artists are offering classes in Raku pottery, mixed media and fused glass jewelry making this month. Pottery and slip mold classes anticipated soon. New members welcome. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
CPR TRAINING MARATHON, Talbot County Community Center, 10028 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Training will take place all day long, with class times at 9 a.m., 11:30 a.m., 1 p.m., 2:30 p.m., 4 p.m. and 5:30 p.m. A certificate will be provided upon completion of the American Heart Association Friends and Family CPR & AED training. Each class is approximately 60 minutes. Classes are free. Registration requested: talbotdes.org/cpr.asp.

The artwork of Shelton Hawkins will be featured, including photos of his basketball murals around the world and his black and white photography. Hawkins will be joined in the gallery by the works of multi-disciplinary mixed media artist Zsudayka Nzinga, mixed media artist John Lister III and abstract Afro-Caribbean artist Bulsby "Buzz" Duncan.

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Editors Inbox

 David Reel, whose commentary articles often appear in the Star Democrat, is not the chairman of the Republican Central Committee in Talbot County. He has not been chairman or been a member of the party for over three years.He resigned as chair in December 2020 and resigned from the committee in February 2021. Reel says: "Since then I have not had any involvement or interaction with the committee. I do not even know exactly who is currently serving on the committee."
A letter to the editor in the March 17 Star Democrat with the headline "Thinking and reflecting," incorrectly stated Reel's role with the Republican Central Committee of Talbot County.

title: Queenstown American Legion hops into Easter
author: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com
content:
Queenstown American Legion hops into Easter

 March 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 144
 Words 

 Read News Document

 QUEENSTOWN — Despite a rainy forecast, American Legion Post 296 of Queenstown welcomed the community for fun games and sweet times with its Easter event with eggs and the Easter bunny March 23.In lieu of the Legion's traditional egg hunt across the lawn, kids of all ages flocked inside to the pavilion for an afternoon with homemade cupcake decorating, coloring pages, face painting, photos and goodie bags of eggs filled with prizes handed out by none other than the Easter Bunny.
One bag held the coveted golden egg with a "egg-citing" special surprise, according to Auxiliary President Nola Willis.
When the weather forecast came in, the Auxiliary wanted to still hold the event indoors to ensure springtime smiles brighter than a sunny-side-up egg.
"We've been doing this forever. It's all about the kids," Willis said.
American Legion Post 296 of Queenstown is located at 6200 Main St.

 March 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

Dover Street, Easton. Talbot County Garden Club's Free Winter Lecture Series concludes with "A Sneak Peek Preview of This Year's May 11 Talbot County Tour of the Maryland House & Garden Pilgrimage." Event co-chairs Zandi Nammack & Kim Eckert will present. Info: connellypaige@gmail.com 301-641-7337.

SOUP DAY, 11:30 a.m. to 1 p.m., Zion UMC, 612 Locust Street. Soups will be chicken noodle, vegetable beef, and peas and dumplings for dining in and carry out at $5 per cup meal or $8 per quart with biscuits. Free delivery is available for four or more. Call to preorder for carry-outs and delivery, 410-228-4910. Must use Glasgow Street entrances for easy access and parking.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com

Like their namesake from the Sly and the Family Stone classic, EDP plays music with good vibes, sings songs about coming together, caring for one another, and so on. edpdelmarva.com/.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 16 N. Second St., Denton, will open Saturdays, March 2, 9, 16, 23, and 30. Explore the history and culture of Caroline County through artifacts and exhibits. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055.
EASTER EGG HUNT, noon, Charles Bilbrough Memorial Park, Rt. 480, Greensboro. Sponsored by the Greensboro Lions Club. Hunt is open to all children 10 and under. All participants receive candy.
JEFF WASHINGTON, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Born in New York City and living much of his life in Philly, Jeff Washington serves up a diverse array of funk, blues, jazz, rock, and R&B with a classic urban feel. jeffwash.com.

Mid-Shore Calendar

 March 29, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Angela Price | Section: Calendar 
 
 3082
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
EVERYDAY PEOPLE, 8 p.m., Avalon Theater, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. A powerful young band of vocalists, focused heavily on harmony from both vocals and horns. Like their namesake from the Sly and the Family Stone classic, EDP plays music with good vibes, sings songs about coming together, caring for one another, and so on. edpdelmarva.com/.
CRYSTALS 101, 3 to 4 p.m., The Foundry, 401 Market St, Denton. Delve into the captivating realm of crystals with Kyleen's Crystals 101 class. Explore the ancient wisdom and healing properties of these mystical gems while crafting your own personalized keepsake. Reserve your spot today. $30/class.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 16 N. Second St., Denton, will open Saturdays, March 2, 9, 16, 23, and 30. Explore the history and culture of Caroline County through artifacts and exhibits. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055.
EASTER EGG HUNT, noon, Charles Bilbrough Memorial Park, Rt. 480, Greensboro. Sponsored by the Greensboro Lions Club. Hunt is open to all children 10 and under. All participants receive candy.
JEFF WASHINGTON, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Born in New York City and living much of his life in Philly, Jeff Washington serves up a diverse array of funk, blues, jazz, rock, and R&B with a classic urban feel. jeffwash.com.
EASTER EGG HUNT, 10 a.m., Talbot County Courthouse, Easton. Thousands of eggs will be spread out on the courthouse grounds. Enjoy an appearance by the Easter Bunny.
TIDEWATER CAMERA CLUB, 7 to 9 p.m., United Universalist Church, 7401 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Guest speaker will be Dave Harp, who will offer critiques of photos submitted by members. All are invited. Visit tidewatercameraclub.org for info or for any changes.
LUNCH AND LEARN, noon, St. Michaels Branch Library. Author Sue Ellen Thompson to discuss her new book "Sea Nettles: New & Selected Poems." The poems explore relationships between people of three generations as they evolve over decades. At the center of many of the poems is a transgender child. Free. Last speaker before library closes for renovations.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
BLACK TRAILBLAZERS IN THE NATURAL WORLD, 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., Learn about upcoming initiatives of the MCAAHC and hear from engaging speakers in the heritage and preservation community. Immediately following the public meeting, attendees and participants are invited to an optional walking tour, led by Community Historian Airlee Ringgold Johnson and Scholar-Practitioner Darius Johnson, exploring the rich Black history and culture of Kent County. The tour spans centuries and is an evolving restorative effort the Starr Center for the Study of the American Experience hones in collaboration with local community curators and Washington College students.
VOLUNTEER BIRDWATCH & WALK, 8 to 10 a.m, Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Have fun bird watching for science at Pickering Creek. Bird watchers of all skill levels are encouraged to assist volunteer leaders with bird monitoring along the center's trails during this monthly bird survey. Help collect data that allow the center to track long-term trends on how birds use the center. Over 230 species have been identified at Pickering Creek. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
UKULELE ORCHESTRA OF GREAT BRITAIN, 7 p.m., Avalon Theater, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Formed in 1985, the current ensemble has been playing together for over 20 years, and has become something of a national institution in their homeland. ukuleleorchestra.com.
WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Sassafras NRMA, meadows and forest. Meet at Turners Creek parking area. Enjoy the brisk air of winter on these 3 to 5 mile hikes. Discover the diversity and wildlife of the area. Follow the Caroline County Schools for weather alerts. Bring water, snack, bug spray, hat. Karen.gianninoto@maryland.gov to register or for info.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
AARP CHAPTER MEETING, 12:30 p.m., American Legion Post 91, Cambridge.
BEHIND THE BRUSSEL SPROUTS, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd. Author Lynn Sanches will give refreshing perspective for parents who are uneasy or overwhelmed in their role. RSVP: oxfordcc.org.
COLLAGE AND MIXED MEDIA: ANIMALS AND NATURE, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts, Denton. Class led by award-winning artist Marcie Wolf-Hubbard. Experiment with materials to create unique collages inspired by animals and nature. All skill levels welcome. Dress for mess. $25/class carolinearts.org/events/collage-mixed-media-animals-and-nature-2/.
OKAN, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Taking their name from the word for heart in the Afro-Cuban religion of Santeria, OKAN, is a Juno-Award winning, women-led ensemble that fuses Afro-Cuban roots with jazz, folk, and global rhythms in songs about immigration, courage and love. okanmusica.com.

Learn how this seemingly static environment is ever-changing. Explore the layers of the forest and discover the interdependence of the plants and animals that live there. Take a closer look at tree parts, investigate the life cycle of a tree from seed to soil, and identify some common Maryland trees. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.

 Author/Byline: Angela Price | Section: Calendar

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.VOLUNTEER BIRDWATCH & WALK, 8 to 10 a.m, Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Have fun bird watching for science at Pickering Creek. Bird watchers of all skill levels are encouraged to assist volunteer leaders with bird monitoring along the center's trails during this monthly bird survey. Help collect data that allow the center to track long-term trends on how birds use the center. Over 230 species have been identified at Pickering Creek. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
UKULELE ORCHESTRA OF GREAT BRITAIN, 7 p.m., Avalon Theater, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Formed in 1985, the current ensemble has been playing together for over 20 years, and has become something of a national institution in their homeland. ukuleleorchestra.com.
WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Sassafras NRMA, meadows and forest. Meet at Turners Creek parking area. Enjoy the brisk air of winter on these 3 to 5 mile hikes. Discover the diversity and wildlife of the area. Follow the Caroline County Schools for weather alerts. Bring water, snack, bug spray, hat. Karen.gianninoto@maryland.gov to register or for info.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
AARP CHAPTER MEETING, 12:30 p.m., American Legion Post 91, Cambridge.
BEHIND THE BRUSSEL SPROUTS, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd. Author Lynn Sanches will give refreshing perspective for parents who are uneasy or overwhelmed in their role. RSVP: oxfordcc.org.
COLLAGE AND MIXED MEDIA: ANIMALS AND NATURE, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts, Denton. Class led by award-winning artist Marcie Wolf-Hubbard. Experiment with materials to create unique collages inspired by animals and nature. All skill levels welcome. Dress for mess. $25/class carolinearts.org/events/collage-mixed-media-animals-and-nature-2/.
OKAN, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Taking their name from the word for heart in the Afro-Cuban religion of Santeria, OKAN, is a Juno-Award winning, women-led ensemble that fuses Afro-Cuban roots with jazz, folk, and global rhythms in songs about immigration, courage and love. okanmusica.com.
COLLAGE AND MIXED MEDIA: ANIMALS AND NATURE, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts, Denton. Class led by award-winning artist Marcie Wolf-Hubbard. Experiment with materials to create unique collages inspired by animals and nature. All skill levels welcome. Dress for mess. $25/class carolinearts.org/events/collage-mixed-media-animals-and-nature-2/.
FAMILY FIELD TRIP, 4 to 6 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Uncover the inner workings of the woodland by joining a PCAC educator on a hike through the New Woods Trail. Learn how this seemingly static environment is ever-changing. Explore the layers of the forest and discover the interdependence of the plants and animals that live there. Take a closer look at tree parts, investigate the life cycle of a tree from seed to soil, and identify some common Maryland trees. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
GOUACHE GEMS, 5 to 8 p.m., Studio B Art Gallery, 7b Goldsborough Street, Easton. The unveiling of Charles Newman's gouache exhibit will be a highlight of the downtown Easton First Friday Gallery Walk.
FIRST FRIDAY GALLERY WALK, downtown Easton. On First Friday, the art galleries of downtown Easton extend their hours and invite visitors on a tour of artistic adventure — openings, lectures, book signings and more.
COLLAGE AND MIXED MEDIA: ANIMALS AND NATURE, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts, Denton. Class led by award-winning artist Marcie Wolf-Hubbard. Dress for mess. $25/class carolinearts.org/events/collage-mixed-media-animals-and-nature-2/.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 16 N. Second St., Denton, will open Saturdays. Explore the history and culture of Caroline County through artifacts and exhibits. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055.
AARP MEETING, noon, Church of the Nazarene, Denton. Caroline County AARP Chapter 915 meets at noon, with a covered dish luncheon. "Healthy Body, Healthy Mind" will be presented by Joanne Rue from the Alzheimer's Association. Guests and New Members are welcome. 410-482-6039.
VOLUNTEER GARDEN AND GROUNDS DAY, 9:30 to 11:30 a.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Volunteers take care of a variety of needs at the Center including trail care, invasive plant management, gardening with native plants and other maintenance activities. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.

HUMAN TRAFFICKING 101, noon to 1 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, Cambridge. For All Seasons will sponsor a Lunch & Learn, "Human Trafficking 101." Register: bit.ly/HumanTrafficing101

UNLEASH YOUR INNER CAPTAIN, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd. Interactive presentation on boater safety. Free and open to the public. Refreshments and oysters available for purchase. Space limited. Info: oxfordcc.org.

Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SATURDAY, APRIL 13

HERON PICKLEBALL TOURNAMENT, beginning at 9 a.m., The Gunston School, Centreville. The format will be round-robin or double elimination, depending on the number of registered teams, with men's doubles, women's doubles, and mixed doubles teams playing on Gunston's tennis courts. $40 per player. Registration closes April 8. Register: gunston.org/pickleball24.
SPLENDOR, 5 to 8 p.m., Tilghman Island Volunteer Fire Hall, 5979 Tilghman Island Road. Raw bar of oysters, freshly shucked by local watermen, fine wines, craft beer and light fare from local restaurants. Fundraiser for Tilghman Watermen's Museum. Tickets $40 at twm6031@gmail.com.
ENCAUSTIC & MIXED MEDIA PAINTING, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts. Three-day exploration of encaustics, including painting and collage with wax, fusing, carving and more. No experience necessary. $99.99/3-Day Course. carolinearts.org/events/encaustic-and-mixed-media-painting-2/
SEASONAL NATURE PHOTOGRAPHY, 3 to 5 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Join nature photographer and Pickering's Field Programs Manager Patrick Carney to explore Pickering Creek's diversity of habitats and wildlife through the camera lens. This introductory nature photography class covers wildlife, landscape, macrophotography and more, with an emphasis on ethically photographing the outdoors. The program is suitable for beginners with any type of camera (including cellphones) and level of experience. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.

DESIGNER BAG BINGO, 1 p.m., SSPP High School Hockmeyer Cafeteria. To benefit Post Prom Doors open at noon. Advanced tickets $30, $35 at the door if space allows. Contact: Lisa Baillif 410-822-2275 or lbaillif@ssppeaston.org.

WORSHIP SERVICES
All Faith Episcopal Chapel, 26282 Tunis Mills Road, Easton. Sunday service 9:30 a.m. followed by coffee hour. First and third Sundays, Holy Eucharist; second and fourth Sundays, morning prayer. Fifth Sunday, vicar's choice. Vicar Loretta Collins. Info: allfaithtunismills@gmail.com Website: allfaithchapel.org Facebook: All Faith Chapel.
Anchor Church, 620 Goldsborough Street, Easton. Sunday morning at 10 a.m. Live stream on Facebook or on website. www.anchoreaston.com 410-822-3038
Asbury United Methodist Church, 18 S. Higgins St., Easton. 10 a.m. Sunday worship service. Bible Study 6 p.m. Tuesday. Pastor Reginald Pinkett.
Bethel AME Church, Chestertown. Conference call worship, prayer and study. Dial in: 425-436-6341, access code: 540836. If unable to join the call after several attempts, call the backup number: 520-420-9081 and follow instructions given. Worship service: Sundays 11 a.m. to noon. Christ Episcopal Church, 601 Church Street, Cambridge. Sunday: Holy Eucharist Service at 9 a.m. Wednesday: Holy Eucharist in chapel 9 a.m., second Sunday of Easter. Info: 410-228-3161, Monday through Thursday, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.
Church of the Brethren, 412 S. Harrison St., Easton. Fellowship Hall. 9:30 a.m. classes; 10:45 a.m. worship. Info: 410-822-0475, eastonchurchofthebrethren@gmail.com or eastonbrethren.org.
Church of the King, 7847 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Service, 10 a.m. every Sunday. Info: 410-822-1965.
Denton Church of the Nazarene, 10 a.m. Sunday. Live feed on Facebook — Denton Church of the Nazarene. Pastor Paul Merritt. Info: 410-443-1047.

 April 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Angela Price | Section: Calendar 
 
 2241
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.BLESSING OF THE FLEET, 3 p.m., Dogwood Harbor, Tilghman. Local watermen bring their boats to the harbor, and local clergy will gather together with the watermen's community to pray for a blessing of safety and prosperity for the upcoming crab, clam and fishing seasons. Free to the public.
AARP MEETING, noon, Church of the Nazarene, Denton. Caroline County AARP Chapter 915 meets at noon, with a covered dish luncheon. "Healthy Body, Healthy Mind" will be presented by Joanne Rue from the Alzheimer's Association. Guests and New Members are welcome. 410-482-6039.
VOLUNTEER GARDEN AND GROUNDS DAY, 9:30 to 11:30 a.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Volunteers take care of a variety of needs at the Center including trail care, invasive plant management, gardening with native plants and other maintenance activities. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
WRITE ON, 6:30 to 8 p.m. via Zoom. Join local legend Keith Shaffer for an engaging writing class where you choose your own writing methods and share your stories with fellow enthusiasts. Participation is free. Don't miss out on this opportunity to hone your craft. carolinearts.org/events/write-on-april-9th
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Tuckahoe State Park, Creekside Trail. Meet at Cemetery Road parking area. Enjoy the brisk air of winter on these 3 to 5 mile hikes. Discover the diversity and wildlife of the area. Follow the Caroline County Schools for weather alerts. Bring water, snack, bug spray, hat. Karen.gianninoto@maryland.gov to register or for info.
HUMAN TRAFFICKING 101, noon to 1 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, Cambridge. For All Seasons will sponsor a Lunch & Learn, "Human Trafficking 101." Register: bit.ly/HumanTrafficing101
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
ADVANCED HEALTHCARE PLANNING. 10 a.m. to noon, Talbot Hospice, 586 Cynwood Drive, Easton. Understand your options for Advanced Directive paperwork. Offered every second Thursday of the month. Free and open to the public. Call 410-822-6681 to register.
UNLEASH YOUR INNER CAPTAIN, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd. Interactive presentation on boater safety. Free and open to the public. Refreshments and oysters available for purchase. Space limited. Info: oxfordcc.org.
ENCAUSTIC & MIXED MEDIA PAINTING, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts. Three-day exploration of encaustics, including painting and collage with wax, fusing, carving and more. No experience necessary. $99.99/3-Day Course. carolinearts.org/events/encaustic-and-mixed-media-painting-2/
BIRDS AND BIRDING ON THE EASTERN SHORE, 2:30 to 4 p.m., Easton Peachblossom YMCA or via Zoom. Join Wayne Bell for a unique opportunity to observe the spring migration of songbirds and shorebirds. Two classroom sessions, Thursdays April 11 and June 6, plus seven field trips by car. $70. Register: chesapeakeforum.org
ZACHARY LUCKY, 7 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Zachary Lucky is unapologetically old-school country, armed with a husky, baritone voice. zacharylucky.com.
CHESAPEAKE BAY HERB SOCIETY, 6 p.m., Christ Church Parish Hall, 111 S. Harrison St., Easton. Speaker: Katie Barney on Colonial Herbs and Their Uses. Potluck Dinner Theme: Spring Herbs. 410-763-8843
IMPROV, 7 p.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd. Improv Easton will perform using audience suggestions. Tickets $10 at oxfordcc.org.
ENCAUSTIC & MIXED MEDIA PAINTING, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts. Three-day exploration of encaustics, including painting and collage with wax, fusing, carving and more. No experience necessary. $99.99/3-Day Course. carolinearts.org/events/encaustic-and-mixed-media-painting-2/
CCPS STUDENT ART EXHIBIT, 4 to 6 p.m., The Foundry. Opening reception. Show will showcase of artistic talent from Caroline County's high and middle school students. Admission is free, and artwork will be available for purchase to support budding artists. carolinearts.org/events/ccps-high-school-student-art-exhibition-3/
FAMILY FIELD TRIP, 4:30 to 6 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Join School Year Educator Logan Carey for a relaxing afternoon on Pickering Creek's pier. Bring your family and friends for a chance to catch some tidal water fish. Pickering Creek will supply fishing poles and bait but participants can bring their own lucky fishing supplies. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SATURDAY, APRIL 13
ARTIST RECEPTION, 5 to 8 p.m., Main Street Gallery, 518 Poplar Street, Cambridge. Second Saturday artist reception. Talk at 6 p.m. Free. Light refreshments provided.
HERON PICKLEBALL TOURNAMENT, beginning at 9 a.m., The Gunston School, Centreville. The format will be round-robin or double elimination, depending on the number of registered teams, with men's doubles, women's doubles, and mixed doubles teams playing on Gunston's tennis courts. $40 per player. Registration closes April 8. Register: gunston.org/pickleball24.
SPLENDOR, 5 to 8 p.m., Tilghman Island Volunteer Fire Hall, 5979 Tilghman Island Road. Raw bar of oysters, freshly shucked by local watermen, fine wines, craft beer and light fare from local restaurants. Fundraiser for Tilghman Watermen's Museum. Tickets $40 at twm6031@gmail.com.
ENCAUSTIC & MIXED MEDIA PAINTING, 5:30 to 8 p.m., Caroline County Council of Arts. Three-day exploration of encaustics, including painting and collage with wax, fusing, carving and more. No experience necessary. $99.99/3-Day Course. carolinearts.org/events/encaustic-and-mixed-media-painting-2/
SEASONAL NATURE PHOTOGRAPHY, 3 to 5 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Join nature photographer and Pickering's Field Programs Manager Patrick Carney to explore Pickering Creek's diversity of habitats and wildlife through the camera lens. This introductory nature photography class covers wildlife, landscape, macrophotography and more, with an emphasis on ethically photographing the outdoors. The program is suitable for beginners with any type of camera (including cellphones) and level of experience. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Mill Creek. Early migrants. Depart from Easton Acme Parking Lot at 7 a.m. or meet at Mill Creek at 7:20 a.m. (GPS 38.91 N, 76.069 W). Leader: Jeff Effinger (410-443-5016 or jkeffinger55@gmail.com). Breakfast will follow at Mill Creek.
COMEDIAN ANDY HAYNES, 7 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Andy Haynes is a New York-based writer, stand-up comic, and actor who was raised on salmon and coffee in Seattle. Since starting comedy in 2004, he has performed on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, Conan, Comedy Central Presents, the Pete Holmes show and Comedy Central's Roast Battle. imandyhaynes.com.
SUNDAY, APRIL 14
DESIGNER BAG BINGO, 1 p.m., SSPP High School Hockmeyer Cafeteria. To benefit Post Prom Doors open at noon. Advanced tickets $30, $35 at the door if space allows. Contact: Lisa Baillif 410-822-2275 or lbaillif@ssppeaston.org.
MONDAY, APRIL 15
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
TUESDAY, APRIL 16
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 17

Discover the diversity and wildlife of the area. Follow the Caroline County Schools for weather alerts. Bring water, snack, bug spray, hat. Karen.gianninoto@maryland.gov to register or for info.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
NAVIGATING INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN RETIREMENT, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA at Peachblossom. Embark on a journey towards financial empowerment in your golden years with this comprehensive course tailored for the needs of seniors. Four sessions, April 17, 24, May 1 and 8. $50. Register: chesapeakeforum.org.
NATURE WALK, 9 to 10:30 a.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Join Director Mark Scallion for an off trail walk at the Center. Walks are a great introduction to the center's activities and programs and an opportunity to learn more about what the center has to offer and for the center to learn about the community's interests. This month the group will wander Pickering's dormant soybean fields looking into and learning about bluebird nest boxes as well as exploring some of the field edge habitat and hearing about agriculture at the center. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
THE HEART COLLECTORS, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. From acoustic harmony-led ballads to Bowie-esque sonic soundscapes, Australian four-piece "epic folk" group The Heart Collectors capture the essence of inspiration, honesty of love, and the nature of the cosmos in their music. theheartcollectors.com.

On clawhammer banjo, Allison de Groot has become a significant voice in the North American traditional, Americana and roots music scenes. Collaboration is at the center of Allison's music. Mid-Shore Calendar

 Author/Byline: Angela Price | Section: Calendar 
 
 2763
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.DESIGNER BAG BINGO, 1 p.m., SSPP High School Hockmeyer Cafeteria. To benefit Post Prom Doors open at noon. Advanced tickets $30, $35 at the door if space allows. Contact: Lisa Baillif 410-822-2275 or lbaillif@ssppeaston.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Lynch Preserve, Robins Creek Trail. Meet at end of Tall Tree Lane, Preston. Enjoy the brisk air of winter on these 3 to 5 mile hikes. Discover the diversity and wildlife of the area. Follow the Caroline County Schools for weather alerts. Bring water, snack, bug spray, hat. Karen.gianninoto@maryland.gov to register or for info.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
NAVIGATING INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN RETIREMENT, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA at Peachblossom. Embark on a journey towards financial empowerment in your golden years with this comprehensive course tailored for the needs of seniors. Four sessions, April 17, 24, May 1 and 8. $50. Register: chesapeakeforum.org.
NATURE WALK, 9 to 10:30 a.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Join Director Mark Scallion for an off trail walk at the Center. Walks are a great introduction to the center's activities and programs and an opportunity to learn more about what the center has to offer and for the center to learn about the community's interests. This month the group will wander Pickering's dormant soybean fields looking into and learning about bluebird nest boxes as well as exploring some of the field edge habitat and hearing about agriculture at the center. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
THE HEART COLLECTORS, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. From acoustic harmony-led ballads to Bowie-esque sonic soundscapes, Australian four-piece "epic folk" group The Heart Collectors capture the essence of inspiration, honesty of love, and the nature of the cosmos in their music. theheartcollectors.com.
ALLISON DE GROOT AND TATIANA HARGREAVES, 8 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. On clawhammer banjo, Allison de Groot has become a significant voice in the North American traditional, Americana and roots music scenes. Collaboration is at the center of Allison's music. Her duo with fiddler Tatiana Hargreaves has been described by Bandcamp Daily as "one living, breathing organism."
'VANITIES', 7:30 p.m., 200 Oxford Road, Oxford. Tred Avon Players present a bittersweet comedy is an astute, snapshot-sharp chronicle of the lives of three Texas girls. Tickets: tredavonplayers.org.

'VANITIES', 7:30 p.m., 200 Oxford Road, Oxford. Tred Avon Players present a bittersweet comedy is an astute, snapshot-sharp chronicle of the lives of three Texas girls. Tickets: tredavonplayers.org.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.

title: Pending legislation could decimate newspapers
author: REBECCA SNYDER Maryland Delaware DC Press Association
content:
Pending legislation could decimate newspapers

 April 21, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: REBECCA SNYDER Maryland Delaware DC Press Association | Section: Columns 
 
 726
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The members of the Maryland Delaware DC Press Association (MDDC) are deeply concerned about the potential consequences of HB1258 on local journalism. This bill, which is on the governor's desk now, would upend the longstanding practice of publishing public notices in local newspapers and their associated websites, threatening the vitality of Maryland's communities and the essential role of the press in fostering civic engagement and accountability.We believe that HB 1258 will create a seismic change in the local media landscape that will decimate and potentially prompt the closure of local news outlets.
For decades, local news media has been at the core of their communities, providing critical information, facilitating public discourse, and holding power to account. Although digital formats now supplement print publications, the watchdog role of news media has remained constant. Public notices, a cornerstone of transparency and accountability in government through independent publication and a deep reach into local communities, have been a fundamental part of this ecosystem.
However, HB1258 seeks to centralize estate notices on a government-operated website alone, effectively pulling critical information for creditors and heirs into a subject specific website that requires a user to have reliable internet access and to know where to look for the information. It also will remove a vital revenue stream for local newspapers, jeopardizing the future of journalism in our state.
The ramifications of this legislation extend far beyond the newsroom. By undermining the financial viability of local newspapers, HB1258 threatens the livelihoods of countless journalists, editors, and other media professionals who work tirelessly to keep our communities informed. Moreover, it potentially deprives readers of access to vital information about government proceedings and community events, thereby undermining civic engagement and transparency.
Cataclysmic change sounds dramatic. Local news, however, is on the precipice.
HB 1258 will abandon a system of public notice that has worked well for decades and eliminate a significant number of jobs in Maryland. Local news will go away if communities, governments and others do not support it. Studies show that when a community loses its source of local news, it experiences decreased voter turnout and civic engagement; increased municipal borrowing costs that lead to higher taxes; and decreased transparency among government and business officials, leading to increased waste, fraud, and abuse.
Proponents of HB1258 argue that centralizing public notices on a government website will increase accessibility and efficiency for the state Register of Wills offices. However, this overlooks the reality that many residents, particularly in underserved communities, lack reliable internet access or the technological literacy to navigate online platforms effectively. Many pandemic-era subsidies that made broadband access affordable for Marylanders have been discontinued. Websites are hacked regularly and government is not immune. The print publication is a tangible, permanent record that is archived by publications and libraries, containing the records of an entire community.
Having these notices appear only on a court website diminishes the independence of notice as the agency placing the notice is the one that is publishing the notice. News media is in the business of audience development and dissemination of information, and the traffic to both member websites and the MDDCNews.com aggregated site dwarfs a state website. Having notices in the context of other news and information the public searches for make notices more visible. That will not happen under this bill.
HB1258 was drafted without input from the very stakeholders it stands to impact most profoundly: local newspapers and the communities they serve. The absence of robust debate and meaningful consultation during the legislative process is a disservice to the principles of democracy and good governance. At its core, HB1258 represents a shortsighted approach to policymaking that prioritizes convenience over the public interest. By hastily dismantling a system that has served our communities well for decades, this bill threatens to irreparably harm the fabric of local journalism and the democratic values it upholds.
Our member publications are committed to their communities, employing local journalists and other professionals, occupying office space, contributing to the community and often serving as media sponsors and supporters of community events. All this will be drastically affected if HB 1258 becomes law. Those jobs won't come back; some publications will not be able to stay in business. Sustaining a $1.7 million hit industrywide will surely mean smaller newsrooms and shoestring operations.
Governor Moore, please stand for local news and veto HB 1258.
Rebecca Snyder is the Executive Director of the MDDC Press Association.

IMPROV EASTON DROP-IN NIGHT, 6 to 7:30 p.m., Waterfowl Building, Easton. This free event invites community members of all ages and experience levels to try improv in a supportive and inclusive environment. Reserve a spot: https://tinyurl.com/SparkImprovMay14.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
NATURE, CULTURE AND ADVENTURE, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA or via Zoom. Join other Chesapeake Forum travel enthusiasts on an 18-day adventure to Borneo, the hidden gem of the world, with Bettye Maki as guide. Learn the ins and outs of Borneo — from how to get there to the hidden wonders that await. $20. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org
BEEKEEPING FUNDAMENTALS, 1 to 2:30 p.m., Easton Family YMCA or via Zoom. Immersive two days into the fascinating and rewarding world of beekeeping. Led by local beekeeper, Jim Scoggins, this course will provide insights into the world of hobbyist, sideliner and commercial beekeepers. Two sessions, May 15 and 22, including a visit to a local apiary 7883 Fox Harbour Lane, St. Michaels. $30. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
OXFORD FINE ARTS SHOW GALA, Oxford Community Center. oxfordcc.org/ for more information, tickets, raffle items, gala tickets.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.

HISTORIC WALKING TOURS, 11 a.m. and noon, Talbot Historical Society, 25 S. Washington St., Easton. Third Saturday of the month. Guided tours of Historic Easton, viewing many of the earliest federal buildings where you hear the stories of the transformation and growth as war, fire and railroads impacted the town. Noon tour will focus on the Ebenezer Methodist Episcopal Church, Market House and Bullitt House and discuss how architecture related to spiritual, civic, and daily life. Tour groups are limited to 10 individuals per tour. Advanced reservation required. Tours are free. 410-822-0773.

title: Newark's Memorial Day ceremony, parade set for Sunday
author: Post staff report
content:
Newark's Memorial Day ceremony, parade set for Sunday

 May 16, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Post staff report | Section: News 
 
 214
 Words 

 Read News Document

 On Sunday, Newarkers will have an opportunity to remember and honor the Americans who have died serving their country.The city's annual, two-part Memorial Day commemoration begins at 1 p.m. May 19 with a somber ceremony in front of the University of Delaware's Memorial Hall, which was built in honor of Delawareans who died in World War I. The ceremony will include drills, the presentation of flags, patriotic music and the firing of a cannon.
Following that, the Memorial Day parade will begin at 2 p.m. with marchers representing military units, veterans' groups, schools and community organizations parading down Main Street.
The parade will start at South College Avenue and end at Chapel Street, with participants traveling opposite the usual flow of traffic.
Both events are free and open to the public. Parking is free in city-run lots.
The following roads will have detours and closures in effect beginning at noon and continuing until 3:30 p.m.:
South College Avenue (Park Place to Main Street)
Delaware Avenue (South Main Street to Academy Street)
The following roads will have detours and closures in effect beginning at 1 p.m. and continuing until approximately 3 p.m.:
Main Street (South College Avenue to Chapel Street)
Academy Street (Delaware Avenue to Main Street)
Chapel Street (Delaware Avenue to Main Street)

Mid-Shore Calendar

 May 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Angela Price | Section: Calendar 
 
 3551
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.TINY EXPLORERS EXPEDITION, 4 to 5:30 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Enjoy a story or two to learn more about areas fairies like most and why they can be so hard to find. Then we will try our own hands at building and decorating fairy homes for our elusive and magical friends to live in! We'll then take a short walk and find the perfect spot for our small shelters for fairies and other creatures to enjoy. This program is geared for children ages 2-5 and their adult companion. Sign up at https://pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
'OUTLAW GUNNER', 2 p.m., Talbot County Free Library, 100 W. Dover St., Easton. The Talbot Historical Society will host Joe Walsh at the Talbot County Free Library. Joe will discuss his father, Dr. Harry Walsh, and his book "The Outlaw Gunner," which has recently been republished.
BEEKEEPING FUNDAMENTALS, 1 to 2:30 p.m., Easton Family YMCA or via Zoom. Immersive two days into the fascinating and rewarding world of beekeeping. Led by local beekeeper, Jim Scoggins, this course will provide insights into the world of hobbyist, sideliner and commercial beekeepers. Two sessions, May 15 and 22, including a visit to a local apiary 7883 Fox Harbour Lane, St. Michaels. $30. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
THE TALBOT COUNTY OF FREDERICK DOUGLASS, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA. What can Frederick Douglass, Talbot County's most famous native son, teach us as America continues struggling with racial divisions, the legacy of enslavement, and the quest for a just, free, and embracing society? Join Jeff McGuiness and Lance Morris in a discussion of the eloquent words penned by Douglass himself, juxtaposed against the very landscape that bore witness to the genesis of his quest for a society that transcends differences and dismantles the constancy of hate. Two sessions, May 22 and 29. $30. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
'JOIN OR DIE' SCREENING, 6:30 to 8 p.m., Easton Branch, Talbot County Free Library. A screening of the documentary film "Join or Die" will spark a community conversation about the need for more people of all ages to adopt the practice of being a "joiner" in local civic organizations, clubs and volunteer corps.
BUCKETS OF WARM SPIT, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA or via Zoom. Join Raymond Vergne, M.D., as he turns his focus on the intriguing lives and careers of selected vice presidents from the 20th century. This course is the final chapter in his comprehensive series, offering a deep dive into the often overlooked but fascinating world of Vice Presidents. Three sessions, May 23, 30 and June 6. $40. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
A SENSE OF PLACE, 10 to 11:30 a.m., via Zoom. This course is a discussion and exploration of our perceived special places. It celebrates the individuality and mutability of places and times. Readings will be suggested. Participation is a requirement. Three sessions, May 17, 24 and 31. $40. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington St., Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot St., St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., 16 N. Second St., Denton. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
BOY BAND REVIEW, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover Street, Easton. Boy band tribute show. boybandreview.com.
SPRING FESTIVAL, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., Neck District Volunteer Fire House, 954 Cook's Point Road, Cambridge, 11 miles west of Cambridge. Food, flea market, plant sales, and other vendors. Festival held rain or shine. Free admission. For information or to rent table space call: 410-228-6916 or 410-330-4790.

Registration opens at 7 a.m. on 4th Street near the skate park. The 200-yard Strawberry Dash for children ages 3-5 is at 7:45 a.m. and is free. Info: ridgelylions.org.

THE TALBOT COUNTY OF FREDERICK DOUGLASS, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA. What can Frederick Douglass, Talbot County's most famous native son, teach us as America continues struggling with racial divisions, the legacy of enslavement, and the quest for a just, free, and embracing society? Join Jeff McGuiness and Lance Morris in a discussion of the eloquent words penned by Douglass himself, juxtaposed against the very landscape that bore witness to the genesis of his quest for a society that transcends differences and dismantles the constancy of hate. Two sessions, May 22 and 29. $30. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
PLANNING FOR OUR FUTURE BEFORE IT REACHES US, 1 to 2:30 p.m., Easton Family YMCA or via Zoom. Two sessions, May 29 and June 5. $30. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
OYSTER GARDENING 101, 4:30 to 6 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Oyster gardening provides import nursery habitat as well as filtering the waters of the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries; oyster reefs are a vital part of conserving the Chesapeake Bay. Come learn about a new spat growing program, the challenges these bivalve face, and the research methods we use to analyze the success of oyster nurseries. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
BUCKETS OF WARM SPIT, 10 to 11:30 a.m., Easton Family YMCA or via Zoom. This course is the final chapter in his comprehensive series, offering a deep dive into the often overlooked but fascinating world of Vice Presidents. Three sessions, May 23, 30 and June 6. $40. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.
NATURE AT NIGHT HIKE, 8:30 to 10:30 p.m., Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Explore Pickering Creek's Farm-to-Bay Loop at night and use special UV flashlights to reveal nocturnal wildlife and unique plants and fungi not usually visible to the human eye. By the main parking lot, stop by a mothing station with the opportunity to see Luna moths and other impressive early summer species. Sign up at pickeringcreek.org/programs/upcoming-programs/.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
A SENSE OF PLACE, 10 to 11:30 a.m., via Zoom. This course is a discussion and exploration of our perceived special places. It celebrates the individuality and mutability of places and times. Readings will be suggested. Participation is a requirement. Three sessions, May 17, 24 and 31. $40. To register, visit chesapeakeforum.org.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
CARPOOL, 8 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover Street, Easton. Carpool is a tribute band that recreates the sound, feel, look and vibe that made the Cars world famous. carpooltributeband.com.
RIDGELY TRAIN STATION, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Open the first Saturdays of the month through September. The Ridgely Historical Society will guide visitors through the history of the town. Info: 410-991-8225.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.

Following the ceremony, attendees are invited to enjoy a complimentary slice of authentic Roman-style pizza at nearby Bluepoint Hospitality eatery, Roma Alla Pala.

title: Gov. Wes Moore, a friend of Maryland newspapers
author: JIM JOHNSON jjohnson@chespub.com
content:
Gov. Wes Moore, a friend of Maryland newspapers

 June 2, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: JIM JOHNSON jjohnson@chespub.com | Section: Columns 
 
 669
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Gov. Wes Moore recently vetoed a Maryland House bill that would have been crippling to state newspapers."There is also a vital public interest in ensuring the existence of thriving independent local media," Moore wrote in his veto letter. "In fact, democracy can not function effectively in the absence of a free press that provides objective information to the citizenry about crucial events in government and in our communities."
The legislation, House Bill 1258, would have taken public notices regarding estate administration, currently published in newspapers, and allowed them to be posted on a state-operated website. The cost to state newspapers was estimated at $1.7 million. If the legislation had taken effect Oct. 1, there is no doubt that by the dawn of the new year would have seen significantly fewer newspaper journalists working in Maryland.
In his veto letter, Moore noted public notice advertising "have helped sustain much of the local print media in Maryland' as advertising dollars have dried up and the media industry has consolidated and downsized.
Moore had some tough words for the newspaper industry, whose lobbying group did not engage in hearings, testimony or conversations about the bill. That was a serious oversight by the Maryland-Delaware-D.C. Press Association, an oversight that could have had disastrous effects on the newspapers that pay dues for the association to represent them in legislative discussions. Moore, without a doubt, bailed out newspapers with his veto.
Sticking on the theme of state politics, the race to replace U.S. Sen. Ben Cardin started hot and continues to sizzle. Democrat Cardin decided not to seek reelection, which set off a ferocious primary battle between Congressman David Throne and Prince George's County Executive Angela Alsobrooks. Despite being outspent 9-1 by Trone who dumped tens of millions of his own money into his campaign, Alsobrooks easily won the nomination.
Alsobrooks will face former Gov. Larry Hogan in November. Hogan is hoping to appeal to Democrats to cross over and vote for him as they did when he was elected governor. Hogan started the morning after the primary, releasing a video showing prominent Democrats praising him during his days when he was governor. The video featured clips of Wes Moore, Barack Obama, Bill Clinton and even Angela Alsobrooks. The message: Hogan has a history of working across the aisle with Democrats.
That message was on display last week when Hogan visited Cambridge where he picked up a couple of endorsements from Dorchester County Councilman Ricky Travers, a Democrat, and County Council Vice President Mike Detmer, a Republican.
"This is especially nice because it's a bipartisan thing," Hogan told Star Democrat reporter Maggie Trovato. "I've always been somebody that reaches across the aisle and tries to find consensus and tries to get things done with Republicans and Democrats working together."
For Travers, it's not about Democrat or Republican when it comes to the Senate seat.
"It's about who's the best person for the job," he said in an interview. "That's the bottom line."
Hogan drew fire from his own party after he posted on Twitter prior to a New York jury finding former President Donald Trump guilty on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in connection with hush-money payments during the 2016 campaign to cover up an affair with adult film actress, Stormy Daniels.
"Regardless of the result, I urge all Americans to respect the verdict and the legal process," he posted on X, formerly Twitter. "… We must reaffirm what has made this nation great: the rule of law."
That drew criticism from Republicans.
"You just ended your campaign," Chris LaCivita, a senior adviser to Trump's presidential campaign, responded minutes later.
Buckle your seatbelts, we are in for a wild ride with this campaign.
Congratulations to Talbot County Council member Keasha Haythe who became a grandmother on March 17 with the birth of Declan James Alexander Haythe. Declan is the son of Marcus Leandre Haythe Jr. and Beatrice Anne Gorman. Keasha Haythe beams when she talks about her grandson.
Jim Johnson is the executive editor of the Star Democrat.

 DENTON — The next Caroline County Commission meeting will be held 9 a.m. Tuesday, June 25, in Room 106 of the Caroline County Courthouse, located at 109 Market Street in Denton.Meetings are held 9 a.m. Tuesdays except the fifth Tuesday of the month, unless announced otherwise. title: Rotary Clubs unite for Men's Clothing Drive to empower communities
author: Staff Writer
content:
Rotary Clubs unite for Men's Clothing Drive to empower communities

 June 12, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Local News 
 
 273
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Rotary Club of Kent Island, in collaboration with Rotary Clubs in Denton, Centerville, Chestertown and Easton, alongside partners including the Queen Anne's County Chamber of Commerce, Tides of Grace and Grasonville Community Center, announced a transformative initiative aimed at making a difference in the lives of men in need.From June 1 to July 31, these organizations will join forces to conduct a men's clothing drive to support the work of Sharp Dressed Men.
The drive seeks donations of dry-cleaned suits, sports coats, slacks, ties, laundered dress shirts, dress shoes and belts. Additionally, clothing that has not been laundered or dry cleaned will be accepted, with arrangements made to have items cleaned at local cleaners and laundries.
Sharp Dressed Men, renowned for its commitment to empowering individuals through professional attire, will be hosting an event at the Grasonville Community Center on Aug. 2. The clothing collected during the drive will directly support this event, providing men with the attire and confidence they need to pursue employment opportunities and achieve self-sufficiency.
"This collaborative effort embodies the spirit of community and compassion," said Candi Cook, president of the Rotary Club of Kent Island. "By coming together with our fellow Rotarians and esteemed partners, we have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact on the lives of men in our communities, helping them take strides toward a brighter future."
Individuals interested in supporting this initiative or seeking further information are encouraged to reach out via email at rotaryofkentisland@gmail.com.
Drop Off Locations:
Lundberg Builders, 314 Main St., Stevensville.Edward Jones, 102 St. Claire Place, Stevensville.Queen Anne's County Library locations: Kent Island Branch, 200 Library Circle, Stevensville; Centreville Branch, 121 S. Commerce St., Centreville.

title: Women to Watch Summer Speaker Series — REinspire: Conversations to Find Your Purpose and Passion
author: Staff Writer
content:
Women to Watch Summer Speaker Series — REinspire: Conversations to Find Your Purpose and Passion

 June 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Events 
 
 269
 Words 

 Read News Document

 WYE MILLS — Since 2020, APG Media of Chesapeake has recognized women in Mid-Shore communities with the annual Women to Watch program.In 2024, community members nominated over 350 women across the Mid-Shore as Women to Watch. To continue the momentum and enthusiasm these communities have for the Women to Watch Program, APG will present the second annual Summer Speaker Series, "REinspire: Conversations to Find Your Passion and Purpose."
Each event will include networking with other community leaders, a light breakfast from a local restaurant, a discussion panel from Women to Watch leaders and, new this year, small group mentoring.
The first series event will take place from 8 to 10 a.m., Thursday, June 20, at Chesapeake College, HPAC Room 141, in Wye Mills.
Panelists will include: Shelly Gross-Wade, principal consultant and CEO of Bay Crossing Consulting; Kim Montooth, assistant vice president of M&T Bank; Shawna D. Payne, MBA, CHC, founder and coach of The BE Academy; and Liz Verhelle, financial advisor of Edward Jones; moderated by Carrie-Ann Barrow, executive coach, owner, author of Scaling Strategies.
During the panel discussion, attendees will learn from the speakers as they share personal and professional stories from their career and development. Following this engaging dialogue, participants will break into small groups to speak panelists and fellow attendees about their own personal and professional challenges.
The discussions and small group mentoring sessions are designed to inspire, enrich and empower attendees as community leaders. Tickets are $30.
More information on the event, panelists and the series can be found on at Women to Watch apgchesapeake.com/summer-speaker-series-2024 or by contacting Kristi English, director of Marketing and Events for APG Media, at kenglish@chespub.com.

title: UPDATED US 301 median crossover to close
author: STAFF REPORT
content:
UPDATED US 301 median crossover to close

 July 13, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: STAFF REPORT | Section: Local News 
 
 200
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CHURCH HILL — The Maryland State Highway Administration will close the MD 405 (Price Station Road) median crossover at US 301 (Blue Star Memorial Highway) in Queen Anne's County beginning Monday, July 29. The closure restricts all movements through the median and will remain in effect until further notice.According to Charlie Gischlar, deputy director with the SHA Office of Communications, between January 2019 and December 2023, 76 crashes were reported at this location. Most of those crashes (62) occurred along southbound US 301 and were attributed to driver inattention or failure to yield.
The State Highway Administration has implemented numerous safety-driven changes in the 500-foot wide median over the past several years including restriping/realignment, audible pavement "rumble strip" warnings and additional signage. These measures have not significantly reduced crash rates, Rager reported.
Drivers are encouraged to plan alternate routes suitable for their travel and vehicle type. Nearby US 301 median crossovers are available at MD 19 (Roberts Station Road, two miles north) and Hayden Clark Road, 1.7 miles south.
A list of all major State Highway Administration projects, can be found by visiting the Project Portal at https://mdot-sha-project-portal-maryland.hub.arcgis.com or the homepage at roads.maryland.gov.
For a look at real-time traffic conditions, go to md511.maryland.gov.

 The proposed construction to replace the Leeds Creek Bridge located in the Village of Tunis Mills is expected to move forward, according to the Talbot County Department of Public Works.In a press release, the county said that to provide comprehensive information about the bridge replacement project, the department will host a public information meeting on Wednesday, Aug. 7, from 5:30 to 7:30 p.m. at St. Stephens AME Church, located at 9467 Unionville Road in Easton.
The meeting will feature detailed presentations on the proposed bridge replacement, including project improvement displays for public review, the release said. County staff and project consultants will be on hand to address any questions, comments or concerns from attendees.
"This project underscores Talbot County's commitment to maintaining and enhancing its infrastructure for the safety and benefit of all residents," the release read. "A full road closure of a portion of Tunis Mills Road will be required during the construction period."
Discussions on the project started nearly 20 years ago when the county did a preliminary engineering report to look into replacing the bridge. In the late 2010s, the previous county council appropriated $1.8 million to the replacement project.
The county then went to the State Highway Administration to look into utilizing federal aid funding to replace the bridge. SHA provided an 80% grant, with 20% of local funding applied to the project. According to the county's website, total costs for the project could be up to $6 million.
Proposed changes to the old wooden bridge include adding an additional two feet of clearance, replacing timber piles with steel piles, adding a wooden laminated deck that can be paved over, widening the bridge slightly for walkers and improving a ramp and unloading platform. Several other bridges in the county have undergone similar laminated deck replacement.
According to the county's website the design phase of the replacement project is almost complete, and an advertisement for construction is expected to go out in the late fall or early winter.
For those unable to attend the meeting Aug. 7, the Public Works is taking inquiries or feedback directly at clarke@talbotcountymd.gov, mmertaugh@talbotcountymd.gov or 410-770-8170.

title: Welcome to Saturday delivery of the Star Democrat
author: JIM JOHNSON Executive Editor
content:
Welcome to Saturday delivery of the Star Democrat

 August 2, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: JIM JOHNSON Executive Editor | Section: Local News 
 
 218
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Welcome to the first weekend edition of the Star Democrat delivered on Saturday.Whether your newspaper is delivered to your driveway or to your mailbox or you view the online e-edition, it was delivered on Saturday instead of Sunday.
This is the first day of the Saturday delivery of the weekend edition. We are making the change because a growing number of our readers have the print edition delivered by the U.S. Postal Service. Saturday distribution means those readers will get the newspaper on the same day as readers who have carrier delivery. Before today, those customers had to wait until Monday — and sometimes later — to receive their Sunday newspaper.
I want to thank all of our colleagues who have worked to make this change as smooth as possible. There was much to be done. Everybody throughout the Star Democrat organization worked to make sure all of those changes were made. Also a big thanks to news and advertising advisory panels that reviewed our plans and made recommendations on the best way to make this happen.
We hope you will be happy with our new weekend edition. We want to hear from you about your thoughts on the new delivery schedule. Please reach out to Executive Editor Jim Johnson at jjohnson@chespub.com. or Assistant General Manager Chad Campbell at ccampbell@chespub.com.

 August 24, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2778
 Words 

 Read News Document

Hilarity ensues in the small town of Eden Falls, Georgia, as a group of spirited women decide to transform their lives at SPA-DEE-DAH!, an abandoned church-turned-day-spa. Presented by the Tred Avon Players. Tickets: https://ci.ovationtix.com/35824/production/1181081.

World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.

WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
THURSDAY, SEPT. 12
OXFORD LAB UPDATE, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Talk is in partnership with Oxford Museum and is in conjunction with the Museum's Oxford Lab exhibit. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
ADVANCED HEALTHCARE PLANNING. 10 a.m. to noon, Talbot Hospice, 586 Cynwood Drive, Easton. Understand your options for Advanced Directive paperwork. Offered every second Thursday of the month. Free and open to the public. Call 410-822-6681 to register.
FRIDAY, SEPT. 13
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SHOE DRIVE, Cordova Firehouse. Collection of gently used shoes for the Volunteer Fire Department Ladies Auxiliary . Shoes can be dropped off at the Cordova Firehouse until Sept. 13. This drive is to raise funds for the firehouse needs.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 14
EXETER HOUSE, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., 408 Old Denton Road, Federalsburg. Exeter is one of the oldest remaining structures in southern Caroline County. Many of its early residents were millers who worked in the grist mill across the road on the Marshyhope Creek. Federalsburg Historical Society plans to hold an open house. Docents will be available. Admission is free, but donations are gratefully accepted.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
SHOW US YOUR WHEELS!, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Rock Hall Yacht Club, 22759 McKinleyville Rd., Rock Hall. Car show. Food, bar, vendors, crafts, music. Register by Sept. 6: carshowpro.com/events/register/1732.
ROAD RALLY, 8 a.m., Oxford Community Center. Classic and Vintage cars are invited to the fifth annual Road Rally. Special interest modern cars will be accepted. Over 70 miles of scenic roads with a minimum of traffic, includes breakfast and lunch for the driver and one passenger at a most beautiful destination. $160 per car. Info: oxfordcc.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
SUNDAY, SEPT. 15
JOUST, 1 p.m., Tuckahoe Equestrian Center, 619 Crouse Mill Road, Queen Anne. Jousting is Maryland's official state sport. Open to the public to watch. Please bring your own chairs. Info: 410-479-0565.
MONDAY, SEPT. 16
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
TUESDAY, SEPT. 17
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
