WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
'AGING IN PLACE', 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Speaker Maggie Black. An informative health presentation about "Aging in Place" — setting the stage with discussions about what is typical aging and when one needs to be concerned. Free. Bring your lunch. Limited seating. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
THURSDAY, SEPT. 19
THIRD THURSDAY, 5 to 7 p.m., downtown Denton. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
COMMUNITY TALK, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Lifetime Wells International President and Co-founder David Powell will talk about Project Africa. This is brought to you by Oxford's Dick and Zoe Schramm. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
FRIDAY, SEPT. 20
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 21
HISTORIC WALKING TOURS, 11 a.m. and noon, Talbot Historical Society, 25 S. Washington St., Easton. Third Saturday of the month. Guided tours of Historic Easton, viewing many of the earliest federal buildings where you hear the stories of the transformation and growth as war, fire and railroads impacted the town. Noon tour will focus on the Ebenezer Methodist Episcopal Church, Market House and Bullitt House and discuss how architecture related to spiritual, civic, and daily life. Tour groups are limited to 10 individuals per tour. Advanced reservation required. Tours are free. 410-822-0773.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., 16 N. Second St., Denton. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
DANCING WITH THE STARS, 7 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Local celebrities participate in a dance competition. This is a fundraiser in partnership with Chesapeake Multicultural Resource Center. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. Tickets cost $25 per person and includes dinner, one cocktail and dancing after the competition. Tickets and voting: oxfordcc.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY, SEPT. 23
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
TUESDAY, SEPT. 24
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.

Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
THURSDAY, SEPT. 26
COMMUNITY TALK, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Dan Small, the associate director of natural land stewardship at the Center for Environment and Society at Washington College, will talk about the plans for expanding the Oxford Conservation Park and how it fits with the goals of the Natural Lands Project. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
FRIDAY, SEPT. 27
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 28
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
SUNDAY, SEPT. 29
JOUSTING CHAMPIONSHIP, 1 p.m., Tuckahoe Equestrian Center, 619 Crouse Mill Road, Queen Anne. Jousting is Maryland's official state sport. Open to the public to watch. Please bring your own chairs. Info: 410-310-7945.
THURSDAY, OCT. 10
ADVANCED HEALTHCARE PLANNING. 10 a.m. to noon, Talbot Hospice, 586 Cynwood Drive, Easton. Understand your options for Advanced Directive paperwork. Offered every second Thursday of the month. Free and open to the public. Call 410-822-6681 to register.

Mid-Shore Calendar

 August 30, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2343
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
TRIO MUSIC: APART AND TOGETHER, Stoltz Listening Room, Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton, 7 p.m. Nevin Dawson (viola, looper pedal), Quinn Parsley (classical guitar), and Ashley Watkins (flute) will play music from a wide variety of time periods and styles.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., 16 N. Second St., Denton. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
CHARITY BOAT AUCTION, 11 a.m., Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum, 213 N. Talbot St., St. Michaels. Dozens of boats and watercraft, ranging in size and performance, will be auctioned off to the highest bidders. New this year, there will be reserves on several top-quality vessels, while the rest will be offered with no minimum. For questions about auction or inventory: boatdonation@cbmm.org or 410-310-5103.
THE FABULOUS HUBCAPS!, 7 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Tickets $35 at oxfordcc.org/product/the-fabulous-hubcaps/. Cash bar.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
RHAPSODY IN BLUE REVISITED, Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton, 7 p.m. Dominick Farinacci and his band will present a new interpretation of Gershwin's iconic work.
CAROLINE COUNTY JOUST, 1 p.m., Caroline County 4-H Park, 8230 Detour Road, Denton. Eastern Shore Jousting Association will be holding their Caroline County Joust. Jousting is Maryland's official state sport. Open to the public to watch. Please bring your own chairs. Info: 410-479-0565.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Hurlock Turf Farm and WWTP Shorebirds. Depart from Easton Acme parking lot at 6:30 a.m. Leader: Jeff Effinger (410-443-5016 or jkeffinger55@gmail.com).
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Pickering Creek eBird Monitoring. Meet at Pickering Creek Audubon Center parking area at 8 a.m. (GPS 38.86 N, 76.124 W). Leader: Susie Pratt (410-924-4925 or prattsuzzie@gmail.com).
AARP CHAPTER MEETING, 1:30 p.m., American Legion Post 91, Cambridge.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com
FRIDAY, SEPT. 6
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
DINNER AND A MOVIE, 6 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Indian cuisine created Roopa and Probal Gupta with Larry Paz. "The Great Exotic Marigold Hotel" is the movie. Dinner and movie is $25 and starts at 6 p.m.; movie only is free and starts at 7 p.m. Limited seating. Purchase tickets at oxfordcc.org.
JAKE SHIMABUKURO, Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton, 7 p.m. With his mother as his first teacher of the instrument, Shimabukuro embraced a deep love and respect for the ukulele and has explored new and unexpected ways to push the boundaries of what was possible on the humble four-strings.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 7
RAFT UP CONCERT, 3 to 6 p.m., Shaw Bay near the mouth of the Wye River. Boat in to Shaw Bay near the mouth of the Wye River and then join the floating raft up on your dinghy, paddle board, or kayak to enjoy a front row seat to the live concert. Info: shorerivers.org/events.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
MUSEUM OF RURAL LIFE, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., 16 N. Second St., Denton. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
CARS AND COFFEE, 8:30 a.m., Oxford Community Center. Free. Sponsored by Prestige Auto Vault, Eat Sprout & Doc's Sunset Grille.
FALL COOKING FESTIVAL, Old Wye Mill, 900 Wye Mills Rd, Wye Mills. Carolyn Graf and D'Nise Hefner are returning to the Mill, and they are bringing friends who will help them prepare selected recipes from the Wye Miller's Grind Cookbook in Dutch ovens. Their creations will feature flours ground at the mill.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.

MONDAY, SEPT. 9
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
TUESDAY, SEPT. 10
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WEDNESDAY, SEPT. 11
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
THURSDAY, SEPT. 12
OXFORD LAB UPDATE, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Talk is in partnership with Oxford Museum and is in conjunction with the Museum's Oxford Lab exhibit. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
ADVANCED HEALTHCARE PLANNING. 10 a.m. to noon, Talbot Hospice, 586 Cynwood Drive, Easton. Understand your options for Advanced Directive paperwork. Offered every second Thursday of the month. Free and open to the public. Call 410-822-6681 to register.
FRIDAY, SEPT. 13
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SHOE DRIVE, Cordova Firehouse. Collection of gently used shoes for the Volunteer Fire Department Ladies Auxiliary . Shoes can be dropped off at the Cordova Firehouse until Sept. 13. This drive is to raise funds for the firehouse needs.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 14
EXETER HOUSE, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., 408 Old Denton Road, Federalsburg. Exeter is one of the oldest remaining structures in southern Caroline County. Many of its early residents were millers who worked in the grist mill across the road on the Marshyhope Creek. Federalsburg Historical Society plans to hold an open house. Docents will be available. Admission is free, but donations are gratefully accepted.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
SHOW US YOUR WHEELS!, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Rock Hall Yacht Club, 22759 McKinleyville Rd., Rock Hall. Car show. Food, bar, vendors, crafts, music. Register by Sept. 6: carshowpro.com/events/register/1732.
ROAD RALLY, 8 a.m., Oxford Community Center. Classic and Vintage cars are invited to the fifth annual Road Rally. Special interest modern cars will be accepted. Over 70 miles of scenic roads with a minimum of traffic, includes breakfast and lunch for the driver and one passenger at a most beautiful destination. $160 per car. Info: oxfordcc.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
RABIES VACCINATION CLINIC, 215 Bay Street, Easton, 1 to 3 p.m. $6 per animal (cash or check). Eligible animals: Dogs, cats and ferrets. Pets must be at least 12 weeks old. To pre-register, call 410-770-6880.

JOUST, 1 p.m., Tuckahoe Equestrian Center, 619 Crouse Mill Road, Queen Anne. Jousting is Maryland's official state sport. Open to the public to watch. Please bring your own chairs. Info: 410-479-0565.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.

RSVP at oxfordcc.org.

COMMUNITY TALK, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Lifetime Wells International President and Co-founder David Powell will talk about Project Africa. This is brought to you by Oxford's Dick and Zoe Schramm. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.

FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 21
HISTORIC WALKING TOURS, 11 a.m. and noon, Talbot Historical Society, 25 S. Washington St., Easton. Third Saturday of the month. Guided tours of Historic Easton, viewing many of the earliest federal buildings where you hear the stories of the transformation and growth as war, fire and railroads impacted the town. Doors open at 6:30 p.m. Tickets cost $25 per person and includes dinner, one cocktail and dancing after the competition. Tickets and voting: oxfordcc.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.

Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.

title: Mid-Shore Calendar
author: Staff Writer
content:
Mid-Shore Calendar

 September 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2891
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.REMEMBRANCE CEREMONY, 8:30 a.m., Corner of West and Dover streets, downtown Easton. Ceremony will recognize the courage of first responders, military personnel, and ordinary citizens who acted selflessly in the face of immense danger.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
GRANTS AND GOVERNMENT CONTRACTING FOR DAY CARE CENTERS, 6 to 7 p.m., online webinar. Instructor: Dr. Amy Stewart, owner of The Night Watch Child Care Center. Learning the requirements of obtaining government contracting will open a whole new world of opportunities for your daycare business. Register: womensbusinesscenteratmarylandcapitalenterprises.org/classes/2398/.
BE A LIFELINE, 6:30 to 8 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 49 E. Dover St., Easton. Jeff Thompson, a research psychologist at Columbia University Medical Center and retired NYPD detective, will: discuss key risk factors and warning signs, clarify and separate common myths from factsProvide practical tips for everyone, regardless of background. Register: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/be-a-lifeline-recognizing-and-responding-to-those-at-risk-of-suicide-tickets.
OXFORD LAB UPDATE, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Talk is in partnership with Oxford Museum and is in conjunction with the Museum's Oxford Lab exhibit. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
ADVANCED HEALTHCARE PLANNING, 10 a.m. to noon, Talbot Hospice, 586 Cynwood Drive, Easton. Understand your options for Advanced Directive paperwork. Offered every second Thursday of the month. Free and open to the public. Call 410-822-6681 to register.
BIRDING AND BOATING THE HARRIET TUBMAN BYWAY, 2 to 6 p.m., Linchester Mill, Preston. Join Harriet Tubman Tours and Delmarva Birding Weekends as they go birding along the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway. During the guided, self-driven tour, attendees 'learn about the many daring escapes led by the famed freedom seeker and human rights activist know as "The Moses of Her People." Contact dmvbirds@gmail.com to reserve your space.
CALEB STINE, 7 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Caleb Stine is a singer-songwriter, multi-instrumentalist, and visual artist. Though he makes his living as a folk musician, Stine wouldn't call what he does a job; he considers it a calling.
CAMBRIDGE FARMERS MARKET, 3 to 6 p.m., Long Wharf, High and Water Streets, Cambridge. Find local produce, meats, cheeses, crafts, and more at the weekly, waterfront Cambridge Farmers Market. Info: office@downtowncambridge.org.
DCHS YARD SALE, 4 to 6 p.m., Dorchester County Historical Society, 1003 Greenway Dr., Cambridge. Historical society members only.
THURSDAY DECK PARTY, 5 to 7 p.m., Blue Point Provision Co., Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay, 100 Heron Blvd., Cambridge. Music, delicious dining specials, and drink specials including our signature Choptank Crush cocktail.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SHOE DRIVE, Cordova Firehouse. Collection of gently used shoes for the Volunteer Fire Department Ladies Auxiliary . Shoes can be dropped off at the Cordova Firehouse until Sept. 13. This drive is to raise funds for the firehouse needs.
JAMES MCMURTY WITH BETTYSOO, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. After 20 years in rock, folk, and Americana, McMurtry's most recent effort, "The Horses and the Hounds" (2021), backs personal narratives with effortless elegance and endless energy. He will be joined on the Avalon stage by Betty Soo, a world-class vocalist.
DCHS YARD SALE, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Dorchester County Historical Society, 1003 Greenway Dr., Cambridge. Open to the public.
EXETER HOUSE, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., 408 Old Denton Road, Federalsburg. Exeter is one of the oldest remaining structures in southern Caroline County. Many of its early residents were millers who worked in the grist mill across the road on the Marshyhope Creek. Federalsburg Historical Society plans to hold an open house. Docents will be available. Admission is free, but donations are gratefully accepted.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
SHOW US YOUR WHEELS!, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Rock Hall Yacht Club, 22759 McKinleyville Rd., Rock Hall. Car show. Food, bar, vendors, crafts, music. Register by Sept. 6: carshowpro.com/events/register/1732.
ROAD RALLY, 8 a.m., Oxford Community Center. Classic and Vintage cars are invited to the fifth annual Road Rally. Special interest modern cars will be accepted. Over 70 miles of scenic roads with a minimum of traffic, includes breakfast and lunch for the driver and one passenger at a most beautiful destination. $160 per car. Info: oxfordcc.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
RABIES VACCINATION CLINIC, 215 Bay Street, Easton, 1 to 3 p.m. $6 per animal (cash or check). Eligible animals: Dogs, cats and ferrets. Pets must be at least 12 weeks old. To pre-register, call 410-770-6880.
CONCERT IN THE PARK, 4 to 7 p.m., James T. Wright Memorial Park, Preston. Home Brew is a trio of local musicians with two guitars, good vocals and tight harmonies. They play an eclectic selection of acoustic music to please all ages. Free to attend with treats available from Jaha Ice.
COMEDY @ THE STOLTZ WITH JARED STERN, 7 p.m. and 9:30 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Headliner Jared Stern has been making complete strangers laugh at him for 20 years and counting. The Stoltz show, which also features Baltimore comic Jim Meyer, is hosted by Ryan Finch.
DCHS YARD SALE, 7 a.m. to 4 p.m., Dorchester County Historical Society, 1003 Greenway Dr., Cambridge. Open to the public.
SECOND SATURDAY BOOK SALE, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Dorchester County Public Library, Cambridge Branch, 303 Gay St., Cambridge. Thousands of books are available, both hardback and paperback, at $1 and $.50 respectively.
SECOND SATURDAY, 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., downtown Cambridge. Monthly celebration in downtown Cambridge features free art gallery receptions, as well as specials in the independently owned shops and great dining. Shops and galleries are open all day and into the evening.
NATIVE AMERICAN FESTIVAL, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., Under the water tower ball field, Vienna. Drumming, singing, dancing, traditional music, storytelling, educational exhibits and demonstrations, arts, crafts, and jewelry vendors, food, and a silent auction. Tickets $7 at the gate, children under 4 free. Info: 410-228-0216, turtletracks.org.
FINANCIAL LITERACY WORKSHOP, 10 a.m. to noon, Eastern Shore Innovation Center, 104 Tech Park Dr., Suite 41, Cambridge. Free. Informative session is designed to provide you with essential financial knowledge and strategies. This workshop is perfect for anyone looking to improve their financial health and make well-informed decisions. Register: 443-521-6274, nealwfg2020@gmail.com.
SAIL ON SKIPJACK NATHAN, 1 to 3 p.m., Long Wharf, Cambridge. Sails are unique depending on wind, weather, captain and crew. Advance reservations are recommended and accepted at skipjack-nathan.org until midnight of the day before the sail.
JOUST, 1 p.m., Tuckahoe Equestrian Center, 619 Crouse Mill Road, Queen Anne. Jousting is Maryland's official state sport. Open to the public to watch. Please bring your own chairs. Info: 410-479-0565.
GUIDED BIRDING TOURS AT BLACKWATER NWR, 8 a.m. to noon, Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge, 2145 Key Wallace Dr., Cambridge. No fee or registration required. Info: 410-228-2677 or www.fws.gov/refuge/Blackwater.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Tilghman Island- Blackwalnut Point. Waterfowl, gulls, terns and passerines. Meet at Blackwalnut parking area in Tilghman at 7 a.m. (GPS 38.6833 N, 76.3437 W) Leaders: Janet MacDonald (973-903-4208 or janetmacdonald68@gmail.com) and Bobbie Wells (410-924-2568 or wellsbk@yahoo.com).
MONDAY, SEPT. 16
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
TUESDAY, SEPT. 17
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WEDNESDAY, SEPT. 18
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
'AGING IN PLACE', 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Speaker Maggie Black. An informative health presentation about "Aging in Place" — setting the stage with discussions about what is typical aging and when one needs to be concerned. Free. Bring your lunch. Limited seating. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
'DANCING IN COLOR,' 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. In this collaboration between the folk-pop band Bombadil and contemporary dancer Madison Rivis, Rivis has choreographed movements for herself and the band using their latest album "In Color" as inspiration. Bombadil in turn taught Rivis how to play and sing the songs.
THURSDAY, SEPT. 19
THIRD THURSDAY, 5 to 7 p.m., downtown Denton. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
COMMUNITY TALK, 5:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Lifetime Wells International President and Co-founder David Powell will talk about Project Africa. This is brought to you by Oxford's Dick and Zoe Schramm. Free. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
WINE EDUCATION SERIES, 6 to 8 p.m., The Ebenezer Theater at Prager Family Center for the Arts, 17 S. Washington St., Easton. Presentation and Tasting; Questions & Answers; Wine Market to shop glassware, books, accessories and art. Pre-orders available for wine & cheese. Led by Wardroom Wine Director, Anthony Austin, guests will sample five wines as they learn about regional details.
CAMBRIDGE FARMERS MARKET, 3 to 6 p.m., Long Wharf, High and Water Streets, Cambridge. Find local produce, meats, cheeses, crafts, and more at the weekly, waterfront Cambridge Farmers Market. Info: office@downtowncambridge.org.
THURSDAY DECK PARTY, 5 to 7 p.m., Blue Point Provision Co., Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay, 100 Heron Blvd., Cambridge. Music, delicious dining specials, and drink specials including our signature Choptank Crush cocktail.
FOUR ELEVEN KITCHEN RIBBON CUTTING, 5:30 to 7 p.m., 411 Kitchen, The Packing House, 411A Dorchester Ave., Cambridge. Business after hours featuring ribbon cutting. Register: info@dorchesterchamber.org or 410-228-3575.
FRIDAY, SEPT. 20
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
SATURDAY, SEPT. 21
HISTORIC WALKING TOURS, 11 a.m. and noon, Talbot Historical Society, 25 S. Washington St., Easton. Third Saturday of the month. Guided tours of Historic Easton, viewing many of the earliest federal buildings where you hear the stories of the transformation and growth as war, fire and railroads impacted the town. Noon tour will focus on the Ebenezer Methodist Episcopal Church, Market House and Bullitt House and discuss how architecture related to spiritual, civic, and daily life. Asbury United Methodist Church, 18 S. Higgins St., Easton. In front of the church, a Blessing Box containing canned goods for people in need in the community. Sponsored by Asbury United Methodist Women.

Events around Caroline

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly | Section: Calendar 
 
 512
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those looking to have an event included in the weekly Caroline County calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.DENTONBishop Wayman program, Oct. 5, 1 to 3 p.m., Caroline County Public Library, Denton Branch. The program will be about the life and contributions of Bishop Wayman; born a free man in Tuckahoe Neck, Caroline County. He was elected the seventh Bishop of the African Methodist Episcopal Church.
Bingo, 7:30 p.m., Tuesdays, American Legion Post 29, 9238 Legion Road. 5 p.m. doors open, 7:30 p.m. games start. Info:410-479-2708.

Third Thursdays in Downtown Denton, 5 to 7 p.m., third Thursdays, downtown. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Tuesday & Wednesday, 401 Aldersgate Drive.
Paws for Reading, 3:40 to 4:25 p.m., every fourth Thursday, Central Branch library. Children ages 5 to 12 can proactice reading to a trained service dog. One registrant per session. Register: carolib.libcal.com.
Museum of Rural Life, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., every Saturday, 16 N. Second Street. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
Farmers market, Wednesdays until Oct. 30, 4 to 7 p.m., Third and Market Street. Shop for local produce, baked goods, coffee, flowers, plants, eggs, meat, art and more.
FEDERALSBURGMonday Bingo, 6 p.m. doors open; 7 p.m. bingo begins., Every Monday. Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Cash prizes, food available.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 4 to 6 p.m., Wednesdays, Community Civic League, 3439 Laurel Grove Road.
Heritage Day, Sept. 28, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., Heritage Museum, 100 Covey-Williams Alley. Special exhibit of images and artifacts from the Caroline County Minutemen. Former Federalsburg Town Manager and State Senator Rich Colburn will be speak at 1 p.m. Raffle, dinner at Exeter House, bake sale, light refreshments.
GOLDSBOROGiving Grace Food Pantry, Goldsboro VFC, 700 Old Line Road. 7 a.m. until; second Saturdays. Info: 302-270-1948.
GREENSBOROFood pantry, 4 to 7 p.m. Thursday, 7 to 9 a.m. Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday. Aaron's Place Pantry at Greensboro Connects, 111 S. Main St., side entrance.
PRESTON2024 Vendor DAZE, The Town of Preston has announced Preston DAZE 2024 Schedule: Oct. 19 and Dec. 7. For vendor applications email prestonmanager@prestonmaryland.us. Info: Town of Preston Facebook page.
Birding and Boating the Harriet Tubman Byway, Oct. 3, 2 to 6 p.m., Linchester Mill. Join Harriet Tubman Tours and Delmarva Birding Weekends as they go birding along the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Byway. During the guided, self-driven tour, attendees 'learn about the many daring escapes led by the famed freedom seeker and human rights activist know as "The Moses of Her People." Contact dmvbirds@gmail.com to reserve your space.
RIDGELYMartin's House & Barn, First Saturdays thrift store open 8 a.m. to noon. Drive-thru pantry and thrift store hours: 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday; 6 to 7:30 p.m. Wednesday.

content:
Mid-Shore Calendar

 October 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 1892
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
BOOK AND DVD DONATIONS, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Talbot County Free Library, Easton Branch. Book and DVD donations accepted at the Easton Library. One box or bag per person. Books and DVDs must be in good condition.
BIRD CLUB MEETING, 7 p.m., Easton Family YMCA, 202 Peachblossom Rd., Easton. Guest speaker will be Jim Brighton, "The Maryland Biodiversity Project." Business meeting will follow.
'AGING IN PLACE', 11 a.m. to 1 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Speaker Wendy Palmer. An informative health presentation about "Aging in Place" — functional fitness and exercise. Free. Bring your lunch. Limited seating. RSVP at oxfordcc.org.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
FALL INTO FLOWERS, 7 to 9 p.m., Cordova Firehouse. Locally grown flowers. Light refreshments included. There is a 40 person maximum limit. Cost is $25.00 and advance reservations are required. Contact Katelin Frase at 410-310-6457.
WALK FOR BREAST CANCER AWARENESS, 4:30 to 6:30, Eastern Shore Wellness Solutions Inc., 824 Fairmount Avenue, Cambridge. 5K walk around waterside Cambridge. umms.surveymonkey.com/r/LZC86H3.
ADVANCED HEALTHCARE PLANNING. 10 a.m. to noon, Talbot Hospice, 586 Cynwood Drive, Easton. Understand your options for Advanced Directive paperwork. Offered every second Thursday of the month. Free and open to the public. Call 410-822-6681 to register.
CAMBRIDGE FARMERS MARKET, 3 to 6 p.m., Long Wharf, High and Water Streets, Cambridge. Find local produce, meats, cheeses, crafts, and more at the weekly, waterfront Cambridge Farmers Market. Info: office@downtowncambridge.org.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
STAND UP COMEDY WITH UMAR KAHN, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton.
NATIONAL COMING OUT DAY WALK AND RESOURCE FAIR, 2 to 4 p.m., Dorchester County Health Department, 3 Cedar Street, Cambridge. Games, snacks, and community resources and vendors. cognitoforms.com/MDH3/JoinWalkingGroup.
HAUNTED HOUSE, 7 to 10 p.m., 1902 Church Creek Road, Church Creek. Haunted house and maze sponsored by Caroline County Volunteer Fire Department. Refreshments available for purchase.
FAIRYFEST, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., Adkins Arboretum, 12610 Eveland Rd., Ridgely. Maypole dancing, magical potions, elven archery, artisan fairy houses, a meadow pirate ship and more. Register: adkins.donorshops.com/product/FAIRYFEST2024/fairyfest-2024.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
EASTON AIRPORT DAY, 9:15 a.m. to 2 p.m., Easton Airport, 29137 Newman Road, Easton. Annual event is a fun-filled gathering that offers a unique opportunity to visit the community airfield and see what flying is all about. Featuring formation flyovers and Rubber Chicken Drop Contest.
EASTON BEERFEST, noon to 4 p.m., Easton Volunteer Fire Department, 315 Leonard Rieck Drive, Easton. Brewers, wineries, and distillers along with live music, games, food, vendors and more.
SECOND SATURDAY BOOK SALE, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Dorchester County Public Library, Cambridge Branch, 303 Gay St., Cambridge. Thousands of books are available, both hardback and paperback, at $1 and $.50 respectively.
SECOND SATURDAY, 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., downtown Cambridge. Monthly celebration in downtown Cambridge features free art gallery receptions, as well as specials in the independently owned shops and great dining. Shops and galleries are open all day and into the evening.
HORN POINT LAB OPEN HOUSE, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., Horn Point Lab, 2020 Horns Point Rd., Cambridge.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 8 to 9 a.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
SAIL ON SKIPJACK NATHAN, 1 to 3 p.m., Long Wharf, Cambridge. Sails are unique depending on wind, weather, captain and crew. Advance reservations are recommended and accepted at skipjack-nathan.org until midnight of the day before the sail.
HAUNTED HOUSE, 7 to 10 p.m., 1902 Church Creek Road, Church Creek. Haunted house and maze sponsored by Caroline County Volunteer Fire Department. Refreshments available for purchase.

Complimentary food and drinks in the private party area, plus three hours of bowling, balls and shoes. $50. per person to raise funds to purchase new books for the St. Michaels Library. Tickets at tcfl.org.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
BOOK AND DVD DONATIONS, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Talbot County Free Library, Easton Branch. Book and DVD donations accepted at the Easton Library. One box or bag per person. Books and DVDs must be in good condition.

Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
INTRO TO AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE, 6 to 7:30 p.m., Talbot County Free Library. Introduction to Learning American Sign Language with Jeremy Hillyard. Free but register at tcfl.org.
DECONSTRUCTING THE BEATLES, 7 to 9 p.m., Oxford Community Center. In thoroughly engaging (and often surprising) ways, acclaimed "Beatle-ologist" Scott Freiman guides you, step by step, on an educational journey and multimedia presentation about all things 'Beatles' and focusing on the album 'Sgt Pepper'. Tickets $20 at oxfordcc.org.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
OXFORD COMMUNITY DAY, 8 a.m. to noon, Oxford Community Center. Visit with your favorite community organizations and learn about ones you didn't know about. Free.

title: Mid-Shore Calendar
author: Staff Writer
content:
Mid-Shore Calendar

 October 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2523
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
STAND UP COMEDY WITH UMAR KAHN, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton.
NATIONAL COMING OUT DAY WALK AND RESOURCE FAIR, 2 to 4 p.m., Dorchester County Health Department, 3 Cedar Street, Cambridge. Games, snacks, and community resources and vendors. cognitoforms.com/MDH3/JoinWalkingGroup.
FAIRYFEST, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., Adkins Arboretum, 12610 Eveland Rd., Ridgely. Maypole dancing, magical potions, elven archery, artisan fairy houses, a meadow pirate ship and more. Register: adkins.donorshops.com/product/FAIRYFEST2024/fairyfest-2024.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
EASTON AIRPORT DAY, 9:15 a.m. to 2 p.m., Easton Airport, 29137 Newman Road, Easton. Annual event is a fun-filled gathering that offers a unique opportunity to visit the community airfield and see what flying is all about. Featuring formation flyovers and Rubber Chicken Drop Contest.
EASTON BEERFEST, noon to 4 p.m., Easton Volunteer Fire Department, 315 Leonard Rieck Drive, Easton. Brewers, wineries, and distillers along with live music, games, food, vendors and more.
SECOND SATURDAY BOOK SALE, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Dorchester County Public Library, Cambridge Branch, 303 Gay St., Cambridge. Thousands of books are available, both hardback and paperback, at $1 and $.50 respectively.
SECOND SATURDAY, 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., downtown Cambridge. Monthly celebration in downtown Cambridge features free art gallery receptions, as well as specials in the independently owned shops and great dining. Shops and galleries are open all day and into the evening.
HORN POINT LAB OPEN HOUSE, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., Horn Point Lab, 2020 Horns Point Rd., Cambridge.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 8 to 9 a.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
SAIL ON SKIPJACK NATHAN, 1 to 3 p.m., Long Wharf, Cambridge. Sails are unique depending on wind, weather, captain and crew. Advance reservations are recommended and accepted at skipjack-nathan.org until midnight of the day before the sail.
SCHOOL-COMMUNITY FLEA MARKET, 7 a.m. to noon, Cambridge South Dorchester High School, 2475 Cambridge Bypass, Cambridge.
BOWLING BASH FOR BOOKS, 5 to 8 p.m., Easton Bowl. Friends of the Library host their 50th anniversary Bowling Bash for Books. Complimentary food and drinks in the private party area, plus three hours of bowling, balls and shoes. $50. per person to raise funds to purchase new books for the St. Michaels Library. Tickets at tcfl.org.
FALL POKER RUN, 9:30 a.m. to 4 p.m., Cambridge Tire, 2486 Cambridge Beltway, Cambridge. Ride will end at the Fire House with bike show, music by Last Call, food and beer.
NANTICOKE RIVER JAMBOREE, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., Handsell Historic Site, 4837 Indiantown Road, Vienna. "Maryland's Emancipation" featuring living history interpreters from three cultures, Pocomoke Indian Nation and Drew Shuptar-Rayvis herbalist, colonial crafts, food truck, more.
TASTE OF CAMBRIDGE, noon to 6 p.m., Race and Poplar streets, downtown Cambridge. Cook-off and vendors.
GOODWILL WELLNESS CENTER BLOCK PARTY, 2 to 4 p.m., Goodwill Wellness Center, 1000 Goodwill Avenue, Cambridge. Fun activities, engaging entertainment and delicious food.
ENMVFD CASH BASH, 4 to 8 p.m., East New Market Volunteer Fire Department, 4020 East New Market Bypass, East New Market. For just $50, your ticket includes delicious food, refreshing sodas, and beer, along with the exciting chance to win over $25,000 in prizes.
POCOMOKE FALL FESTIVAL, noon to 4 p.m., downtown Pocomoke. Live entertainment, trick or treat, kids' costumes, face painting, food vendors, hay rides, corn pit, arts and craft vendors, bouncy house, petting farm, more.
GUIDED BIRDING TOURS AT BLACKWATER NWR, 8 a.m. to noon, Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge, 2145 Key Wallace Dr., Cambridge. No fee or registration required. Info: 410-228-2677 or www.fws.gov/refuge/Blackwater.
EASTERN SHORE BLUEGRASS ASSOCIATION CONCERT, Doors at 12:30 p.m., featured performers 2 p.m., American Legion Hall Post 29, 9238 Legion Road, Denton. $15 admission. Refreshments for sale.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
CAROLINE COUNTY AARP, noon, Church of the Nazarene, Denton. Covered dish luncheon. Guest speaker: Crystal Terhune from the University of Maryland Extension Service.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
BOOK AND DVD DONATIONS, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Talbot County Free Library, Easton Branch. Book and DVD donations accepted at the Easton Library. One box or bag per person. Books and DVDs must be in good condition.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
INTRO TO AMERICAN SIGN LANGUAGE, 6 to 7:30 p.m., Talbot County Free Library. Introduction to Learning American Sign Language with Jeremy Hillyard. Free but register at tcfl.org.
SMALL GROUP FILED DAY ON THE FARM, 10 a.m. to 3 p.m., Emilys Produce, 2214 Church Creek Road, Cambridge. Groups with 5-15 children welcomed to the farm for entry into fields of fun, which includes corn maze, activity area, animal visiting and a scarecrow making station (you just need to bring clothes for each child's scarecrow). On the way out all children get a free baby pumpkin. Admission $8 per child/chaperone, and 1 adult for every 5 kids gets free admission.
CAROL'S KITCHEN RIBBON CUTTING, noon to 1 p.m., Carol's Kitchen, Cambridge-Dorchester County Airport, 5263 Bucktown Road, Cambridge.
DECONSTRUCTING THE BEATLES, 7 to 9 p.m., Oxford Community Center. In thoroughly engaging (and often surprising) ways, acclaimed "Beatle-ologist" Scott Freiman guides you, step by step, on an educational journey and multimedia presentation about all things 'Beatles' and focusing on the album 'Sgt Pepper'. Tickets $20 at oxfordcc.org.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
ADULT HALLOWEEN PARTY, 7 to 8 p.m., Cambridge Moose Lodge, 5446 Moose Lodge Road, Cambridge. Dancing, games, costume contest, sweets.
SATURDAY, OCT. 19
OXFORD COMMUNITY DAY, 8 a.m. to noon, Oxford Community Center. Visit with your favorite community organizations and learn about ones you didn't know about. Free.
5K RUN/WALK FOR MENTAL HEALTH, 8 to 11 a.m., Oxford Community Center. The run/walk helps raise money for the Eastern Shore's mental health programs. Register at oxfordcc.org.
PICKET FENCE AUCTION, 5 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Local artists from Oxford, Easton and St. Michaels have volunteered their time, talents, and creativity to produce colorful painted scenes on a 4-picket section of the iconic Oxford Fence representing Eastern Shore Life. These works of art will be auctioned, with all proceeds going to local charities and nonprofits. oxfordcc.org.

title: Apply for a Brighter Christmas Fund award
author: Staff Writer
content:
Apply for a Brighter Christmas Fund award

 October 23, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: News 
 
 370
 Words 

 Read News Document

 APG Chesapeake and The Star Democrat's Brighter Christmas Fund has kicked off its 41st year of helping families in need. The Fund's board of directors and partner agencies invite Mid-Shore residents to share in the joy of giving to help their neighbors during the holiday season.Families needing assistance are urged to apply as soon as possible. To be eligible for assistance, you must be a resident of Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's or Talbot counties.
Pick up an application through your local social services department or at The Star Democrat, 29088 Airpark Drive, Easton. Return the completed application no later than 3 p.m. Nov. 18.
If you receive assistance from social services, you must apply through your agency.
If you do not receive assistance from social services, applications can be picked up in the lobby at The Star Democrat's office, located at 29088 Airpark Dr in Easton. The Star Democrat's office is open from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Monday through Friday.
You must submit with your application:
Copies of Social Security cards for adults and children on application.Proof of home address (copy of utility bill, rent or mortgage payment in your name).Proof of income (copy of 2022 income tax return and/or last two pay stubs).
If you receive assistance from any other Christmas charitable program, you will not be eligible to participate in the Brighter Christmas Fund.
After parents and guardians apply for Brighter Christmas Fund awards, their applications are vetted by the pertinent counties' social services agencies. Award letters will be mailed by the week of Dec. 3.
Eligible families may receive a shopping voucher for $100 per child, with a $300 maximum per family, to be redeemed at their local Walmart. Shopping must be done by Sunday, Dec. 31. A limited number of applications will be accepted, and families are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.
Families may receive assistance from the Brighter Christmas Fund for up to three consecutive years. Families that have received funds from the program for three years in a row must wait one year before they are eligible to reapply.
Brighter Christmas Fund awards are dependent on donations from the community. Filling out an application does not guarantee that you will receive anything.
For more information call 410-200-1884 or email bcf@chespub.com.

Christ Centered Prayer, 9 a.m. Sunday, with the Rev. Sandra Casey-Martus, Trinity Cathedral, 314 North St., Easton. Info: 410-822-1931, trinitycathedraleaston@gmail. Or trinitycathedraleaston.com.

Christ Episcopal Church, 601 Church St., Cambridge. Noon to 1 p.m. Every Wednesday. WOW (Worship On Wednesday) in the chapel with Bible study afterwards in Barber Hall. Bagged lunch optional.

 October 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2452
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
PARKER BARROW WITH MOJO ACES, 7 p.m., Cult Classic Brewing Company, 1169 Shopping Center Rd., Stevensville.
FALL-O-WEEN SIP-N-MUNCH-N-PAINT, 2:30 to 4:30 p.m., Craft Bakery & Cafe, Denton. Create a fun autumn/Halloween-themed porch sign or canvas painting. $30 for regular canvas or add $10 extra if you prefer the barn board. Register: 443-448-4042.
FALL HARVEST FAIR, 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., Dorchester County Recreation and Parks, 515 Leonards Lane, Cambridge. Pumpkin decorating contest, costume contest, games, educational area, crafts, and trunk or treat. Admission is $2 per person with pre-registration or $5 the day of. Contest entry is free.
'BLITHE SPIRIT', 7:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Tred Avon Players presents spirited and witty play that promises an evening of supernatural hilarity and sophisticated charm. Tickets: tredavonplayers.org.
MAIN STREET TRICK OR TREAT, 4 to 7 p.m., Cambridge Main Street district. Bring the kids out, in their Halloween costumes, for an evening of trick or treating.
ANNUAL CRAFT SHOW, Academy Art Museum, Easton. The show will feature a wide array of juried exhibitors, including established artists, returning favorites from years past and many more artists new to the show.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
ST. MICHAELS FARMERS MARKET, 8:30 to 11 a.m., 206 S. Talbot Street, St. Michaels. Open rain or shine.
INDOOR CRAFT AND YARD SALE, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., Caroline County 4-H Park, 8230 Detour Road, Denton. Benefits the 4-H program.
HALLOWEEN DANCE AND COSTUME PARTY, 7 to 11 p.m., Dorchester Post 91, 98 Sunburst Highway, Cambridge. GOLDEN TOUCH band. Cost is $13 per person, and there will be food available for purchase plus a cash bar. Prizes will be given for best costumes, there will be a 50/50 raffle and a live auction of baked items and desserts. Tickets and reservations are available at the Post 91 Lounge or 443-521-7838. Proceeds benefit veterans affairs.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 8 to 9 a.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
SAIL ON SKIPJACK NATHAN, 1 to 3 p.m., Long Wharf, Cambridge. Sails are unique depending on wind, weather, captain and crew. Advance reservations are recommended and accepted at skipjack-nathan.org until midnight of the day before the sail.
'BLITHE SPIRIT', 7:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Tred Avon Players presents spirited and witty play that promises an evening of supernatural hilarity and sophisticated charm. Tickets: tredavonplayers.org.
SUNSET IN THE STALKS, 3 to 6 p.m., Emily's Produce, 2214 Church Creek Road, Cambridge. Live music from Reagan Kent, local brews, happy hour treats, Fields of Fun adventures, & so much farm festivity. Info: emilysproduce.com.
TRUNK OR TREAT, 5 to 7 p.m., Neck District Volunteer Fire Company, 954 Cooks Point Road, Cambridge. Awards for best costume (kid and adult) and best decorated trunk. Food for sale to benefit Neck District Volunteer Fire Company. Candy donations are appreciated. Info and RSVP for parking spot: 301-928-3651.
OYSTERFEST, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum, 213 North Talbot St., St. Michaels. Sip, slurp, and savor, oysters. Live music, retriever demonstrations and more.
TRUNK OR TREAT, 5 to 7 p.m., Robbins Family YMCA, 201 Talbot Avenue, Cambridge. Music, costume parade, trunk decorating contest, crafts.
HALLOWEEN COSTUME PARTY WITH THUNDERBALL, 7 to 10 p.m., Old Saltys, 2560 Hoopers Island Road, Fishing Creek.
ANNUAL CRAFT SHOW, Academy Art Museum, Easton. The show will feature a wide array of juried exhibitors, including established artists, returning favorites from years past and many more artists new to the show.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Frederick Douglass on the Tuckahoe Park. Sparrows and field birds . All welcome. Bring binoculars. Depart from Easton Acme parking lot at 7 a.m. or meet at Frederick Douglass Park at 7:30 a.m. (GPS 38.9107 N, 75.9503 W). Leader: Ron Ketter (707-373-5532 or rgketter@gmail.com).
HAM AND CRAB CAKE DINNER, 11 a.m. to 2 p.m., Church Creek Volunteer Fire Company, 1902 Church Creek Road, Church Creek. Contact Mike Bramble for pre-orders at 443-521-9679.
TRUNK OR TREAT, 2 to 4 p.m., Cambridge Elks Lodge #1272, 5464 Elks Lodge Road, Cambridge. Bring the kids to a fun and safe afternoon of trick or treating.
'BLITHE SPIRIT', 2 p.m., Oxford Community Center. Tred Avon Players presents spirited and witty play that promises an evening of supernatural hilarity and sophisticated charm. Tickets: tredavonplayers.org.
TRUNK OR TREAT, 4 to 6 p.m., Pleasant Day Child Care Center, 2474 Cambridge Beltway, Cambridge. Visitors can also explore care center's new facility.
TRUNK OR TREAT, 4:30 to 6 p.m., Immanuel United Church of Christ, 5401 White Hall Road (at the corner of US Rt. 50), back parking lot, Cambridge. Children 12 and under will have the opportunity to trick or treat the decorated trunks of volunteer "treators."
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MONDAY BINGO, 6 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. bingo, Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Every Monday. Cash prizes, food available.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.

Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.

NATIONAL HERITAGE AREA COMMUNITY MEETING, 5:30 p.m., Eastern Shore Higher Education Center, Chesapeake College, 1000 College Circle, Wye Mills. Heavy Hors d'oeuvres will be served.

Sessions designed for adults and mature, self-assured youth. $5 for chapter members. $10 for non members. Register: form.jotform.com/242716431647054.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Oxford Conservation Park. Waterfowl, meadowlarks and sparrows. Bring binoculars. All welcome. Meet at park at 7 a.m. (GPS 38.6847 N, 76.1586 W). Leaders: Susie Pratt (410-924-4925 or prattsuzzie@gmail.com) and Peggy Ford (410-725-1101 or pjford21@gmail.com). Breakfast to follow hosted by Janet Mackey and Ron Ketter for $5 donation.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB WORK WEEKEND, Irish Grove Sanctuary. Sanctuary maintenance (and birding). Bring binoculars, own bedding & sleeping bags. May camp if desired. Contact Jeremy Castle (jeremy.castle@mdbirds.org) for more details.

title: Temporary closure eastbound span of Bay Bridge set for Nov. 10
author: Staff Writer
content:
Temporary closure eastbound span of Bay Bridge set for Nov. 10

 November 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: News 
 
 264
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — The Maryland Transportation Authority is partnering with Anne Arundel and Queen Anne's counties to accommodate the Bay Bridge Run on Sunday, Nov. 10. The run will be held on the eastbound span of the bridge.As a result, the eastbound Bay Bridge will be closed to traffic Nov. 10 from approximately 12:01 a.m. to 2 p.m., weather permitting. The MDTA will have two-way traffic operations in place on the westbound span. One lane of traffic will operate in each direction on the westbound span, with the center lane closed to traffic. The center lane may open to traffic intermittently to help reduce westbound delays.
For information on the event, go to thebaybridgerun.com.
Along with the eastbound span closure, the following closures and detours will be in place on the Eastern Shore during the event:
The off-ramp from eastbound US 50 to MD 8 will be closed. A detour will be in place to direct motorists to the next exit at Thompson Creek Road. From there, motorists will travel westbound on MD 835 to the signal at MD 8.
The on-ramp from MD 8 to westbound US 50 will be closed. Traffic attempting to access westbound US 50 will be directed to MD 18 to the roundabout at Castle Marina Road and onto westbound US 50. Additionally, residents wishing to travel west on US 50 should approach the highway from either Duke Street or Castle Marina Road.
Motorists using the Bay Bridge on Nov. 10 should expect significant delays throughout the day. To avoid delays, motorists are urged to travel prior to 6 a.m. or after 6 p.m.

title: Exercise your constitutional right to vote Tuesday
author: ORESTES BAEZ APG Regional President
content:
Exercise your constitutional right to vote Tuesday

 November 4, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ORESTES BAEZ APG Regional President | Section: Editorials 
 
 540
 Words 

 Read News Document

 On Tuesday, Nov. 5, we have an opportunity to exercise our constitutional right to vote. It is not a God-given right, it's a right detailed by our founding father's document to orchestrate a democratic world to exist and prosper in. And it's not about who you vote for, more importantly it's that you take the time to process choices and select a candidate you would be happy with in hopes others feel the same and provide enough support to move your candidate forward. Your candidate may or may not win.I shudder to think at what the founding fathers would say about the word smithing, arbitrary use of language, misinterpretation of the truth, and just some outright tomfoolery that some candidates show. I suspect that was not their original goal.
But why is this all so divisive? Why are our human choices creating chasms of space between people, friends and family?
My perspective comes from a small, rare point — I am a political refugee from Cuba. My father was in a prosperous country with lots of acceptance until the Russians made friends with the Communist Party in Cuba. My father was told he would be going to Czechoslovakia to teach the Russians how to fix cars. It was the second time they came for him.
"No thanks" was not an option. A friend from UNESCO smuggled my parents into the American Embassy and helped fake some documents so we could leave the country.
Come hang out in our communist world and see how popular it feels.
With $75, me, my sister, my dad's parents and my mom and dad flew to Miami to start over. Crowded living conditions, hard work ethic, no handouts were the beliefs we followed. Life of service — how can we help you? — was my mother's driving core belief. Ny uncles served in the Army to give back the country that accepted us.
We turned down relocation efforts around the U.S. because we would work to create our own prosperous world. We earned our keep each and every day. Our friends who were doctors and engineers pumped gas and sold newspapers to help generate money for the family until they could get an education and be certified to do what they did in Cuba.
The world was OK. We were tolerant of each other. Could we say that today? Should we say that today?
I visit the old neighborhood occasionally to remind me of my roots — the upstairs apartment over the garage that housed all of us, the old Sts. Peter and Paul church where I did my first Holy Communion, and the local markets where we shopped before the supermarkets existed.
People knew of you and helped you. We never fought over who to vote for. The most contentious conversations were the ones debating when the regime in Cuba would fall and how all would return to how it was. But we were still together.
What happened?
Today we can't put the genie back in the bottle. We are where we are and need to move forward. We need to find more middle ground and help all of us prosper. We need to vote and be tolerant.
Please join me in exercising your constitutional right on Nov. 5. And let's all be more tolerant.

 After her husband died, a grandmother needed help providing a Christmas celebration for her two young grandsons last year.The grandmother also cared for her adult son, the boys' father, who is blind. The boys' mother had died.

All Faith Episcopal Chapel, 26282 Tunis Mills Road, Easton. Sunday service 9:30 a.m. followed by coffee hour. First and third Sundays, Holy Eucharist; second and fourth Sundays, morning prayer. Asbury United Methodist Church, 18 S. Higgins St., Easton. 10 a.m. Sunday worship service. Bible Study 6 p.m. Tuesday. Pastor Reginald Pinkett.
Bethel AME Church, Chestertown. Conference call worship, prayer and study. Dial in: 425-436-6341, access code: 540836. If unable to join the call after several attempts, call the backup number: 520-420-9081 and follow instructions given. Worship service: Sundays 11 a.m. to noon. Corporate prayer: Mondays 7 to 7:30 p.m. Life Application Bible study: Wednesdays 7 to 8 p.m. All are welcome.
Bethesda Methodist Church, 155 Main St., P.O.Box 147, Preston. Contemporary Service and Bethesda Bible Adventures held Sundays at 9 a.m. Traditional Service at church at 11 a.m. Pastor Nate Weaver. Info: 410-673-7538 or bethesdapreston.faith.
Temple B'nai Israel, The Satell Center for Jewish Life on the Eastern Shore, a reform temple, Easton. For information, visit BnaiIsraelEaston.org.
Bozman United Methodist Church, 7988 Bozman-Neavitt Road, Bozman. Worship service 1 p.m. Sunday. The Rev. Marty Wiley is pastor.

Sunday services: 8 a.m. Rite 1 with communion, 9:15 a.m. contemporary service, 11 a.m. traditional service. 9:15 a.m. and 11 a.m. Sunday school. Info: christchurcheaston.org, Facebook.

title: Veterans Day Roundup
author: Staff Writer
content:
Veterans Day Roundup

 November 8, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: News 
 
 481
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The origins of Veterans Day in the U.S. date back to 1921 with the burial of an unknown World War I American soldier on a hillside overlooking the Potomac River in Arlington National Cemetery.England and France had already memorialized the end of WWI with burials of unknown soldiers and ceremonies on the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month in 1918, the day the war came to an official close.
An annual commemoration of the formal cease fire was first known as Armistice Day.
A Congressional resolution in 1926 officially named Armistice Day, and it became a national holiday 12 years later.
But according to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, in 1947 in Birmingham, Alabama, the first celebration under the name Veterans Day was held with parades and other festivities to honor all veterans.
Communities throughout the nation, including Barron County, continue the tradition of holding Veterans Day ceremonies. Here is a snapshot of some opportunities on Monday, Nov. 11, to thank veterans for serving their country.
Rice LakeRice Lake Middle School, 204 Cameron Road, will host a 2024 Veterans Day service with a free program open to the public beginning at 10 a.m.
The event will be live-streamed on the Rice Lake Community Media Channels and via the website ricelaketv.com, and a photo gallery will be available to view on Chronotype.com.
The program will include the presentation of Honor Banners honoring 21 service members to their families.
Rice Lake Main Street Association spearheads the banner project. The banners bear the picture and name of a veteran, their branch of service, and how many years or wars in which they were involved.
The banners were hung on Memorial Day weekend along Veterans Lakeshore Drive and were taken down on Patriot Day on Sept. 11 to be washed in preparation to be presented to the veterans' families at the ceremony.
Biographies of the 21 veterans can be found at rlveteransdrivepro.wixsite.com/rlvdprojects. To nominate veterans for next year's project email a service members name and rank, military branch, years of service/war(s) and a photo to rlveteransdriveprojects@gmail.com.
HaugenHaugen Elementary School's Veterans Day Program begins at 1:45 p.m. at the school. The program will include student performances, and fourth-grade students will be setting the missing man table with the audience learning what the different pieces of the table represent.
The program is scheduled to conclude by 2:15 p.m.
CameronCameron High School is hosting a Veterans Day program at 9:45 a.m. in the high school gymnasium, featuring music from the band and choir. Guest speaker is U.S. Army Master Sergeant Justin Imlo. The public is welcome.
The FBLA will be hosting a brief appreciation gathering afterwards with snacks and drinks for veterans. The program should take around 30 minutes.
BarronVeterans Day Programs will be held at Barron High School at 8:20 a.m., Woodland Elementary School at 9 a.m., Riverview Middle School at 10 a.m., Almena Elementary School at 10:30 a.m. and Ridgeland/Dallas Elementary School at 2 p.m.

title: Donations ease financial needs
author: Staff Writer
content:
Donations ease financial needs

 November 9, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Editors Inbox 
 
 339
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Maryland Association of Social Services Boards (MASSB) Foundation is composed entirely of volunteers who serve on local boards in all 23 counties in the state of Maryland.For those of you who are not familiar with the Caroline County Department of Social Services' Advisory Board, our mission is to provide assistance to support families in financial crisis that do not meet federal and/or state program eligibility but need assistance.
Under the auspices of the Maryland Association of the Social Services Boards, an established nonprofit, the Caroline County Department of Social Services' Board of Directors oversees the Community Assistance Fund, which responds to unmet needs that are fundamental to the safety, health and well-being of Caroline County's children and adults.
Since its inception in 2012, Caroline's Community Assistance Fund has assisted county residents with rental, utilities arrearages and food insecurities. Additionally, the fund provides support in the form of medical supplies and emergency repairs for the elderly.
As you may be aware, there continues to be a growing number of county residents with unmet needs. As we move into the winter months and the holiday season we anticipate an increased need for holiday assistance for families with children and our elderly who are not as fortunate. Any assistance garnered through this drive will also go towards assisting our seniors in need.
We would like to thank you for the generous support you've provided in the past and encourage you to donate whatever you can to our organization to help our less-fortunate neighbors. Please make your checks payable to MASSB Foundation and mail them to:
Juanita A. Webster, Board Chair; Caroline County Department of Social Services; P.O. Box 400; Denton, MD 21629.
Donations can also be made via credit card at massbfoundation.org. Please add a note that your donation is in support of Caroline County Department of Social Services. All donations are 100% tax deductible.
MASSB is an all-volunteer organization so you will have the comfort of knowing that your funds will go directly to those in need.
Thank you for your kindness and your support.
JUANITA A. WEBSTER
Denton

Samaritan House Thrift Shop, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Wednesday to Friday; 9 a.m. to noon Saturday. 5th Street behind the post office.
Third Thursdays in Downtown Denton, 5 to 7 p.m., third Thursdays, downtown. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Tuesday & Wednesday, 401 Aldersgate Drive.
Paws for Reading, 3:40 to 4:25 p.m., every fourth Thursday, Central Branch library. Children ages 5 to 12 can proactice reading to a trained service dog. One registrant per session. Register: carolib.libcal.com.
Museum of Rural Life, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., every Saturday, 16 N. Second Street. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
Caroline Branch NAACP election, Thursday, Nov. 14, 4 to 8 p.m., Choptank Electric Cooperative Building, Denton. Election of 2025-2026 officers and at-large executive committee members. All members in good standing are eligible to vote. The election will be conducted by the NAACP National Office using the electronic system Election Buddy.
Tree luminary pottery class, Saturday, Nov. 16, 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m., The Foundry. Join Sharon Guzman to create a hand-built pottery luminary. Cost $30, materials included. Register: carolinearts.org/events/tree-luminary-pottery-class/.
FEDERALSBURGMonday Bingo, 6 p.m. doors open; 7 p.m. bingo begins., Every Monday. Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Cash prizes, food available.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 4 to 6 p.m., Wednesdays, Community Civic League, 3439 Laurel Grove Road.
Federalsburg Floods, Fridays 10 a.m. to noon, Saturdays 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Federalsburg Heritage Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave. Eight significant floods that devastated Federalsburg in the 20th century are highlighted in a new exhibit at the Historical Society's museum.
GOLDSBOROGiving Grace Food Pantry, Goldsboro VFC, 700 Old Line Road. 7 a.m. until; second Saturdays. Info: 302-270-1948.
GREENSBOROFood pantry, 4 to 7 p.m. Thursday, 7 to 9 a.m. Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday. Aaron's Place Pantry at Greensboro Connects, 111 S. Main St., side entrance.

The banquet theme is "Caroline County is All IN for Freedom, Justice, and Equality of Rights for All." The event will feature thought-provoking presenters, emerging youth leaders, distinguished honorees, great music, and wholesome fellowship. Panelists: the Rev. Pearl Geter, Sheriff Donald Baker, the Rev. Alfred Woods and the Rev. Gregory McLaurin. Tickets $45 for adults, $20 for youth 12 and under. No tickets will be sold at the door. Info: 410-726-8087, 410-253-1273 or naacp7013@gmail.com.
2024 Vendor DAZE, The Town of Preston has announced Preston DAZE 2024, Dec. 7. For vendor applications email prestonmanager@prestonmaryland.us. Info: Town of Preston Facebook page.

Family can't take on extra expenses after HVAC replacement

 November 20, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Words 

 Read News Document

 A family is barely making ends meet after financing the replacement of their HVAC system, which broke earlier this year."We always work to make sure bills are paid 100%, and at times that leaves little for anything else," the mother said.
With the holidays approaching, this mother was worried she wouldn't be able to provide a Christmas celebration for her two young children.
This family will receive assistance with their holiday celebration from the Brighter Christmas Fund.
Your donation to the Brighter Christmas Fund could help local families in similar situations provide a holiday celebration for their children.
The Brighter Christmas Fund is a nonprofit helping families in need on the Mid-Shore. Donations may be sent to The Star Democrat at 29088 Airpark Dr., Easton, MD 21601. Donations also may be made online via credit card or PayPal at brighterchristmasfund.org. Click the "Donate" button.
Donations are tax-deductible.

title: Be a Santa program serves Mid-Shore seniors
author: Tom McCall
content:
Be a Santa program serves Mid-Shore seniors

 November 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Tom McCall | Section: Life 
 
 737
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Usually when it comes to holiday gifts comes, children are top priority, but according to organizers of a program serving multiple Mid-Shore counties, there is another deserving population for shoppers to keep in mind.Senior citizens will receive a small gift and some community connection through the "Be a Santa to a Senior" program this holiday season.
"A simple, thoughtful gift can bring immense happiness to an older adult who may not have family around to celebrate with," said Jenna Marchi, owner of the Home Instead office in Easton, which is coordinating the effort. "Being a Santa to a Senior is about more than presents—it's about showing care, love, and letting these individuals know they are not forgotten."
The program aims to help combat the loneliness many seniors feel around the holiday season.
There are trees with seniors' names on the ornaments at 20 different locations from Easton, to Grasonville, to Preston. Those interested in purchasing a gift for a senior are asked to select an ornament, buy the gift listed on it, and return the gift and ornament to the location where they found it.
Childlene Brooks is the Senior Center manager at Brookletts Place in Easton.
"All of the name tags are gone. Some of the gifts are back. We had 23 names to start with. They wanted stacked baskets, slippers, sweaters, hats, perfume and bath towels. Word games and gloves. Nothing costly. The last ones came off the tree on Friday," Brooks said of the tree at Brookletts Place.
The tags that go on her tiny tree have the recipient's first name, a code number and whether they are male or female. "It also indicates what they want," Brooks said.
Her favorite part is to help seniors in the community out.
"They probably don't have any other avenue of obtaining some of these things or any family to help them out. I am one for helping. If I can help in any way, that is what I want to do. A lot of them are still living alone. They need contact with other people," Brooks said.
The Ridgely Pharmacy has been participating in the program for over 10 years.
"It is going wonderfully. I think we are one of the top ones that help. We try to do over 200. It is very rewarding to help these seniors. We have six left to go," Brenda Walls said. She is the owner of The Ridgely Pharmacy.
There were gifts like a lap blanket, shoes, lotion, cleaning products and a cane listed on ornaments at her store.
"I have a following now. As soon as I put it on my Facebook page, we had people coming in. It is all about giving back to our community," Walls said.
Although there is a physical transaction, the emotional one is just as crucial.
"This program is about so much more than giving gifts—it's about creating moments of joy and connection between older adults and the community," Marchi said. "There's nothing more rewarding than seeing the smile on a senior's face when they open their gift and feel the love behind it."
