title: Tides of Grace presents 5th annual Christmas Magic Toy Drive
author: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com
content:
Tides of Grace presents 5th annual Christmas Magic Toy Drive

 November 22, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com | Section: Local News 
 
 348
 Words 

 Read News Document

 STEVENSVILLE — Ensuring the joy of Christmas is spread throughout the Eastern Shore community, Tides of Grace once again welcomes the return of its signature Christmas Magic Toy Drive.This year's annual drive anticipates serving nearly 1,000 children and is currently collecting gently used toys for infants through teens. The drive serves as a perfect way to make room for new gifts this holiday season and show children the joy of giving, Leann Rhodes, Tides of Grace executive director, said.
Toys will be collected from drop off locations starting at midnight, Dec. 6 and volunteer elves will come out for an extravagant Christmas pajama party at The Edge Arena to sort and lay all the goodies across the 25,000 square-foot edge arena.
From 7 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. Dec. 7, Christmas magic will welcome registered parents to shop for free toys for children ages infant to 17.
This jolly big event is designed for parents only, with children left at home to maintain the element of surprise.
No income verification is required, but parents must register ahead of time.
This event takes a total of 200 volunteers from the community starting from midnight on Friday, Dec. 6 through the morning hours of Saturday, Dec. 7 to make it possible.
"It's really awesome to see the community come together in such a big way," Rhodes said.
The annual event began in 2020 with a group of moms wanting to spread holiday cheer, and it has grown tremendously over the years, from helping 100 children in 2020 to over 600 children in 2023, she said.
Donators are asked to ensure toys are in working condition and keep all parts together with a bag to prevent them from getting lost during sorting.
The drive is not accepting stuffed animals, used clothes, or books this year.
Drop off locations are located throughout the Eastern Shore with volunteers available to arrange pickups if donations can't be dropped off in person.
"Together, we can spread joy and ensure that every child in our community feels the love this holiday season," Rhodes said.
More information including child registration and drop off locations can be found at tidesofgraceinc.org/christmas-magic.

author: Connie Connolly
content:
Caroline County Commission to meet Dec. 10

 November 27, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly | Section: News 
 
 207
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON — The next Caroline County Commission meeting will be held 9 a.m. Tuesday, Dec. 10, in Room 106 of the Caroline County Courthouse, located at 109 Market Street in Denton.Meetings are held 9 a.m. Tuesdays except the fifth Tuesday of the month, unless announced otherwise. There will be no meeting Dec. 3. Meetings are open to the public for attendance. Attendees will be security screened as they enter the courthouse.
All Commission agendas with hyperlinks to documents can be found at www.carolinemd.org.
The public can also attend meetings and work sessions remotely via ZOOM at https://zoom.us/j/300062187. The toll-free phone numbers to dial in are 888-475-4499 or 877-853-5257, and the meeting ID number is 300 062 187.
Public comment will be held during the beginning and end of each meeting. You may submit written comments through the county's email system, website, and by USPS at 109 Market Street, Room 123, Denton, MD 21629. Written comments received prior to a meeting will be entered into the record and made available to the Commissioners prior to the meeting or hearing.
All speakers, including the Commissioners must announce their name each time before they speak. Any document being voted on by the Commissioners will be linked on the agenda in advance when possible.

Compare shipping costs

 December 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Editors Inbox 
 
 365
 Words 

 Read News Document

 I want to assure you that the U.S. Postal Service is primed and ready to deliver exceptional service during the 2024 holiday rush. Thanks to the substantial progress USPS has made under the Delivering for America plan our operational, transportation and delivery processes have never been more finely tuned and our ability to move packages and mail throughout our network has never been stronger.As you and your family prepare for the holidays, it's always a good idea to ship early. We encourage everyone to send their holiday mail and packages well in advance to ensure they reach their destinations on time, but we understand that sometimes cards or packages are sent last minute.
This year, our recommended send-by dates for expected holiday delivery within the continental U.S. before Dec. 25 are:
Dec. 18 — USPS Ground Advantage service; first class mail service.
Dec. 19 — Priority Mail service.
Dec. 21 — Priority Mail Express service.
USPS continues to offer the lowest postage rates and the most affordable and reliable way to ship packages and mail this holiday season.
How can you save money this holiday season?
Here are some important questions: what are you shipping, how much does it weigh, where is it going, how soon does it have to be there?
Here is one example. If you are sending a 10-pound package from Salisbury (or any post office in Maryland) to Santa Claus, Indiana, comparing our options, using Ground Advantage, the postage would be $20.15, Priority Mail Service by weight, $25.40, Priority Large Flat Rate Box, $26, and for the procrastinators, Priority Mail Express, $115.25. These prices have no "hidden fees" like surcharges for fuel, residential and Saturday/Sunday delivery.
What else sets us apart from our competitors?
We offer free boxes and tape for our Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express services. We include $100 insurance and free tracking on our Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express services and have free pick-up at home or your business. All these can be found on our website, usps.com.
Dare to compare with our competitors; however, I am confident you will prepare to compare USPS services before Dec. 18 to save money this holiday season and year-round.
MARK WAHL
Washington, D.C.

 December 7, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Editors Inbox 
 
 106
 Words 

 Read News Document

 As a longtime subscriber, I was dismayed to learn that there will no longer be home delivery of the Star Dem. Andre Thurman, the gentleman who has delivered my newspaper for many years, has done a stellar job, and I am very sorry to learn that he is no longer going to be employed by the newspaper. He is a wonderful person and deserves to keep his job.Most of your subscribers on his route have tiny P.O. boxes that will fill up if they contain more than two newspapers.
To avoid that, please consider rehiring Mr. Thurman to continue delivering the Star Dem to us.
JOAN WETMORE
Neavitt

title: Nominations open for Women and Girls Fund Award
author: Staff Writer
content:
Nominations open for Women and Girls Fund Award

 December 11, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Life 
 
 353
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Women and Girls Fund of the Mid-Shore is accepting nominations for its annual Women and Girls Fund Award, which will be presented to the recipient at the annual grants and awards luncheon in the spring. Established in 2004, the award honors a community member from Caroline, Dorchester, Kent, Queen Anne's or Talbot counties who has made outstanding professional or personal contributions towards addressing the needs of local women and girls.Candidates for this award should have demonstrated leadership, vision, integrity, compassion, cooperation and generosity of time and talent in their efforts to improve the lives and opportunities of women and girls.
The 2024 Women and Girls Fund Award was presented to Amelia "Amy" Blades Steward of Easton for her outstanding professional and personal contributions to the Mid-Shore. As a volunteer and board member, both locally and statewide, she has been active with numerous organizations, including Talbot Arts, Talbot Community Connections, Channel Marker, Character Counts, Waterfowl Festival, Shore Leadership Alumni Association and Bay to Ocean Writer's Conference Committee.
As the owner of Steward Writing and Communications, she has helped elevate the visibility local nonprofits through marking, public relations and fundraising services. As a regional storyteller, Amy has focused her writing on telling the stories of those who are often overlooked in our community. She has made long-lasting contributions to improving the lives of women, girls and families in the Mid-Shore.
The late Lois Duffy of Centreville and Chestertown was the first recipient. In succeeding years, the Women & Girls Fund has honored: the late Harriet Critchlow; Sandra King; Dr. Maria Boria; Sister Patricia Gamgort, OSB; Tracy Davenport; Sandra Redd; Sara Jane Davidson; the Hon. Karen Murphy Jensen; the five founders of For All Seasons Behavioral Health and Rape Crisis Center; Mary Lou McAllister; the late Diana Mautz; the late Kathy Weaver; Ellen Rajacich; Susan Stockman; Krista Pettit; Carlene Wilson; Julie Lowe; Chrissy Aull and Jo Ann Asparagus Murray.
The application deadline is Jan. 3. Nomination forms can be downloaded from womenandgirlsfund.org/awards and submitted by mail to 102 E. Dover St., second floor, Easton, MD 21601 or email to info@womenandgirlsfund.org. For further information, call the office at 410-770-8347.

content:
Mid-Shore Calendar

 December 14, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 1252
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.EASTON FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to 1 p.m., 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine. Live music at 10:30 a.m.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
SECOND SATURDAY BOOK SALE, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., Dorchester County Public Library, Cambridge Branch, 303 Gay St., Cambridge. Thousands of books are available, both hardback and paperback, at $1 and $.50 respectively.
SECOND SATURDAY, 10 a.m. to 9 p.m., downtown Cambridge. Monthly celebration in downtown Cambridge features free art gallery receptions, as well as specials in the independently owned shops and great dining. Shops and galleries are open all day and into the evening.
WREATHS ACROSS AMERICA, noon, Denton Cemetery, Denton. First time that the ceremony will be held in Denton and is being organized by local boy scout Billy Quick as his Eagle Scout service project. Volunteer or sponsor a wreath: wreathsacrossamerica.org/MDDCEM.
FEDERALSBURG FLOODS, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Federalsburg Heritage Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave., Federalsburg. Eight significant floods that devastated Federalsburg in the 20th century are highlighted in a new exhibit at the Historical Society's museum.
SANTA'S WORKSHOP, noon to 4 p.m., Wharves of Choptank Visitor & Heritage Center, 3 Crouse Park Ln., Denton. A holiday event where families can create toys with "elves" and meet Santa. Suggested Donation: $15 per child. Registration: carolinearts.org/events/santas-workshop-in-the-island-of-misfit-toys/.
HOLIDAY PARADE, 10:30 a.m., Talbot Street, St. Michaels.
LIGHTED BOAT PARADE, 6 p.m., St. Michaels Harbor. Decorated boats parade around the harbor.
FOUNDATION OF HOPE ANNUAL LUNCHEON, 11:30 a.m., Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay, Cambridge. Networking, silent auction, lunch, presentation. Guest speaker: Dr. Trudy Hall, chief medical officer of TidalHealth. Tickets: foundationofhopemaryland.org/annual-luncheon.
OLD FASHIONED CHRISTMAS DINNER, 11 a.m., Union United Methodist Church, 100 Fremont Street, St. Michaels. The menu includes sliced roast turkey with trimmings, Maryland fried oysters, baked macaroni and cheese, candied sweet potatoes, Blue Lake green beans, dinner roll and assorted desserts. $25.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
HOLIDAY POTLUCK AND ENTERTAINMENT, 5:30 to 8:30 p.m., Oxford Community Center. A good old fashioned potluck dinner to celebrate the holidays. Entertainment by the Tred Avon Players. RSVP oxfordcc.org, including what you're bringing.
MAKE MOSAIC AND CRYSTAL ORNAMENTS, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m., The Foundry, Denton. Craft two ornaments in one workshop with Joanne Gelles and Kyleen Asche. Price: $45 (materials included). Registration: carolinearts.org/events/make-mosaic-crystal-ornaments/.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
FEDERALSBURG FLOODS, 10 a.m. to noon, Federalsburg Heritage Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave., Federalsburg. Eight significant floods that devastated Federalsburg in the 20th century are highlighted in a new exhibit at the Historical Society's museum.
BENEDICTINE SCHOOL FUNDRAISER, 5 to 9 p.m., Ridgely Train Station, Ridgely. Hot cocoa and popcorn, light display.
HISTORIC WALKING TOURS, 11 a.m. and noon, Talbot Historical Society, 25 S. Washington St., Easton. Third Saturday of the month. Guided tours of Historic Easton, viewing many of the earliest federal buildings where you hear the stories of the transformation and growth as war, fire and railroads impacted the town. Noon tour will focus on the Ebenezer Methodist Episcopal Church, Market House and Bullitt House and discuss how architecture related to spiritual, civic, and daily life. Tour groups are limited to 10 individuals per tour. Advanced reservation required. Tours are free. 410-822-0773.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
FEDERALSBURG FLOODS, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Federalsburg Heritage Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave., Federalsburg. Eight significant floods that devastated Federalsburg in the 20th century are highlighted in a new exhibit at the Historical Society's museum.
BREAKFAST WITH SANTA, 7 a.m. to noon, Hyatt Regency Chesapeake Bay, Cambridge. Take photos with Santa while enjoying a delicious holiday buffet. $27 for adults, Kids 5-12 pay their age, Kids under 5 free. 15% off meal when unopened toy brought to donate to Toys for Tots. Reservations: hyattexperiences.com/hyatt-regency/chesa?icamp=property_page_menu_book_experiences#!/.

title: Grandmother stretched thin for the holidays
author: Staff Writer
content:
Grandmother stretched thin for the holidays

 December 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: News 
 
 318
 Words 

 Read News Document

 A grandmother has been disabled for more than 20 years.Though she is unable to work, she cares for her daughter, who is experiencing mental health challenges, and her two grandchildren on the household's limited income.
With the holidays approaching, the grandmother wasn't sure how she would provide Christmas presents for her 1- and 2-year old grandchildren. She will receive help with her family's holiday celebration from the Brighter Christmas Fund.
Your donation to the Brighter Christmas Fund could help local families in similar situations provide a holiday celebration for their children.
The Brighter Christmas Fund is a nonprofit helping families in need on the Mid-Shore. Donations may be sent to The Star Democrat at 29088 Airpark Dr., Easton, MD 21601. Donations also may be made online via credit card or PayPal at brighterchristmasfund.org. Click the "Donate" button.
Donations are tax-deductible.
The administrative costs for the Brighter Christmas Fund are covered entirely by The Star Democrat and APG Chesapeake, so 100% of donations go to families in need. For more information about the fund, call 410-200-1884.
The total donated for this year's Brighter Christmas Fund to date is $51,173.75.
Those in the sharing spirit of giving with others this holiday season include:

title: Caroline County Commission to meet Dec. 24
author: Connie Connolly
content:
Caroline County Commission to meet Dec. 24

 December 18, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly | Section: News 
 
 207
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON — The next Caroline County Commission meeting will be held 9 a.m. Tuesday, Dec. 24, in Room 106 of the Caroline County Courthouse, located at 109 Market Street in Denton.Meetings are held 9 a.m. Tuesdays except the fifth Tuesday of the month, unless announced otherwise. There will be no meeting Dec. 31. Meetings are open to the public for attendance. Attendees will be security screened as they enter the courthouse.
All Commission agendas with hyperlinks to documents can be found at www.carolinemd.org.
The public can also attend meetings and work sessions remotely via ZOOM at https://zoom.us/j/300062187. The toll-free phone numbers to dial in are 888-475-4499 or 877-853-5257, and the meeting ID number is 300 062 187.
Public comment will be held during the beginning and end of each meeting. You may submit written comments through the county's email system, website, and by USPS at 109 Market Street, Room 123, Denton, MD 21629. Written comments received prior to a meeting will be entered into the record and made available to the Commissioners prior to the meeting or hearing.
All speakers, including the Commissioners must announce their name each time before they speak. Any document being voted on by the Commissioners will be linked on the agenda in advance when possible.

title: Caroline County Commission to meet Jan. 6
author: Connie Connolly
content:
Caroline County Commission to meet Jan. 6

 December 25, 2024 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly | Section: News 
 
 207
 Words 

 Read News Document

 DENTON — The next Caroline County Commission meeting will be held 9 a.m. Tuesday, Jan. 7, in Room 106 of the Caroline County Courthouse, located at 109 Market Street in Denton.Meetings are held 9 a.m. Tuesdays except the fifth Tuesday of the month, unless announced otherwise. There will be no meeting Dec. 31. Meetings are open to the public for attendance. Attendees will be security screened as they enter the courthouse.
All Commission agendas with hyperlinks to documents can be found at www.carolinemd.org.
The public can also attend meetings and work sessions remotely via ZOOM at https://zoom.us/j/300062187. The toll-free phone numbers to dial in are 888-475-4499 or 877-853-5257, and the meeting ID number is 300 062 187.

Written comments received prior to a meeting will be entered into the record and made available to the Commissioners prior to the meeting or hearing.
All speakers, including the Commissioners must announce their name each time before they speak. Any document being voted on by the Commissioners will be linked on the agenda in advance when possible.

title: National Day of Mourning closes post office
author: Staff Writer
content:
National Day of Mourning closes post office

 January 7, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: News 
 
 84
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The U.S. Postal Service will be closed on Thursday due to the National Day of Mourning for President Jimmy Carter. There will be no mail delivery on that day. The Star Democrat will be delivered to local post offices early Thursday morning as usual, but all mail deliveries will not restart until Friday.Newspapers will be delivered to local stores that retail the Star Democrat and will be available on Thursday. The e-edition of the newspaper will be available on StarDem.com early Thursday morning.

WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
CHESAPEAKE FORUM PREVIEW PARTY, 3:30 to 6 p.m., Academy Art Museum, Easton. Enjoy light hors d'oeuvres and refreshments while getting a first look at what is coming up at the Chesapeake Forum this winter. Event is free but reservations required: chesapeakeforum.org.
SAILING SPEAKERS SERIES, 6 p.m., Miles River Yacht Club. A trio of veteran sailors will follow dinner and offer insights into long-distance sailing preparations, rigors, and rewards, which fascinate both sailors and non-sailors. $30 per person, including dinner. Cash bar. RSVP by Jan. 6 at 410-745-9511, ext. 6.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
MURDER MYSTERY DINNER PARTY, 6 to 9 p.m., Queenstown Harbor, 310 Links Lane, Queenstown. A historically significant performer to share local folklore and historic tales of Queenstown, from the settlement of Lord Baltimore to the involvement of the Audobon Society history. The only problem is that when dinner is served and the entertainment is to begin, the entertainer is no where to be found because he's dead. title: Events around Caroline
author: Connie Connolly
content:
Events around Caroline

 January 8, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly | Section: Calendar 
 
 376
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those looking to have an event included in the weekly Caroline County calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.DENTONMartin Luther King Jr. Day march, Jan. 20, 9 a.m., Lockerman Middle School. March begins at 10 a.m. and concludes at the Caroline County Courthouse where the "I Have a Dream Speech" will be read and bag lunches will be distributed to everyone.
Bingo, 7:30 p.m., Tuesdays, American Legion Post 29, 9238 Legion Road. 5 p.m. doors open, 7:30 p.m. games start. Info:410-479-2708.
Samaritan House Thrift Shop, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Wednesday to Friday; 9 a.m. to noon Saturday. 5th Street behind the post office.
Third Thursdays in Downtown Denton, 5 to 7 p.m., third Thursdays, downtown. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Tuesday & Wednesday, 401 Aldersgate Drive.
Paws for Reading, 3:40 to 4:25 p.m., every fourth Thursday, Central Branch library. Children ages 5 to 12 can proactice reading to a trained service dog. One registrant per session. Register: carolib.libcal.com.
Museum of Rural Life, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., every Saturday, 16 N. Second Street. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
FEDERALSBURGMonday Bingo, 6 p.m. doors open; 7 p.m. bingo begins., Every Monday. Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Cash prizes, food available.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 4 to 6 p.m., Wednesdays, Community Civic League, 3439 Laurel Grove Road.
Federalsburg Floods, Fridays 10 a.m. to noon, Saturdays 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Federalsburg Heritage Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave. Eight significant floods that devastated Federalsburg in the 20th century are highlighted in a new exhibit at the Historical Society's museum.
GOLDSBOROGiving Grace Food Pantry, Goldsboro VFC, 700 Old Line Road. 7 a.m. until; second Saturdays. Info: 302-270-1948.
GREENSBOROFood pantry, 4 to 7 p.m. Thursday, 7 to 9 a.m. Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday. Aaron's Place Pantry at Greensboro Connects, 111 S. Main St., side entrance.
RIDGELYMartin's House & Barn, First Saturdays thrift store open 8 a.m. to noon. Drive-thru pantry and thrift store hours: 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday; 6 to 7:30 p.m. Wednesday.

title: Easton residents, aiming to bridge political divide, bring workshop to Talbot County
author: Konner Metz
content:
Easton residents, aiming to bridge political divide, bring workshop to Talbot County

 January 10, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Konner Metz | Section: Local News 
 
 500
 Words 

 Read News Document

 EASTON — Easton residents Ronnie Halperin and Sharon Harrington have seen political division worsen over time to the point where they have hesitated to openly discuss their viewpoints or place political signs in their yards.That trend, escalated during recent elections, motivated the two residents to bring an event to the Talbot County Free Library this Saturday. It's a workshop by Braver Angels, a volunteer-led nonprofit organization that aims to bridge political division in local communities.
Halperin says the idea to bring Braver Angels to Easton was birthed when she realized the lack of political diversity within her community book club.
"We realized that everyone in the book group was a Democrat," Halperin said. "And we know that our community is only — at most — half Democrat. So we felt kind of bad about that. What did that mean? It spoke to the polarization that exists now."
One of the book club's members discovered the Braver Angels website. Watching an example workshop video, Halperin said the nonprofit's work struck her as "really effective and really meaningful."
After being trained by the Braver Angels group, Halperin and Harrington are organizing Saturday's event, which is free to the public and takes place from 9:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.
The purpose of Saturday's workshop — titled "Depolarizing Within" — is not to change anyone's political beliefs or discuss specific issues. Instead, it's to teach those on both sides of the aisle how to converse with others "in a way that doesn't include rancor and demonizing and dismissiveness," Halperin said.
"I don't want anybody to walk in there thinking this is a group that's going to try to change my mind," Harrington said. "That is not our goal."
Braver Angels is a New York-based organization that was founded after the 2016 presidential election. It defines itself as the "nation's largest cross-partisan, volunteer-led movement to bridge the partisan divide for the good of our democratic republic" on its website.
A professional moderator will be at Saturday's workshop. The two organizers say they've had pre-registrations come in from both liberal- and conservative-leaning residents, though they're hoping for more of the latter to achieve a balanced discussion.
Talbot County has had its share of political divide in recent elections. Prior to 2024's November election, local political committees reported vandalism of yard signs.
The presidential race was a dead heat in Talbot County, with 11,125 residents voting for Republican nominee and President-elect Donald Trump and 11,119 voting for Democratic nominee Kamala Harris.
Harrington believes Saturday's workshop is a step in the right direction to bridging the partisan nature in the region.
"In the past political year, we've been aware that people have been uneasy about expressing their preferences and have kind of gone underground because of animosity or hurt feelings or things of that sort," Harrington said. "And we wanted to bring something to the town where people could find a way to talk about their differences without going the ugly route or without escalating."
To register, visit braverangels.org/event/depolarizingwithin-4/. For more information, contact Ronnie Halperin or Sharon Harrington at halperinandharrington@gmail.com.

content:

 January 15, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Connie Connolly | Section: Calendar 
 
 488
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those looking to have an event included in the weekly Caroline County calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.DENTONArtist of the month exhibit, Friday, Jan. 17, 4 to 6 p.m., The Foundry, 401 Market St. Experience the raw intensity of self-taught artist Andrew Wingate's bold, vivid paintings created during his journey to sobriety. His work reflects transformation and resilience.
Anime matinee, Saturday, Jan. 18, 1 to 3 p.m., Central Library. For teens. Grab some popcorn and Pocky and watch "The Boy and the Beast," an adventurous and heart-warming story full of action, fantasy and fun.
Martin Luther King Jr. Day march, Jan. 20, 9 a.m., Lockerman Middle School. March begins at 10 a.m. and concludes at the Caroline County Courthouse where the "I Have a Dream Speech" will be read and bag lunches will be distributed to everyone.
Bingo, 7:30 p.m., Tuesdays, American Legion Post 29, 9238 Legion Road. 5 p.m. doors open, 7:30 p.m. games start. Info:410-479-2708.
Samaritan House Thrift Shop, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Wednesday to Friday; 9 a.m. to noon Saturday. 5th Street behind the post office.
Third Thursdays in Downtown Denton, 5 to 7 p.m., third Thursdays, downtown. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Tuesday & Wednesday, 401 Aldersgate Drive.
Paws for Reading, 3:40 to 4:25 p.m., every fourth Thursday, Central Branch library. Children ages 5 to 12 can proactice reading to a trained service dog. One registrant per session. Register: carolib.libcal.com.
Storytime, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Wednesday through April 30, Central Branch library. For children ages birth to 5.
Museum of Rural Life, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., every Saturday, 16 N. Second Street. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
FEDERALSBURGMonday Bingo, 6 p.m. doors open; 7 p.m. bingo begins., Every Monday. Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Cash prizes, food available.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 4 to 6 p.m., Wednesdays, Community Civic League, 3439 Laurel Grove Road.
Federalsburg Floods, Fridays 10 a.m. to noon, Saturdays 10 a.m. to 2 p.m., Federalsburg Heritage Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave. Eight significant floods that devastated Federalsburg in the 20th century are highlighted in a new exhibit at the Historical Society's museum.
GOLDSBOROGiving Grace Food Pantry, Goldsboro VFC, 700 Old Line Road. 7 a.m. until; second Saturdays. Info: 302-270-1948.
GREENSBOROFood pantry, 4 to 7 p.m. Thursday, 7 to 9 a.m. Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday. Aaron's Place Pantry at Greensboro Connects, 111 S. Main St., side entrance.
Storytime, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Tuesday through April 29, North County Branch library. For children ages birth to 5.
RIDGELYMartin's House & Barn, First Saturdays thrift store open 8 a.m. to noon. Drive-thru pantry and thrift store hours: 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday; 6 to 7:30 p.m. Wednesday.

title: Tidewater Rotary hosting fundraising events for Talbot Hospice
author: Staff Writer
content:
Tidewater Rotary hosting fundraising events for Talbot Hospice

 January 24, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Entertainment 
 
 195
 Words 

 Read News Document

 The Tidewater Rotary Club is hosting two upcoming events to help raise money for Talbot Hospice, which offers help for individuals and their families who are facing serious health conditions and end-of-life situations.Team Bowling Night
Date: Monday, March 10, 2025
Time: 5:30 PM — 7:30 PM
Location: Easton Bowl (101 Marlboro Ave #39, Easton, MD)
Bowling enthusiasts and casual players alike are invited to join this lively evening of team bowling. Teams of four will enjoy friendly competition, raffle prizes, and fun awards such as "Best Dressed" and "Team Spirit."
Trivia Night
Date: Monday, May 7, 2025
Time: 5:30 PM — 7:30 PM
Location: 4 Dogs Brewing Co. & Pub (219 Marlboro Ave #52B, Easton, MD)
Put your knowledge to the test at Trivia Night, where teams will compete for prizes and bragging rights. This evening of lighthearted rivalry is perfect for friends, colleagues, and trivia lovers looking to support an important community resource.
Sponsorship Opportunities
Local businesses and organizations are encouraged to sponsor one or both events:
$600 per event / $1,000 for both events
Sponsorships include entry for four participants per event, offering an excellent way to engage with the community while supporting Talbot Hospice's essential mission.
For more: www.tidewaterrotary.org/fundraisers / www.talbothospice.org

title: Tides of Grace raises a toast to a new community resource center
author: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com
content:
Tides of Grace raises a toast to a new community resource center

 February 10, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 434
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — As a beacon of hope and a testament to the resilience of the community, Tides of Grace unveiled a ribbon cutting of its grand opening of its Community Resource center Feb. 6.Welcoming a center to celebrate special moments with the community, the new larger building is located at 207 C N. Liberty Street, and at 2,200 square feet, it has plenty of space to take in monthly donations and host community outreach events throughout the year.
More than serving just the low-income, when unexpected needs arise for anyone Tides of Grace volunteers and community support mobilize to make a difference and ensure no one faces hardship alone, Founder Leann Rhodes-Ickes said.
"The truth is we all experience these storms," she said, and tides of kindness, compassion and support can make a difference.
The 100% volunteer nonprofit serves nearly 400 community members in need every month.
Knowing firsthand the experience of hardship, Rhodes-Ickes shared heartfelt testimonies and her own personal journey growing up in a turbulent environment, and uncertainty, including family struggling with addiction.
"Hardships don't break us, they shape us," she said.
Rhodes-Ickes said she eventually grew faith through her struggles and overcame adversity, breaking generational curses to graduate college, get married, publish books and raise children.
The idea for Tides of Grace developed during Covid when clearing her son's unused toys free to those in need ended up sparking an entire community campaign.
Rhodes-Ickes realized there must be many more families in need throughout the area, and set to work connecting others with resources and building a repertoire of support and Tides of Grace was eventually born as a non-profit.
Understanding every family deserves hope and every child deserves warm home filled with love and protection, Tides of Grace seeks to be the no-questions-asked organization "that offers a helping hand to every single person who needs grace during their hard storms," she said.
"Everyone has a story," Rhodes-Ickes said, including the shared passion of the Tides of Grace volunteers and Board of Directors and encouraged everyone to utilize their own life experiences to support others.
More than a building, the new community resource center will allow Tides of Grace to unite the community, respond to crisis faster, serve more people and unite the community, Rhodes-Ickes said.
Tides of Grace is currently accepting formal attire donations for its Pop-up Prom Boutique in April.
Providing a wide selection of new and gently used dresses and suits as well as accessories and shoes, anyone in need of formal attire is welcome for a whole boutique experience.
More information about Tides of Grace, including upcoming events and to schedule the space for use can be found at: tidesofgraceinc.org.

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.CROSSROADS COMMUNITY 40TH ANNIVERSARY GALA, 6 p.m., Packing House, 411 Dorchester Ave., Cambridge. Indulge in a delectable three-course meal crafted by the talented chefs at RAR/Dive Club. Tickets: zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/crossroads-community-40th-anniversary-gala.
BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
COMMUNITY CRAFTING EVENT, noon, Shore Neurocognitive & Behavioral Health, 29466 Pintail STE 9 Drive, Easton. Create your own felted bear. Space is limited. $35 per person. Reserve your spot today by calling 443-746-3698 or by emailing maggieblack@snhealth.net.
CHESAPEAKE FIRE & ICE FESTIVAL, historic downtown Easton. Live ice carvings, music, restaurant specials, fire performances, outdoor ice skating, and the unveiling of the weekend's ice sculptures with a free self-guided tour. Info: discovereaston.com/fireandice.
EASTON WINTER FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to noon, 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 8 to 9 a.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.

BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
CHESAPEAKE FIRE & ICE FESTIVAL, historic downtown Easton. Live ice carvings, music, restaurant specials, fire performances, outdoor ice skating, and the unveiling of the weekend's ice sculptures with a free self-guided tour. Info: discovereaston.com/fireandice.
INTERLUDE CONCERT, Ebenezer Theater, Easton. Two award-winning musicians will be featured: pianist Janice Carissa and violinist Stella Chen. Tickets $50 at chesapeakemusic.org.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.

STORYTIME, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Tuesday through April 29, North County Branch library, Greensboro. For children ages birth to 5.
BILLIONS OF BABY OYSTERS, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Harriet Tubman Museum & Education Center, 424 Race St., Cambridge. Horn Point Laboratory's oyster hatchery has produced billions of baby oysters, both to restore populations in the Bay and for the oyster farming industry. What does it take to raise healthy baby oysters? Hatchery Director Stephanie Alexander will lead attendees on a virtual tour of the famous hatchery.

WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Trappe Pond State Park. Bob Trail. Meet at Nature Center parking area.

Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.

EMPTY BOWLS DINNER, St. Mark's United Methodist Church, Easton. Fundraiser dinner addressing food insecurity. Tickets go on sale Jan. 13. Info: facebook.com/TalbotCountyEmptyBowls. Donations: mscf.org.
EASTON WINTER FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to noon, 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine.

content:
Mid-Shore Calendar

 February 21, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 1571
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
NATIONAL OUTDOORS SHOW, 5 to 9 p.m., 3485 Golden Hill Rd., Church Creek. The Outdoor Show is held in Dorchester County each year with the goal of preserving Dorchester county's heritage by recognizing its resources and spot-lighting the people who carry out unique talents in their way of life. Main objective is to educate both newcomers to the area and visitors about our rich and unique culture. Adults $8, children $4. Info: nationaloutdoorshow.org/.
EMPTY BOWLS DINNER, 4:30 or 6:30 p.m., St. Mark's United Methodist Church, Easton. Guests will choose a bowl and dine from a selection of delicious soups, including vegetarian options, created by chefs from local restaurants with all proceeds benefitting local food pantries.Tickets $30. Info: facebook.com/TalbotCountyEmptyBowls. Donations: mscf.org.
EASTON WINTER FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to noon, 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 8 to 9 a.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
FREDERICK DOUGLASS 207TH BIRTHDAY, 3:45 p.m., Historic Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. To honor Douglass's life and legacy, the Bailey-Grocè Family Foundation will host a 207th birthday celebration featuring musical performances, poetry, and art. Dinner to follow at Waterfowl Building. Tickets $75 performance only and $125 with dinner at avalonfoundation.org/events.
NATIONAL OUTDOORS SHOW, matinee 10:30 a.m., evening 6 p.m., 3485 Golden Hill Rd., Church Creek. The Outdoor Show is held in Dorchester County each year with the goal of preserving Dorchester county's heritage by recognizing its resources and spot-lighting the people who carry out unique talents in their way of life. Main objective is to educate both newcomers to the area and visitors about our rich and unique culture. Adults $8, children $4. Info: nationaloutdoorshow.org/.
NANTICOKE HISTORIC PRESERVATION ALLIANCE ANNIVERSARY, 3 p.m., Robbins Center, Dorchester County Historical Society, 1003 Greenway Drive, Cambridge. Reflecting on what NHPA has done over past 20 years. Soup and appetizers being served.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
STORYTIME, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Tuesday through April 29, North County Branch library, Greensboro. For children ages birth to 5.
WINTER GARDEN LECTURE. 11 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. Talbot County Free Library, 100 W. Dover St., Easton. Talbot County Garden Club hosts Samantha Nestory to explore garden design and management at Stoneleigh, a "modernized" estate property in Villanova, Pennsylvania in "Gardens Alive: Elevating Our Landscapes through Ecology." Free. Info: Camille Massie at camille.massie501@gmail.com or 703-608-0477.
WINTER HIKE, 10:30 a.m., Terrapin Nature Park. Cross Island Trail. Meet at Exit 37 parking area.
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
STORYTIME, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Wednesday through April 30, Central Library, Denton. For children ages birth to 5.
VIRTUOUS VIRUSES, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Dorchester Center for the Arts, 321 High St., Cambridge. Join ocean virus ecologist Joaquín Martínez Martínez for a discussion on the fascinating vital role viruses play in marine life and ocean health. Discover how understanding viral infection is important to find solutions to pressing environmental challenges.
BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
DESIGNER BAG BINGO, 1 p.m., Sts. Peter and Paul High School Hockmeyer Cafeteria, Easton. Benefits post prom. Doors open at noon. Advanced tickets $30 and $35 at the door if space allows. Contact: Lisa Baillif 410-822-2275 or lbaillif@ssppeaston.org.
FREEDOM ROWERS INFO NIGHT, 5:30 p.m., Aspire Room, Easton Family YMCA. Learn about the rowing team for those ages 18 and younger. Swim test afterward. Info: tongchloe92@gmail.com, 410-924-6621.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
SHELLS AND ROCKS, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Talbot Community Center, Wye Oak Room, 10028 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Baby oysters prefer to grow on the shells of other oysters. But because oyster shells are in short supply, scientists are experimenting with other materials to find out what surfaces can support healthy populations. Professor Elizabeth North will take attendees on the science journey to evaluate solutions to increase oysters and their habitat in the Bay.
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 5
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
THURSDAY, MARCH 6
TRADITIONAL RUG HOOKING, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., The Fibre Arts Center, 7 N. Fourth St., Denton. $150/members, $160/non-members. Kit Fee: $55 paid directly to instructor at time of first class. This three-day class (March 6, 13 and 20) in beginning traditional rug hooking will allow students to accomplish making a small piece by learning the technique, choosing colors, dry-dyeing, painting with wool and finishing. To sign up: 443/448-461 or info@fiberartscenter.com.
MONDAY, MARCH 10
TEAM BOWLING NIGHT, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m., Easton Bowl, 101 Marlboro Ave #39, Easton. Bowling enthusiasts and casual players alike are invited to join this lively evening of team bowling. Teams of four will enjoy friendly competition, raffle prizes, and fun awards such as "Best Dressed" and "Team Spirit." Fundraiser for Talbot Hospice.
AARP, noon, Church of the Nazarene, Denton. Caroline County AARP Chapter 915 meets with a covered dish luncheon. Rescheduled Bingo. Guests and new members are welcome. Enjoy free magazines. Info:410-482-6039.
TUESDAY, MARCH 11
WHEN WATERS BLOOM, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Talbot Community Center, Wye Oak Room, 10028 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Every drop of water is teaming with life, including microscopic algae. Most are beneficial and provide the food on which all aquatic life depends. However, some are harmful, even toxic, not only for fish but people. These harmful events are increasing around the world. Phytoplankton ecologist, Professor Pat Glibert will lead attendees through the latest research on harmful algal blooms.

The annual meeting provides members and the community an opportunity to get updates on activities related to the Dorchester County Business Community. The 2025 Board of Directors will be introduced. Mid-Shore Calendar

 February 28, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2951
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Those seeking to have an event published in the Star Democrat's calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
WOODSHED BLUES BAND, 7 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. The Woodshed Blues Band consists of some of the Mid-Shore's finest musicians. Info: facebook.com/profile.php?id=61566026330834.
BOOK SALE, 10 a.m. t o 5 p.m., St. Luke's Chapel, 7208 Main Street, Queenstown. Books Café: 20,000 books, 90% off; lunch, baked goods, snacks. Info: 410-827-8484.
CARS AND COFFEE, 8:30 to 10:30 a.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. Free. Exotics, classics, muscle cars, imports all welcome. Sponsored by Prestige Auto Vault, Eat Sprout & Doc's Sunset Grille.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
EASTON WINTER FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to noon, 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine.
'BLEEKER STREET' (A TRIBUTE), 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Newmyer Flyer captures the essence of Simon & Garfunkel, the most successful music duo of all time, and for many "the sound of the 1960s." INFO: youtube.com/watch?v=rl55sO00OZU.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Waterfowl, forest birds, sparrows. Meet at Pickering Creek Audubon Center parking area at 8 a.m. (GPS 38.86 N, 76.124 W). Leaders: Linda and Peter Yungbluth (410-924-8135 or lyungbluth@gmail.com).
DESIGNER BAG BINGO, 1 p.m., Sts. Peter and Paul High School Hockmeyer Cafeteria, Easton. Benefits post prom. Doors open at noon. Advanced tickets $30 and $35 at the door if space allows. Contact: Lisa Baillif 410-822-2275 or lbaillif@ssppeaston.org.
FREEDOM ROWERS INFO NIGHT, 5:30 p.m., Aspire Room, Easton Family YMCA. Learn about the rowing team for those ages 18 and younger. Swim test afterward. Info: tongchloe92@gmail.com, 410-924-6621.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
SHELLS AND ROCKS, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Talbot Community Center, Wye Oak Room, 10028 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Baby oysters prefer to grow on the shells of other oysters. But because oyster shells are in short supply, scientists are experimenting with other materials to find out what surfaces can support healthy populations. Professor Elizabeth North will take attendees on the science journey to evaluate solutions to increase oysters and their habitat in the Bay.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
STORYTIME, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Tuesday through April 29, North County Branch library, Greensboro. For children ages birth to 5.
STRONG AND STEADY, 10 a.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. Workout class for adults seeking to improve muscle strength with Janet Pfeffer. $10 per class. $80 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Help with E-bird monitoring. Bring binoculars. Meet at Pickering Creek Audubon Center parking area at 8 a.m. (GPS 38.86 N, 76.124 W). Leader: Cristina Niciporciukas (973-216-5216 or cnicipo71@outlook.com).
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
THE STEEL WHEELS, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Tickets: $30. Virginia-based folk-rock band The Steel Wheels have spent almost 20 years writing, recording, and touring, all the while constantly honing their evolving brand of American roots music. Info: thesteelwheels.com.
KNITTING NEEDLEPOINT AND CROCHET, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., The Fiber Arts Center, 7 N. Fourth St., Denton. $5 for members, $10 for non-members. Bring your projects that are in the works or new starts and learn from our fabulous instructors, Alice Engle and Victoria McConnell, how to get through and correct mistakes, confusing techniques, trying new stitches, cast-ons and bind-offs. Sign up: 443-448-4611.
TRADITIONAL RUG HOOKING, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., The Fibre Arts Center, 7 N. Fourth St., Denton. $150/members, $160/non-members. Kit Fee: $55 paid directly to instructor at time of first class. This three-day class (March 6, 13 and 20) in beginning traditional rug hooking will allow students to accomplish making a small piece by learning the technique, choosing colors, dry-dyeing, painting with wool and finishing. To sign up: 443/448-461 or info@fiberartscenter.com.
STRONG AND STEADY, 10 a.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. Workout class for adults seeking to improve muscle strength with Janet Pfeffer. $10 per class. $80 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
FRIDAY NIGHT DINNER, 5 to 7:30 p.m., VFW Post 5118, 355 Glebe Road, Easton. Community invited. Held every Friday.
POST MARDI GRAS LOUISIANA MUSIC NIGHT, 7 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Philip Dutton & the Alligators serve up a zesty musical Jambalaya that brings Louisiana's Bayou right here to Maryland's Easton Shore. Info: facebook.com/philipduttonandthealligators/.
SATURDAY, MARCH 8
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
EASTON WINTER FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to noon, 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine.
SWAMP DONKEY, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Stretching the "grass" concept to the limit and offering a unique sound in the process, the Annapolis/Baltimore-based electric newgrass band Swamp Donkey delivers an exciting combination of original songs and unique covers that span many genres in a style they have made all their own. Info: swampdonkeymusic.com.
MONDAY, MARCH 10
TEAM BOWLING NIGHT, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m., Easton Bowl, 101 Marlboro Ave #39, Easton. Bowling enthusiasts and casual players alike are invited to join this lively evening of team bowling. Teams of four will enjoy friendly competition, raffle prizes, and fun awards such as "Best Dressed" and "Team Spirit." Fundraiser for Talbot Hospice.
AARP, noon, Church of the Nazarene, Denton. Caroline County AARP Chapter 915 meets with a covered dish luncheon. Rescheduled Bingo. Guests and new members are welcome. Enjoy free magazines. Info:410-482-6039.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
TUESDAY, MARCH 11
WHEN WATERS BLOOM, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Talbot Community Center, Wye Oak Room, 10028 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Every drop of water is teaming with life, including microscopic algae. Most are beneficial and provide the food on which all aquatic life depends. However, some are harmful, even toxic, not only for fish but people. These harmful events are increasing around the world. Phytoplankton ecologist, Professor Pat Glibert will lead attendees through the latest research on harmful algal blooms.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.
YARN AND NEEDLE GROUP, 12:30 to 3 p.m., Brookletts Place Talbot County Senior Center, Easton. Every Tuesday. Some help may be available for knitting and crocheting. Open to anyone 60 years of age or older at no cost. Info: 410-822-2869.
STORYTIME, 10:30 to 11 a.m. every Tuesday through April 29, North County Branch library, Greensboro. For children ages birth to 5.
STRONG AND STEADY, 10 a.m., Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. Workout class for adults seeking to improve muscle strength with Janet Pfeffer. $10 per class. $80 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
MID-SHORE COMMUNITY BAND CONCERT, 7 p.m., North Caroline High School, 10990 River Rd., Ridgely. Free concert of Irish music for St. Patrick's Day. Donations accepted.
WEDNESDAY, MARCH 12
WEDNESDAY MORNING ARTISTS, weekly at 9:30 a.m., 900 Peachblossom Place, Cambridge. All are welcome, from beginners to pros. There is always opportunity and something interesting to learn and see. Group shares our artwork at meetings and collaborates with many different forms of media. Artists' work displayed in the window of Vintage Venue on Race Street in Cambridge. Facebook: wednesdaymorningartists. Email is: wednesdaymorningartists@gmail.com.
KNITTING NEEDLEPOINT AND CROCHET, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., The Fiber Arts Center, 7 N. Fourth St., Denton. $5 for members, $10 for non-members. Bring your projects that are in the works or new starts and learn from our fabulous instructors, Alice Engle and Victoria McConnell, how to get through and correct mistakes, confusing techniques, trying new stitches, cast-ons and bind-offs. Sign up: 443-448-4611.
THURSDAY, MARCH 13

TALBOT BIRD CLUB, Pickering Creek Audubon Center. Waterfowl, forest birds, sparrows. Meet at Pickering Creek Audubon Center parking area at 8 a.m. (GPS 38.86 N, 76.124 W). Leaders: Linda and Peter Yungbluth (410-924-8135 or lyungbluth@gmail.com).
DESIGNER BAG BINGO, 1 p.m., Sts. Peter and Paul High School Hockmeyer Cafeteria, Easton. Benefits post prom. Doors open at noon. Advanced tickets $30 and $35 at the door if space allows. Contact: Lisa Baillif 410-822-2275 or lbaillif@ssppeaston.org.
FREEDOM ROWERS INFO NIGHT, 5:30 p.m., Aspire Room, Easton Family YMCA. Learn about the rowing team for those ages 18 and younger. Swim test afterward. Info: tongchloe92@gmail.com, 410-924-6621.
YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.

Professor Elizabeth North will take attendees on the science journey to evaluate solutions to increase oysters and their habitat in the Bay.

Phytoplankton ecologist, Professor Pat Glibert will lead attendees through the latest research on harmful algal blooms.

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Calendar 
 
 2272
 Words 

 Read News Document

POST MARDI GRAS LOUISIANA MUSIC NIGHT, 7 p.m., Stoltz Listening Room 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Philip Dutton & the Alligators serve up a zesty musical Jambalaya that brings Louisiana's Bayou right here to Maryland's Easton Shore. Info: facebook.com/philipduttonandthealligators/.
STEAK DINNER, 5 to 7 p.m., American Legion Post 296, 6200 Main St., Queenstown. 410-827-8182.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Rd., Oxford. 9:30 a.m. Intermediate yoga with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
EASTON WINTER FARMERS MARKET, 8 a.m. to noon, 100 Block North Washington Street, Easton. Open rain or shine.
SWAMP DONKEY, 7 p.m., Avalon Theatre, 40 E. Dover St., Easton. Stretching the "grass" concept to the limit and offering a unique sound in the process, the Annapolis/Baltimore-based electric newgrass band Swamp Donkey delivers an exciting combination of original songs and unique covers that span many genres in a style they have made all their own. Info: swampdonkeymusic.com.
TILGHMAN ISLAND HELATH FAIR, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., Tilghman Island Volunteer Fire Department. Sponsored by Talbot County Health Department. Health services provided include Hep C and HIV testing, blood pressure screening, diabetes blood glucose check, colon cancer screening, vision screening, hearing screening, family planning and STI screening, Narcan training and more. Free $25 Aldi gift card, swag bag and lunch to all who attend.
TEAM BOWLING NIGHT, 5:30 to 7:30 p.m., Easton Bowl, 101 Marlboro Ave #39, Easton. Bowling enthusiasts and casual players alike are invited to join this lively evening of team bowling. Teams of four will enjoy friendly competition, raffle prizes, and fun awards such as "Best Dressed" and "Team Spirit." Fundraiser for Talbot Hospice.

YOGA CLASS, Oxford Community Center, 200 Oxford Road. 1 p.m. Yoga for advanced beginners with Suzie Hurley. $20 per class. $150 for 10 classes. Info: 410-226-5904 or oxfordcc.org.
WHEN WATERS BLOOM, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m., Talbot Community Center, Wye Oak Room, 10028 Ocean Gateway, Easton. Every drop of water is teaming with life, including microscopic algae. Most are beneficial and provide the food on which all aquatic life depends. However, some are harmful, even toxic, not only for fish but people. These harmful events are increasing around the world. Phytoplankton ecologist, Professor Pat Glibert will lead attendees through the latest research on harmful algal blooms.
YOGA WITH PATTY, 5 to 6 p.m., Dorchester Chamber of Commerce, second floor conference room, 306 High St., Cambridge. Designed for all skill levels, this class offers a harmonious blend of postures and breathing techniques to rejuvenate both mind and body. Call/text 410-463-8393 for reservations.

title: QACHS to host National Vietnam War Veterans Day commemoration
author: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com
content:
QACHS to host National Vietnam War Veterans Day commemoration

 March 16, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: ANDREA GRABENSTEIN agrabenstein@chespub.com | Section: News 
 
 180
 Words 

 Read News Document

 CENTREVILLE — Queen Anne's County High School will honor the legacy of Vietnam veterans with a distinguished Veterans Day ceremony at the QACHS auditorium March 29 at 2 p.m.Veterans, their families, and the public are invited to attend the distinguished ceremony to honor all who served during the Vietnam Era during the 50th anniversary of the official end of the Vietnam War.
A day of fellowship to honor and remember the valiant service of all Vietnam War veterans, all are welcome to ensure their legacy is preserved for future generations. All Vietnam Era service members who served on active duty anywhere in the world are invited for a pinning ceremony.
The keynote speech will be led by Jack Farley, retired judge with the United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims and wounded Vietnam veteran.
A proclamation will be presented by the Queen Anne County's Board of Commissioners with participation from Boy Scout Troop 278 and the U.S. Naval Sea Cadet Corps.
More information about the National Vietnam War Veterans Day ceremony can be found by contacting event coordinator Dave Peterson at sdpeterson71@gmail.com

title: Events planned to mark 50th anniversary of end of Vietnam War
author: STAFF REPORT
content:
Events planned to mark 50th anniversary of end of Vietnam War

 March 28, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: STAFF REPORT | Section: Local News 
 
 338
 Words 

 Read News Document

 Saturday, March 29, is National Vietnam War Veterans Day, a national day of observance for those who served during the 20-year conflict. This year marks the 50th anniversary of the war's end.Several Mid-Shore organizations will host events this weekend to commemorate the occasion and recognize those who served.
Easton parade, ceremony
On March 30, Veterans of Foreign Wars Post 5118 plans to hold a wreath laying ceremony before a parade through downtown Easton and a short program in honor of Vietnam veterans.
The event begins at 1 p.m. Sunday.
The parade route, which has already been approved by the Town of Easton, will begin at the intersection of Dover and Washington streets, then make its way down Washington Street and Glebe Road to the VFW. Event organizers plan to distribute American flags for spectators to wave.
Those who wish to be involved in the event can contact 410-310-5748.
QACHS commemoration
Queen Anne's County High School will honor the legacy of Vietnam veterans with a distinguished Veterans Day ceremony at the QACHS auditorium Saturday, March 29, at 2 p.m.
Veterans, their families, and the public are invited to attend the distinguished ceremony to honor all who served during the Vietnam Era during the 50th anniversary of the official end of the Vietnam War.
The keynote speech will be led by Jack Farley, retired judge with the United States Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims and wounded Vietnam veteran.
A proclamation will be presented by the Queen Anne County's Board of Commissioners with participation from Boy Scout Troop 278 and the U.S. Naval Sea Cadet Corps.
For more information, contact sdpeterson71@gmail.com.
Caroline County observation
On Saturday, March 29, at 1 p.m., Caroline American Legion Post 29 invites all legion members and Caroline County residents who served anywhere in the world between Nov. 1, 1955, and May 15, 1975, to a special recognition event as part of the National Vietnam War Commemoration.
The event will take place at the post.
Widows of servicemen during this period will also be acknowledged and recognized for their strength and resilience. Light refreshments will be served.
Call 410-200-5640 to RSVP.

title: Pastoral Ponderings: National Day of Prayer
author: PAUL TWINING
content:
Pastoral Ponderings: National Day of Prayer

 April 29, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: PAUL TWINING | Section: Columns 
 
 206
 Words 

 Read News Document

 On May 1, our nation will be commemorating the 73rd annual National Day of Prayer.This year's theme resonates with an answer to a desperate cry that sounds forth from every sector of American life: "May the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, so that by the power of the Holy Spirit, you may abound in hope." (Romans, 15:13)
Hope coming to us from an infinite divine source is absolutely necessary; otherwise, it is nothing more than wishful thinking. However, the hope extended to us from the heart and hand of Almighty God is a gift that fully meets our need. The only condition stipulated is that we believe. No politician, military force, medical professional or human companion has what it takes to deliver this gift; only one loving, omnipotent, omniscient Creator can.
Please join us on May 1 in Denton on the courthouse greens from noon to 1 p.m. to pray. We will be one of over 35,000 groups meeting throughout America to intercede before God for his blessing on our nation by turning our hearts from our sinful ways to Him. Many of our Caroline County leaders will be participating, and a free lunch will be provided following the event.

 386
 Words

 Those looking to have an event included in the weekly Caroline County calendar are asked to email details to community@stardem.com.DENTON
Bingo, 7:30 p.m., Tuesdays, American Legion Post 29, 9238 Legion Road. 5 p.m. doors open, 7:30 p.m. games start. Info:410-479-2708.
Samaritan House Thrift Shop, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Wednesday to Friday; 9 a.m. to noon Saturday. 5th Street behind the post office.
Third Thursdays in Downtown Denton, 5 to 7 p.m., third Thursdays, downtown. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Tuesday & Wednesday, 401 Aldersgate Drive.
Paws for Reading, 3:40 to 4:25 p.m., every fourth Thursday, Central Branch library. Children ages 5 to 12 can proactice reading to a trained service dog. One registrant per session. Register: carolib.libcal.com.
Museum of Rural Life, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., every Saturday, 16 N. Second Street. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
FEDERALSBURG
Remembering Cantner's Drug Store, May 10, 1 p.m., Federalsburg Historical Society Museum, 100 Covey Williams Ave. Guest speakers, informational display, light refreshments.
Monday Bingo, 6 p.m. doors open; 7 p.m. bingo begins., Every Monday. Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Cash prizes, food available.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 4 to 6 p.m., Wednesdays, Community Civic League, 3439 Laurel Grove Road.
GOLDSBORO
Giving Grace Food Pantry, Goldsboro VFC, 700 Old Line Road. 7 a.m. until; second Saturdays. Info: 302-270-1948.
GREENSBORO
Our Buried History, Saturday, May 10, 6 to 8 p.m., 104 E. Sunset Ave. Experience the hidden world beneath our feet. Steveo Butler from Choptank Treasure Hunters reveals the wonderful relics he has unearthed through metal detecting. Light refreshments provided.
Food pantry, 4 to 7 p.m. Thursday, 7 to 9 a.m. Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday. Aaron's Place Pantry at Greensboro Connects, 111 S. Main St., side entrance.
RIDGELY
Martin's House & Barn, First Saturdays thrift store open 8 a.m. to noon. Drive-thru pantry and thrift store hours: 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday; 6 to 7:30 p.m. Wednesday.
COUNTYWIDE
Sweet Caroline Home Tour, Saturday, May 17, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. Tour five historic Caroline County properties. Hosted by the Caroline County Historical Society. Tickets $40 at carolinehistory.org/ or $45 day of.

Info: 410-482-6039.
Bingo, 7:30 p.m., Tuesdays, American Legion Post 29, 9238 Legion Road. 5 p.m. doors open, 7:30 p.m. games start. Info:410-479-2708.
Samaritan House Thrift Shop, 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. Wednesday to Friday; 9 a.m. to noon Saturday. 5th Street behind the post office.
Third Thursdays in Downtown Denton, 5 to 7 p.m., third Thursdays, downtown. Businesses extend their hours and offer specials. Info: DowntownDenton.com.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., Tuesday & Wednesday, 401 Aldersgate Drive.
Paws for Reading, 3:40 to 4:25 p.m., every fourth Thursday, Central Branch library. Children ages 5 to 12 can proactice reading to a trained service dog. One registrant per session. Register: carolib.libcal.com.
Museum of Rural Life, 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., every Saturday, 16 N. Second Street. World War I and II, a sharecropper's cabin, new Buffalo Soldier exhibit, among many other artifacts and stories about Caroline County. A docent is on hand for tours. Free to the public. Info: carolinehistory.org or 410-479-2055 and leave a message.
FEDERALSBURGMonday Bingo, 6 p.m. doors open; 7 p.m. bingo begins., Every Monday. Federalsburg VFW Post 5246, 2630 Veterans Drive. Cash prizes, food available.
Aaron's Place Food Pantry, 4 to 6 p.m., Wednesdays, Community Civic League, 3439 Laurel Grove Road.
GOLDSBOROGiving Grace Food Pantry, Goldsboro VFC, 700 Old Line Road. 7 a.m. until; second Saturdays. Info: 302-270-1948.
GREENSBOROOur Buried History, Saturday, May 10, 6 to 8 p.m., 104 E. Sunset Ave. Experience the hidden world beneath our feet. Steveo Butler from Choptank Treasure Hunters reveals the wonderful relics he has unearthed through metal detecting. Light refreshments provided.
Food pantry, 4 to 7 p.m. Thursday, 7 to 9 a.m. Saturday, 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Monday. Aaron's Place Pantry at Greensboro Connects, 111 S. Main St., side entrance.
RIDGELYMartin's House & Barn, First Saturdays thrift store open 8 a.m. to noon. Drive-thru pantry and thrift store hours: 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. Tuesday, Thursday and Friday; 6 to 7:30 p.m. Wednesday.
Strawberry Festival, Sunday, May 25, Martin Sutton Park. Music, food vendors, family fun, parade at noon. Fundraiser for Lion's Club.

title: Mid-Shore Memorial Day ceremonies and events
author: STAFF REPORT
content:
Mid-Shore Memorial Day ceremonies and events

 May 23, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: STAFF REPORT | Section: News 
 
 464
 Words 

 Read News Document

 In the coming days, Mid-Shore communities and organizations will hold several ceremonies and events in observation of Memorial Day.Denton Memorial Day parade
A parade honoring those who dies in service will take place on Friday, May 23, in downtown Denton.
The parade will make its way down Market Street starting at 6 p.m.
The event is sponsored by American Legion Post 29.
Classic Motor Museum Memorial Day Parade
On Saturday, May 24, from 10:30 to 11:30 a.m., a parade featuring over 50 exhibits will make its way down Talbot Street in St. Michaels.
The parade will include military and veteran groups, classic cars and community groups. Spectators are encouraged to wear patriotic outfits.
An event will be held at the Classic Car Museum on E. Marengo Street following the parade.
Eastern Shore Veterans Cemetery flag placement
Community members are invited to help place flags on 7,000 veteran graves at the cemetery, located at 6827 E. New Market Ellwood Rd. in Hurlock.
Volunteers are encouraged to wear gloves to prevent blisters.
The event begins at 8 a.m. on Saturday, May 24.
Chestertown Memorial Day programming
hestertown celebrates Memorial Day with a parade and remembrance on May 26.
The Memorial Day Committee is inviting community members to participate in the parade by creating floats or showcasing vehicles of interest. Walking groups with patriotic themes are also welcome. No pre-registration is required. Participants will gather at 9 a.m. at Dixon Drive. The parade will start at 10 a.m. and proceed down High Street to Memorial Park.
In advance of the parade, from 9 to 10 a.m., entertainment will be provided by Chester River Voices and the Ukulele Club. Chestertown River Arts will be on hand to distribute "thank you cards" to be sent to veterans. The community arts organization will also sell tissue paper poppies.
Following the parade, keynote speaker Aubrey Sarvis, an Army veteran, will give a short presentation on the Korean War, which claimed the lives of more than 50,000 Americans.
Dorchester American Legion ceremony
The Dorchester American Legion Post 91 will hold its annual Memorial Day Service Monday, May 26, from 11 a.m. to noon at Long Wharf Park in Cambridge.
The flag will be raised and cannon will go off to begin the Service at 11 a.m.
The park will be closed to vehicle traffic at 10 a.m.
Chairs will be limited. Attendees are encourages to consider bringing their own.
At the conclusion of the event, the American Legion will host the community for finger foods and light refreshments.
Eastern Shore Veterans Cemetery Memorial Day service
A ceremony will be held at 1:30 p.m. on Friday, May 30, at the cemetery, located at 6827 E. New Market Ellwood Rd. in Hurlock.
The event will last between 15 and 20 minutes and will feature a keynote speaker and a performance by the Easton Middle School band.
Following the ceremony, a meal will be provided at the Hurlock American Legion.

title: Mission rooted in values
author: Staff Writer
content:
Mission rooted in values

 May 31, 2025 | Star Democrat, The (Easton, MD)

 Author/Byline: Staff Writer | Section: Editors Inbox 
 
 200
 Words 

 Read News Document

 I want to thank The Star Democrat for highlighting our recent rebrand to Fello. While the name is new, our mission remains deeply rooted in the values that have guided us for 64 years.Fello embodies fellowship and partnership. It means being a neighbor who contributes to building community by creating spaces of trust and connection. It means being a citizen who embraces responsibility and collaboration. It means being an ally who stands beside people with disabilities with purpose and resolve, championing equity and respect.
Together, these elements embody belonging, shared purpose, and the strength found in unity. Our new name reflects this belief in the power of connection, individuality and collective strength—because when we stand together with purpose and resolve, nothing is impossible.
While our name has changed, our mission remains the same: to walk beside people with disabilities every step of the way, providing personalized support, advocating for inclusion, and building communities of belonging across Maryland.
Fello honors our history while opening doors to new opportunities. Here, we build trust, foster respect and create community — together.
We are grateful for the ongoing support of our communities as we continue this important work under a new name, with the same heart.
JONATHON RONDEAU
Linthicum
